items.title: zmerge example
items.text:
This site merges the documentation of two projects with zmerge. Both are built from their GitHub repositories and share one navigation and one search.

  • lev: a fast Python library for the Levenshtein distance.
  • datamodel-code-generator: generates Python data models from OpenAPI, JSON Schema and more.

items.title: datamodel-code-generator
items.text:
🚀 Generate Python data models from schema definitions in seconds.

Getting Started Open Playground Lead maintainer available for work

items.title: ✨ What it does
items.text:
Pick any one of the supported inputs and pick the Python model style you want as output. --input-model path/to/file.py:ClassName can even retarget an existing Pydantic, dataclass, or TypedDict class defined in another Python file to a different output type.

  • 📄 Converts OpenAPI 3, AsyncAPI, JSON Schema, Apache Avro, XML Schema, Protocol Buffers/gRPC, GraphQL, MCP tool schemas, and raw data (JSON/YAML/CSV) into Python models
  • 🐍 Generates from existing Python types (Pydantic, dataclass, TypedDict) via --input-model
  • 🎯 Generates Pydantic v2, Pydantic v2 dataclass, dataclasses, TypedDict, or msgspec output
  • 🔗 Handles complex schemas: $ref, allOf, oneOf, anyOf, enums, and nested types
  • ✅ Produces type-safe, validated code ready for your IDE and type checker

items.title: 🧪 Try It In Your Browser
items.text:
Generate models in your browser without installing anything.

Playground privacy

Generation runs locally in your browser with Pyodide. Your schema and options are not sent to a backend. Shared repro URLs encode them in the URL fragment (#state=...), which browsers do not send to the server; the full URL can still be stored in your browser history or wherever you share it.

items.title: 🚀 Start Here
items.text:
Install the CLI and generate your first model from Getting Started. Then add --recommend-options to that command to get options suited to your schema (experimental).

Default output model

When --output-model-type is omitted, datamodel-code-generator generates Pydantic v2 BaseModel output (pydantic_v2.BaseModel). Use --output-model-type explicitly when you want dataclasses, TypedDict, or msgspec output.

items.title: 📥 Choose Your Input
items.text: Input Type File Types Example 📘 OpenAPI 3.0/3.1/3.2 .yaml, .json API specifications 📡 AsyncAPI .yaml, .json Event-driven API specifications 📋 JSON Schema .json, .yaml Data validation schemas 🪶 Apache Avro .avsc, .json Avro schemas 🧾 XML Schema .xsd XML document schemas 🧩 Protocol Buffers / gRPC .proto Protobuf messages and service schemas 🔷 GraphQL .graphql GraphQL type definitions 🛠️ MCP Tool Schemas .json, .yaml MCP tool input/output schemas 📊 JSON/YAML/CSV Data .json, .yaml, .csv Infer schema from data 🐍 Python Models .py Pydantic, dataclass, TypedDict

items.title: ✅ Conformance Signals
items.text: CI exercises datamodel-code-generator against pinned external corpora for XML Schema, JSON Schema, AsyncAPI, Apache Avro, and Protocol Buffers. See the Conformance Dashboard for the generated summary of runner scripts, tox environments, CI jobs, expected corpus counts, and upstream sources.

items.title: 📤 Choose Your Output
items.text:
# 🆕 Pydantic v2 (recommended for new projects)
datamodel-codegen --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel ...

# 🏗️ Python dataclasses
datamodel-codegen --output-model-type dataclasses.dataclass ...

# 📝 TypedDict (for type hints without validation)
datamodel-codegen --output-model-type typing.TypedDict ...

# ⚡ msgspec (high-performance serialization)
datamodel-codegen --output-model-type msgspec.Struct ...

See Supported Data Types for the full list.

items.title: 🌐 Generate a FastAPI server or an HTTP client (experimental)
items.text:
Experimental

Server and client generation are experimental since 0.84.0: their options and generated packages may change. See Experimental Features.

From one OpenAPI document, --generate-server fastapi writes a FastAPI server package and --generate-client httpx2 an HTTPX2 client package, in the same run as the models. The models stay the runtime contract: routes and client methods take and return the generated models, so the server and the client parse and produce the same classes you already use. Every generated file is regenerated on each run; keep your own code outside the generated packages. The commands put everything in one application package, app: the generated app/models.py, app/server/, and app/client/, and your app/services/, so no generic top-level name such as models or server is taken.

This example is the FastAPI server tutorial, and the tests of this project run it as shown.

Input (openapi.yaml) 
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Pets
  version: "1.0"
servers:
  - url: http://localhost:8000
paths:
  /pets:
    get:
      operationId: listPets
      tags: [pets]
      parameters:
        - name: limit
          in: query
          schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 100, default: 20}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The pets.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Pets"}
    post:
      operationId: createPet
      tags: [pets]
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/NewPet"}
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Created.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Pet"}
  /pets/{petId}:
    get:
      operationId: getPet
      tags: [pets]
      parameters:
        - name: petId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema: {type: integer}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The pet.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Pet"}
        "404":
          description: No pet has this ID.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Error"}
components:
  schemas:
    NewPet:
      type: object
      required: [name]
      properties:
        name: {type: string}
        tag: {type: string}
    Pet:
      type: object
      required: [id, name]
      properties:
        id: {type: integer}
        name: {type: string}
        tag: {type: string}
    Pets:
      type: array
      items: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Pet"}
    Error:
      type: object
      required: [message]
      properties:
        message: {type: string}

Commands

# The application package app, which the generated packages go into
mkdir -p app && touch app/__init__.py

# FastAPI server package in app/server/
datamodel-codegen \
  --input openapi.yaml \
  --input-file-type openapi \
  --openapi-scopes schemas api \
  --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel \
  --preset standard-py312-20261019 \
  --output app/models.py \
  --generate-server fastapi \
  --server-output app/server \
  --server-package app.server \
  --server-model-package app.models

# HTTPX2 client package in app/client/
datamodel-codegen \
  --input openapi.yaml \
  --input-file-type openapi \
  --openapi-scopes schemas api \
  --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel \
  --preset standard-py312-20261019 \
  --output app/models.py \
  --generate-client httpx2 \
  --client-output app/client \
  --client-package app.client \
  --client-model-package app.models

--openapi-scopes must include api, and both need Python 3.11 or later, to run and as the target version (the preset sets 3.12); left unset, the run sets them and says how. Each run ends by printing the runtime dependencies of its package to stderr:

Add the runtime dependencies of app.server to your project:
  uv add "fastapi>=0.141.1" "pydantic>=2.14.0" "typing-extensions>=4.16"
Next steps: implement the stubs in app/services/pets.py, then run the server:
  uv add uvicorn && uv run uvicorn app.server.main:app --reload
or: uv add "fastapi[standard]" && uv run fastapi dev --entrypoint app.server.main:app
See app/server/README.md.
Add the runtime dependencies of app.client to your project:
  uv add "httpx2>=2.13.0" "typing-extensions>=4.16" "pydantic>=2.14.0"
Next steps: call the API with the client:
  from app.client import Client

  with Client(base_url=...) as client:
      client.pets.list_pets(...)
See app/client/README.md.

Generated files (trimmed)

app/
├── __init__.py
├── models.py
├── server/
├── services/
└── client/

Implement the server in app/services/pets.py, which generation wrote once with stubs, by replacing the stubs of the Pets class that subclasses the generated service Protocol; type checkers report a missing method or a mismatched signature:

from app import models
from app.server import HTTPResult
from app.server.services import PetsService


class Pets(PetsService):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.pets: dict[int, models.Pet] = {}

    def list_pets(self, *, limit: int) -> models.Pets:
        return models.Pets(list(self.pets.values())[:limit])

    def create_pet(self, *, body: models.NewPet) -> models.Pet:
        pet = models.Pet(id=len(self.pets) + 1, name=body.name, tag=body.tag)
        self.pets[pet.id] = pet
        return pet

    def get_pet(self, *, pet_id: int) -> models.Pet | HTTPResult[models.Error]:
        if (pet := self.pets.get(pet_id)) is None:
            return HTTPResult(404, models.Error(message=f"Pet {pet_id} not found"))
        return pet

uv add uvicorn
uv run uvicorn app.server.main:app

Call it with the client in call.py, which sends to the document's server URL by default:

from app.client import Client
from app.client.errors import NotFoundError
from app.models import NewPet

with Client() as client:
    pet = client.pets.create_pet(body=NewPet(name="Mimi", tag="cat"))
    print(pet)
    for listed in client.pets.list_pets(limit=10).root:
        print(listed.name)
    try:
        client.pets.get_pet(pet_id=99)
    except NotFoundError as error:
        print(error.status_code, error.body)

It prints:

id=1 name='Mimi' tag='cat'
Mimi
404 message='Pet 99 not found'

AsyncClient offers the same methods as coroutines. See FastAPI Server Generation and Python Client Generation for every option, the pyproject.toml settings, authentication, and the Python API.

items.title: CLI option quick starts
items.text:
Use these starting points when combining options; each option links to the generated CLI reference for details and examples.

  • Generate a local schema file: Pin the input type and destination when the source extension is ambiguous or generated output needs a stable path. Options: --input, --input-file-type, --output.
  • Target Pydantic v2 on modern Python: Set the output model family and Python/Pydantic compatibility targets together. Options: --output-model-type, --target-python-version, --target-pydantic-version.
  • Use modern Python annotations: Target a recent Python version and prefer built-in collection and union syntax in generated types. Options: --target-python-version, --use-union-operator, --use-standard-collections.
  • Normalize incoming field names: Convert source names to Python identifiers while preserving explicit alias data for runtime IO. Options: --snake-case-field, --original-field-name-delimiter, --aliases.
  • Generate operation-focused models: Limit OpenAPI output to operation shapes and name models from operation IDs and status codes. Options: --openapi-scopes, --use-operation-id-as-name, --use-status-code-in-response-name.
  • Resolve remote references deliberately: Enable remote $ref loading and configure request metadata, timeouts, or local ref roots. Options: --allow-remote-refs, --http-headers, --http-timeout, --http-local-ref-path.

See the CLI Reference for the full option list and category-specific recipes.

items.title: 🤖 Get CLI Help from LLMs
items.text:
Generate a prompt to ask LLMs about CLI options:

datamodel-codegen --generate-prompt "Best options for Pydantic v2?" | claude -p

See LLM Integration for more examples.

items.title: 🌐 Generate from URL
items.text:
pip install 'datamodel-code-generator[http]'
datamodel-codegen --url https://example.com/api/openapi.yaml --output model.py

The http extra is the stable, non-deprecated backend. For the experimental HTTPX2 alternative, pass --http-backend httpx2; see HTTP backend selection.

items.title: ⚙️ Use with pyproject.toml
items.text:
pyproject.toml
[tool.datamodel-codegen]
input = "schema.yaml"
output = "src/models.py"
output-model-type = "pydantic_v2.BaseModel"

Then simply run:

datamodel-codegen

See pyproject.toml Configuration for more options.

items.text:

items.title: 🏷️ Field Aliases
items.text: The --aliases option allows you to rename fields in the generated models. This is useful when you want to use different Python field names than those defined in the schema while preserving the original names as serialization aliases.

items.title: 🚀 Basic Usage
items.text:
datamodel-codegen \
    --input schema.json \
    --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel \
    --output model.py \
    --aliases aliases.json

You can also pass the same mapping inline:

datamodel-codegen \
    --input schema.json \
    --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel \
    --output model.py \
    --aliases '{"id": "id_", "type": "type_"}'

items.title: 📋 Alias Format
items.text: The alias JSON maps original field names to their Python aliases. Pass it either inline or as a JSON file path.

items.title: 📝 Flat Format (Traditional)
items.text:
The simplest format applies aliases to all fields with the matching name, regardless of which class they belong to:

{
  "id": "id_",
  "type": "type_",
  "class": "class_"
}

This will rename all fields named id to id_, all fields named type to type_, etc.

items.title: 🎯 Scoped Format (Class-Specific)
items.text:
When you have the same field name in multiple classes but want different aliases for each, use the scoped format with ClassName.field:

{
  "User.name": "user_name",
  "Address.name": "address_name",
  "name": "default_name"
}

⚡ Priority: Scoped aliases take priority over flat aliases. In the example above:

  • User.name will be renamed to user_name
  • Address.name will be renamed to address_name
  • Any other class with a name field will use default_name

items.title: ✨ Generated Output
items.text:
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class User(BaseModel):
    user_name: str | None = Field(None, alias="name")
    id: int | None = None


class Address(BaseModel):
    address_name: str | None = Field(None, alias="name")
    city: str | None = None


class Root(BaseModel):
    root_name: str | None = Field(None, alias="name")
    user: User | None = None
    address: Address | None = None

items.title: 📌 Notes
items.text:
• The ClassName in scoped format must match the generated Python class name (after title conversion)
  • For allOf models, the final generated class name includes any configured prefix, suffix, or collision suffix. A matching final-name alias takes priority over a legacy alias using the original schema name; legacy aliases remain a fallback when no final-name alias is supplied.
  • When using --use-title-as-name, the class name is derived from the title property in the schema
  • Aliases are applied during code generation, so the original field names are preserved as Pydantic alias values for proper serialization/deserialization

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
datamodel-code-generator is organized around one central idea: many input formats are normalized into a shared generation graph, then rendered through output-model-specific backends.

This page is partly generated from source code. The generated inventory is intentionally small so the narrative can stay hand-written while release-time details such as parser routes and output backends stay synchronized.

items.title: Generation Pipeline
items.text:
flowchart TD
    subgraph entry["Entry points"]
        direction TB
        cli["CLI\n__main__.py"]
        api["Python API\ngenerate()"]
    end

    subgraph setup["Configuration and input handling"]
        direction TB
        config["GenerateConfig\nParserConfig"]
        normalize["Input normalization\ninfer / fetch / convert"]
    end

    subgraph parsing["Parsing"]
        direction TB
        parser["Parser.parse()"]
        raw["parse_raw()\nformat-specific parser"]
        model_graph["Generation graph\nDataModel / DataType / Reference"]
    end

    subgraph rendering["Rendering"]
        direction TB
        render["Templates\nmodel/template"]
        format["CodeFormatter"]
        output["Python files\nstdout / return value"]
    end

    cli --> api --> config --> normalize --> parser
    parser --> raw --> model_graph
    parser --> model_graph
    model_graph --> render --> format --> output

The CLI builds a Config from command-line arguments, pyproject.toml, and presets. It then calls the same generate() API that library users can call directly. generate() selects the parser, runs it, and either returns code or writes files. Model Processing Passes lists the passes inside Parser.parse().

items.title: Entry Points
items.text:
The executable entry point is defined in pyproject.toml:

datamodel-codegen = "datamodel_code_generator.__main__:main"

src/datamodel_code_generator/__main__.py owns CLI-only behavior:

  • fast paths for --version, --help, prompt helpers, and JSON Schema output
  • argument parsing and shell completion
  • pyproject.toml profile loading and inheritance
  • --check diff generation
  • --watch regeneration
  • structured JSON command output
  • --input-model loading before normal generation

src/datamodel_code_generator/__init__.py owns the public generation API:

  • generate()
  • input type inference
  • raw JSON/YAML/CSV/Dict conversion through genson
  • MCP tool schema conversion
  • parser construction
  • generated headers and output file writing
  • optional model metadata emission

items.title: Parser Model
items.text:
Each parser turns its input into DataModel objects. The parser-specific part is parse_raw(). The shared part is Parser.parse(), which handles sorting, module layout, imports, rendering, exports, formatting, and optional metadata.

flowchart TD
    parse["Parser.parse()"]
    raw["parse_raw()\nimplemented by subclasses"]
    sort["sort_data_models()"]
    modules["_build_module_structure()"]
    process["_process_single_module()"]
    render["_generate_module_output()"]
    metadata["_build_model_metadata()"]
    result["str or module map"]

    parse --> raw --> sort --> modules --> process --> render --> metadata --> result

JSON Schema is the main reusable parser surface. OpenAPI and AsyncAPI extend it. Avro, XML Schema, Protocol Buffers, raw data, and MCP tools convert to a JSON Schema-shaped document before using the same model-building machinery. GraphQL is the main parser that builds models directly from its own schema API.

Ordering and module splitting use small graph helpers. _scc.py finds strongly connected components with an iterative Tarjan traversal so large graphs do not hit Python recursion limits. parser/_graph.py provides stable topological ordering. Together they keep sort_data_models() deterministic and let _build_module_structure() move circular module SCCs into _internal.py forwarder modules when imports would otherwise cycle. The passes that read cycles or an order among models (module dependencies, class body order, circular root models, keep model order, alias cycles, nested model default factories) each take a snapshot of one reference graph, _reference_graph.py: the models by model key and the edges between them by kind, which answers their components and orders. The predicates that models answer on demand by walking base classes, root types or mapping defaults (inherited fields, ancestors, cyclic ancestry, the C3 order of bases, msgspec struct tags, pydantic protected namespaces, preservable root constraints, recursive dataclass mapping defaults) take a snapshot of the models they reach when asked and answer from it, each model once. Under the MODEL_GRAPH check, each answer is compared with the computation it replaced.

items.title: Intermediate Model Graph
items.text:
The generation graph is built from a small set of core objects:

  • DataModel: a generated class, root model, type alias, enum, scalar alias, or union alias.
  • DataModelFieldBase: one field on a generated model, including defaults, aliases, constraints, and metadata.
  • DataType: a Python type annotation tree, including containers, unions, literals, generated-model references, and imports.
  • Reference: a schema reference path and generated Python name.
  • GenerationStore: the parser-owned model list plus a query index over model and type dependencies.
classDiagram
    class Parser
    class GenerationStore
    class GenerationIndex
    class ModelResolver
    class DataModel
    class DataModelFieldBase
    class DataType
    class Reference

    Parser --> GenerationStore
    Parser --> ModelResolver
    GenerationStore --> GenerationIndex
    GenerationStore --> DataModel
    DataModel --> DataModelFieldBase
    DataModelFieldBase --> DataType
    DataModel --> Reference
    DataType --> Reference
    ModelResolver --> Reference

GenerationStore is the preferred mutation boundary for parser-side changes that affect dependency facts. Parser code should register models and update references, fields, bases, names, and paths through store methods instead of mutating the live objects directly. GenerationIndex keeps stable facts about the model list and gives later phases efficient queries such as "which data types point at this reference?". A refresh records only the models that were appended or that store mutations changed, and rebuilds every fact only when the model list changes otherwise or discard_derived_facts() drops them.

items.title: Model Processing Passes
items.text: Parser.parse() runs a fixed sequence of passes between parse_raw() and rendering. Most of them change models, fields and data types in place, so a fact that one pass reads may still be changed by a later pass. This section lists the passes in execution order, says when each fact becomes final, and shows where a new decision belongs. Paths are relative to src/datamodel_code_generator/; names are given as file:function so they can be found with git grep.

items.title: Layers
items.text:
Layer Entry point Purpose L0 input loading parser/jsonschema.py:JsonSchemaParser.parse_raw, parser/openapi.py:OpenAPIParser.parse_raw Load sources and normalize the raw document before any schema object exists. L1 parsing parser/jsonschema.py:JsonSchemaParser.parse_obj, parser/graphql.py:GraphQLParser.parse_raw Build Reference, DataModel and DataType objects and register models in the store. L2 settle segment settle of parser/base.py:Parser.__PIPELINE Settle yielding names, report diagnostics, sort models and base classes. L3 module structure parser/base.py:Parser._build_module_structure Group models into output modules, remove duplicates, reuse across modules, merge circular imports. L4 cross-module pre-pass segment plan of parser/base.py:Parser.__PIPELINE Facts every module reads before any module is processed. L5 per-module processing parser/base.py:Parser._process_single_module Prepare and process the models of one module; runs once per module and hands the module over to its render preparation. L6 cross-module finalization segments cross_module, generic_base_class, decide, render_preparation and finish of parser/base.py:Parser.__PIPELINE, parser/base.py:Parser._finalize_modules First point where every module has been processed: tags of tagged bases, import repairs, generic base class, decisions, constructor order and render preparation of each module, imports, final renames. L7 rendering parser/base.py:Parser.__render_modules, parser/base.py:Parser._generate_module_output, model/base.py:DataModel.render Module code, templates or compiled renderers, exports. L8 formatting and output format.py:CodeFormatter, __init__.py:_format_deferred_output, __init__.py:generate Format module bodies and write or return the result.

__init__.py:_parse_generation may run L0–L8 again with a fresh parser (root-model collapse that stops before a data type cycle, yielding names that class-keyed options name, untyped nullable maps, invalid dotted stdout modules). These are retries around the whole pipeline, not passes inside it.

L0. _load_source_dict calls _read_document, which keeps the document as written and, under --use-single-value-enum-as-const, rewrites one-value enum to const copy-on-write, except beside nullable: true when the value is not null (_single_value_enum_as_const, which skips instance-data keywords and extension keys other than x-propertyNames through _document_child_entries). _parse_file then calls _prepare_schema_resources, which adds the document to the schema graph (parser/_schema_graph.py): walk_schema_resources finds which absolute URI names which schema of it (the root, $id or draft-04 id resources, the implicit component resources of OpenAPI, $anchor and $dynamicAnchor) and returns one frozen DocumentResources record, from which ResourceRegistry.register fills the registry dicts L1 resolves references through; then $refs that resolve through an embedded $id are rewritten copy-on-write (_rewrite_schema_resource_refs), each $ref and $dynamicRef keyword becomes a ResolvedRef (a str equal to the value, carrying its RefEdge: the holder's location and document; SchemaGraphBuilder.with_ref_edges, copy-on-write, only at the keywords that hold schemas, never inside instance data, examples, extensions, OAuth scopes, discriminator mappings or unknown keywords; JsonSchemaObject and the OpenAPI ReferenceObject keep the edge through a wrap validator), and the location of every object of the prepared document is indexed (SchemaGraphBuilder.index_document, see Metadata Output). Referenced documents go through the same steps when resolve_ref loads them: documents enter the graph in the order L1 asks for them, and the graph never loads one by itself. With DATAMODEL_CODE_GENERATOR_CHECK_SCHEMA_GRAPH=1, which tests/conftest.py sets for the test suite, each registration is compared with the registry that the walk the graph replaced (_register_schema_resources) leaves for the same document, and each edge with its resolution at the sites: the key get_ref_data_type and resolve_ref would compute in their own context equals the edge's key, unless that context raises or names no value of a loaded document (a reference resolved outside its own document, recorded as fixed-context), and the object _load_ref_schema_object, get_ref_model, _resolve_asyncapi_ref and the api scope load is the registered target the edge names, except a pointer the parser splits at another / and references of documents that resolve references against themselves (_resolve_lenient_resource_ref). Every reference whose target is static carries an edge: a rewrite of a reference to name its target (rebased, canonicalized, lenient or normalized) keeps it (keep_resolved_ref); an object a reference names is read as a schema once (SchemaGraphBuilder.read_as_schema), so a $ref the walk read as data or names there (a nested definitions container) gets one too; schemas converted from another format are mounted with edges to the locations their targets are mounted at (an AsyncAPI payload converted from Protocol Buffers or XML Schema under the internal container of a root the graph owns for its document, SchemaGraphBuilder.mount_root and mount_in, so the loaded document is never written); and a reference the parser derives gets the edge of the reference it stands for, with its RefOrigin (_derived_ref: discriminator mappings and subtypes, x-python-type names, a merged $recursiveRef with a fixed target, an itemSchema projection, an AsyncAPI Reference Object). Only the references of the dynamic-scope rule (_dynamic_scope_target: a $recursiveRef, and a plain-name $dynamicRef bound in the dynamic scope or named by the first $dynamicAnchor of its name in the document being parsed) stay plain strings: they resolve against the dynamic scope of the model being parsed, not their own document. With report:<path>, one line per site and origin counts the references that reached it with their edge and as plain strings. Every L1 site takes the key of a reference from its edge (_ref_key, _ref_path): the edge's spelling resolved once, at its first consumption, in the document that holds it (_home_context: its location, root $id and, for an OpenAPI input document or under the api scope, its $self; a schema the parser keeps in a document of its own, an Avro schema of an AsyncAPI document, names that document as its edges' home) through the external mapping, the embedded resource, the normalized spelling and ModelResolver.resolve_ref; a new model is named after that spelling (ModelResolver._add_ref_at). A plain string has no edge and resolves in the context its caller set. OpenAPI and AsyncAPI register a schema that declares a discriminator, and a component schema whose allOf names one, under the key of the reference that names the schema from its own document (_schema_key), the key the references to it get, whatever document is being parsed when the discriminators are collected. A JSON object of a loaded document is validated once per parse (SchemaGraphBuilder.schema): the targets _load_ref_schema_object, _load_inherited_schema_object and OpenAPI's resolve_object load, the response and request body targets of get_ref_model, and the if, then, else and not branches _get_conditional_schema reads share one object per located value and its type, which no reader writes; the schema graph check compares each shared object at the end of L1 with the fingerprint taken when it was validated (kind="shared-schema"). The walks that follow references from a schema (field flags, literal and null checks, inherited properties and overrides, validation sources, uniqueItems rules, merged allOf values) visit each schema graph node once (SchemaNodeId, the location of the object a reference names: _key_node), and a $ref target merged with its sibling keywords is dumped once per node and document being parsed (_ref_target_dump). A local reference whose model a document has not parsed yet is reserved for that document (reserved_refs). _parse_file, _resolve_unparsed_json_pointer and AsyncAPI's _resolve_asyncapi_unparsed_json_pointer take the targets from one worklist (_reserved_targets: a ReservedTarget with the document, the key and the node the key names in the document's prepared tree), in key order, repeating while a round reserves more keys (_parse_file) or adds models (the others), and parse each target from the prepared tree; the schema graph check loads the source again and compares the value at each target (kind="reserved-target"). walk_schema_resources also keeps the anchor tables of each document: its $dynamicAnchor names (the first in walk order wins) and its $recursiveAnchor: true schemas (ResourceRegistry.anchor_tables). The $dynamicRef analysis (_dynamic_anchors_used, _dynamic_ref_edges) and the models specialized for a dynamic scope are keyed by the schema graph node a reference names, so references that spell one schema differently share its analysis and its specialized model. The fallbacks of the dynamic-scope rule still read the anchors L1 has registered so far (_build_anchor_indexes and _parse_file: the root, the definitions and each schema parsed through _parse_raw_or_validated_obj): _resolve_dynamic_ref, _resolve_recursive_ref and _recursive_ref_target. The schema graph check compares each of their answers with the one of the document's anchor tables and records a difference (kind="anchor-answer"): a $recursiveAnchor below properties is never registered, and an OpenAPI component's $dynamicRef parsed before the component that declares its anchor resolves through its edge instead. OpenAPI parses its main document in _parse_specification (merging path-level parameters into shallow copies of operations in _process_path_items) instead of _parse_file. Converted inputs (Avro, XML Schema, Protocol Buffers) build a JSON Schema dict and call _parse_file without _read_document, so document rewrites do not apply to them.

L1. Each place where the parser meets a schema object chooses its parse method from one table of parser/_schema_dispatch.py (Position): DEFINITION in _parse_schema_obj (definitions, roots, reserved targets, AsyncAPI payloads and the api scope), FIELD in parse_item (fields, items and map values) and OPENAPI_OPERATION in OpenAPIParser.parse_schema (the bodies, responses and parameters of the legacy scopes). A table holds, in order, the steps that rewrite the site (a $ref with sibling keywords merged with its target, _merge_ref_with_schema) and the rows whose predicates choose parse_array, parse_all_of, parse_one_of or parse_any_of (both through parse_combined_schema), parse_object, parse_enum, parse_root_type and the other builders; the rows of an object-kind schema (_OBJECT_KIND_ROWS) are shared by the definition table and _parse_object_kind_schema. Rows call the public hooks through the parser, so overriding subclasses keep working; a change of what a position parses is a row edit. _choose returns the chosen row and the position's method builds it in its own frame, so a nested schema costs no more stack frames per level than the parse methods it reaches (test_main_nesting_within_recursion_limit fails when it does). The schema graph check also asks the dispatch each table replaced (_legacy_*_path) and reports a schema for which it takes other entries (kind="dispatch"). That merge, the inherited $ref property merge (_resolve_inherited_parent_property) and a property that overrides an inherited one (_merge_properties_with_parent_constraints, unless --allof-merge-mode none) stand for the intersection of their parts: the earlier merge (_deep_merge, _merge_property_schemas) stays wherever it enforces what the intersection enforces, and parser/_intersection.py:intersect_keywords writes the tightest bounds, the least common multipleOf, the common type and enum values, the union of required and a false that a part sets where the merge does not; nested schemas follow the same rule. Where the document's dialect (draft 7 or earlier, OpenAPI 3.0) does not read $ref siblings as parts, a sibling enum that the document writes does not narrow the referenced schema (the legacy sibling enum row; an inherited property override is a part in every dialect). Null comes from the site's own nullable, type list or null value, else only if every part admits it. A keyword whose parts have no value in common keeps the earlier value and warns (warn_unsatisfiable); pattern, format, tuple positions, combinators and allOf members are not intersected there yet. A oneOf/anyOf of constants can become a synthetic enum (_extract_const_enum_from_combined). An enum class takes a value base (IntEnum, StrEnum, --use-subclass-enum's (T, Enum)) only when that base keeps every member value (T(v) == v, NaN equal to itself), and is a plain Enum otherwise (model/_decisions/enum_kind.py:decide_enum_kind). A const that admits some but not all values of the enum beside it leaves every enum class as written; parse_enum records the const for the model it builds (_note_const_narrowing), the end of L1 marks every value that names that model, and L5 __type_const_narrowed_values types those values. A Literal enum route (_enum_value_type), a propertyNames key and a Literal root type keep only the admitted values (_const_narrowed_enum); a const equal to none of the values only warns. Under --read-const-beside-enum and --use-single-value-enum-as-const each enum route reads an enum that admits the const beside it as that const, without an enum class (_reads_enum_as_const); like the L0 rewrite, it keeps an enum beside nullable: true and a const other than null, and a model built for the schema object itself then holds only the admitted values (_definition_enum). An object map, an object without properties whose keys and values patternProperties, propertyNames or additionalProperties type, is built by one builder at every position (_parse_object_map): one dict whose value type is the union of the value types of its key classes, never a union of dicts. The dict itself admits the null of a type array of object and null, or of nullable: true under --strict-nullable as _get_data_type does for other types, so property counts stay on it, and the other types of a type array join it in a union. A nullable that parse_combined_schema copies from an anyOf or oneOf parent into a branch is marked on the branch, and the dict of that branch leaves it to the union. Names come from ModelResolver.add. Each model records the location of the schema object it is built from on its Reference (_record_schema_object). Every use of a reference gets a new DataType that points to the one shared Reference. allOf $ref items become base classes; inherited fields whose parent is not parsed yet stay as placeholders that L5 resolves. Discriminators are only captured here (field.extras["discriminator"]). Field construction already decides const handling: DataModelFieldBase.__init__ calls process_const(), which types the const and decides its default and nullability (model/_decisions/literal_default.py). Dataclass-like models (dataclasses, Pydantic dataclasses, msgspec Structs) sort their fields when they are built, by DataModel.FIELD_CONSTRUCTION_ORDER_KEY. The key reads only facts known then: on a Pydantic dataclass, a None default that --strip-default-none may keep counts as no default, while a msgspec Struct counts every optional field as having one, as it never strips its defaults. __fix_constructor_field_ordering, after the decision phase, decides with the output model's assignment facts (DataModel._field_assignment_facts, the row FIELD_ASSIGNMENT_CHECKER is a view of), which state what the template writes, and moves fields whose default the template keeps after the fields without one.

L2–L4.

Pass (parser/base.py) Reads Changes ModelResolver.settle_yielding_names (reference.py) names that yield to --model-name-map Reference.name of yielding models sort_data_models references through the store index model order, models that need forward-reference updates sort_base_classes_for_mro base classes base order (before L3 and L5 reuse add bases) L3 _union_tags snapshot discriminator mappings union tags that reuse compares, taken before any merge L3 __delete_duplicate_models rendered model text (ModelShapes.key of parser/_model_shapes.py) redirects users, edits base lists, removes models L3 __replace_duplicate_name_in_module class names class_name L3 __reuse_model_tree_scope rendered model text across modules moves canonicals to a shared module, replaces duplicates by empty subclasses or removes them L3 __resolve_circular_imports module dependency graph, class names merges cyclic modules into _internal modules, relocates models; a model whose class name an earlier model of the merge holds takes <name>_<n> with the smallest n no merged model holds (_merged_class_names) L4 __flatten_conflicting_base_layouts (msgspec) bases, fields, possible tags (__find_possible_tag_names) and reuse duplicates (__find_possible_reuse_duplicates) copies base fields into Structs whose generated bases have conflicting layouts, sorted by the construction key (DataModel.FIELD_CONSTRUCTION_ORDER_KEY), and drops those bases L4 unconstrain_union_members (msgspec) union members field types L4 __set_circular_root_model_paths root-model reference graph the circular root models (RecursionFacts by model key) that every module's collapse reads

Module order is not dependency order: _internal modules of import cycles come first, then the tree-scope shared module, then _group_models_by_module's sort (longest module path first, reverse lexical). Single-file output has one module, so "per module" then means the whole graph.

L5, per module, in this order:

Step Pass (parser/base.py) Reads Changes prepare alias_shadowed_imports (parser/_passes/_shared.py) field names vs imported names import aliases prepare override_required_field (parser/_passes/_shared.py) inherited placeholders, base models (any module) replaces placeholders by copies of inherited fields, required, defaults prepare __replace_unique_list_to_set uniqueItems, defaults list to set (_create_set_from_list), set defaults prepare __change_from_import references to other modules module imports, data_type.alias prepare __extract_inherited_enum field-less models with Enum bases replaces the model by a new Enum with the same Reference, of the class of its first Enum base (decide_enum_kind) process __set_reference_default_value_to_field defaults of referenced models field defaults process __reuse_model rendered model text and union tags of this module's models replaces duplicates by empty subclasses (users in this module redirected) or removes them (Enums, --collapse-reuse-models: users in every module redirected) process __collapse_root_models root models referenced from this module (any module), circular paths from L4, the module of each inner model (found by identity in the live module lists) inlines root types, merges constraints, calls process_const() again, redirects references to a root model's inner model and imports it where this module does not emit it, renames (the parent strategy names the inner model of any module after the root it replaces, decided at the root's first holder; from then on the root is no member of its module for __change_from_import and __import_renamed_types), marks unused roots; inlining a root's tree under a data type that the tree reaches would make that data type contain itself, so collapse raises _CollapseRootModelsRecursionError before it and _parse_generation parses again with every circular root model kept named (a RecursionError in collapse takes the same retry and is a MODEL_GRAPH check violation) process __set_default_enum_member defaults vs Enum members defaults process __sort_models --keep-model-order model order process __change_field_name field names vs type names field names, class names of referenced types (any module) process __restore_inherited_field_names_for_unique_aliases inherited field names field names process __apply_discriminator_type captured discriminators, variant models (any module); tag values from model/_decisions/tag_value.py, tag defaults from model/_decisions/literal_default.py tag field types, required and defaults on variants, appended tag fields, msgspec struct tags (possibly deferred to a later module) process __type_const_narrowed_values values marked at the end of L1 with the const that narrows the enum they name, the enum now named (after reuse and collapse), its members types each value Literal[<Enum>.<member>] when the members equal their values and the output's Literal holds members, None for a null const; otherwise keeps the enum and warns once per schema location process __set_one_literal_on_default required one-literal fields; decision from model/_decisions/literal_default.py default, required, nullable process refresh_field_config (model) field state backend field config process __rename_fields_hiding_types same-named fields and types of the model family field names or type names process __remove_overridden_models model-level --type-overrides removes overridden models from the module's list (constructor ordering still runs on them) process __apply_field_type_overrides --type-overrides, field names field types of the kept models; model-level overrides edit nodes on fields in place process __type_dict_keys_by_root_types dict keys that name a RootModel whose instances cannot be dict keys (DataModel._keys_take_root_type: not frozen, no validators, methods or custom root template), its root type and Field() constraints (any module) types the key by the root type, the constraints written into a string type; follows root models inside that type, not union members of a key; refreshes the backend config finalize __apply_base_class_type_overrides model-level --type-overrides base classes; edits base-class nodes in place and keeps the generated model each replaced base stood for, which constructor ordering reads

L6, after the module loop:

Pass (parser/base.py) Changes _tag_fields_of_tagged_bases (msgspec) tags structs that inherit a tagged base (the tag field becomes a ClassVar) or opts them out __import_removed_reuse_canonicals imports of models that a later module's reuse removed __import_renamed_types imports of types that a later module renamed __import_enum_member_literal_classes imports for enum member literals __apply_generic_base_class inserts the generated base model and rewrites base classes decision phase: the decisions of Parser._DECISION_PASSES (omit_held_null behind --omit-redundant-reference-null) the facts each declares, read from FinalFacts (Decision Phase)

Render preparation, module by module in module order, for the models each module had at the end of L5:

Pass (parser/base.py) Reads Changes __fix_constructor_field_ordering required and default state, inherited fields (a base a model-level override replaced as the generated model it stood for), rendered nullability (types.py:DataType.admits_none), field types after overrides field order, constructor adjustments unbind_fields (model) hidden type names field binding __update_type_aliases model order, forward references quotes forward references in place (data_type.alias), union operator along one .parent chain __set_validate_default_on_fields live models, defaults deserialized defaults, default validation __assign_forward_reference_fields --use-annotated with deferred annotations assignment form, may reorder fields __warn_required_assignments_after_defaults field order warnings

Then, over every model:

Pass (parser/base.py) Changes __fix_tag_opt_out_field_ordering (msgspec) keyword-only order of the structs that opted out of a tag, and of those inheriting from them _finalize_modules: __prepare_type_alias_fields, finalize_type_alias_users (backend) type-alias field form, backend config __mark_set_item_models_hashable identity hash for set item models _finalize_structured_imports imports __decide_nested_model_default_factories, __freeze_field_render_plans the nested models' default factories (row legacy.L-NF), one frozen render plan per field of the built-in output models (B2) model imports snapshot, unused-model removal imports, module model lists remove_unused, resolve_module_import_conflicts (backend), _bind_module_field_names module imports, field binding __change_imported_model_name renames models that collide with imports (the last class-name change) model._name_final_classes (model hook) renders TypedDict extra_items again from the data type it was built from, so that it names the final class _check_model_inheritance, warnings, _set_nested_model_default_factory_metadata errors, warnings, publishes the nested-factory decision for the models that render without frozen plans

Three L6 passes repair results built from facts that changed afterwards: __import_removed_reuse_canonicals and __import_renamed_types (reuse and renames in a later module, including the parent collapse rename) and __fix_tag_opt_out_field_ordering (constructor ordering counts an opted-out struct's own field named like the tag at the place of the base's tag class variable).

Constructor ordering and render preparation run once, after the decision phase, for every model: ordering reads the facts every module and decision left, so a model's constructor no longer depends on whether the module of its base is processed before or after its own (since 0.87.0). Code that overrides _process_single_module and runs after super() sees the module before its constructor order and render preparation; the generic base class, the decision phase and that render preparation run in the pipeline before _finalize_modules, so an override of _finalize_modules that does not call super() no longer skips them, and a direct call of _finalize_modules no longer applies the generic base class.

Module imports. The passes from L1 to L7 write the imports of a module (ModuleContext.imports) and the imports all modules share (Parser.imports) only through parser/_imports_plan.py:ModuleImportLedger, which applies each write to the live Imports at once and keeps it as an entry with its producer: the pass (ImportPass), and the model and field it wrote for. The live Imports is the replay of its entries (replay). The import block that _generate_module_output writes is ModuleImportLedger.rendered: a copy of the live Imports minus what the entries wrote of their models' unrendered imports (DataModel._unrendered_imports), counted as the difference between the replay of the entries and their replay without those imports, so the module lines keep their order and imports written outside the ledger stay. The named row legacy.enum-member-import-bindings uses it: an Enum's imports keep the imports of its member declarations (pydantic's Field for described members), so the module binds their names for class names and reuse keys as in 0.86.0, while the import block leaves them out. The output model's resolve_module_import_conflicts gets the live Imports; ModuleImportLedger.external records what it changed. DATAMODEL_CODE_GENERATOR_CHECK_MODULE_IMPORTS compares each module's imports with the replay of their entries when the import text is written, so a write that bypasses the ledger fails the check, which the test suite turns on. The names the module's ModelResolver gives its imports are asked for through the ledger too (NameLog). After the last rename, Parser.__plan_module_imports plans the models each module names from the final names (NameTable): ModuleImportPlan holds the imports of other modules' models, named by allocate_bindings in the order the module asked for them (row legacy.alias-order), and what the module writes for each model. Nothing is written from the plan yet; under the same check, the module must write what the plan writes and its imports must bind every planned import.

L7. _generate_module_output builds the import block, calls the backend's render_module_code, renders each model and formats the body. DataModel.render uses the compiled renderer in model/_compiled_templates/ for built-in templates and Jinja2 when a custom template directory is set. Type-alias styles are chosen when the parser is built (model/__init__.py:get_data_model_types). Rendering a type hint and collecting a field's imports write no nullability: type_hint renders the None of the type, of the nullable model it names and, for a union, of the members whose hints strip it (types.py:DataType._hint_null_source), and import collection reads types.py:DataType.admits_none. Render preparation writes rendered nullability once, in its first pass (parser/base.py:Parser.__finalize_rendered_nullability, after the module bodies, whose type-alias updates write the union operators and quotes the members' hints read), through types.py:DataType._materialize_render_state, which marks the None it adds; msgspec's top-level None and the Field() default plan read the value without it (legacy-msgspec-top-level-null-as-written, legacy-strip-keeps-written-null-only). Before it, only parser/base.py:_flatten_union_members (L5 finalize), which moves member nullability onto the union, and L3's DataModel._write_pre_render_nullability (legacy-l3-import-nullability, which overrides and constructor ordering read; DataModel._prepare_dedup_key writes it for every field whose hint renders its own type before a dedup key renders, so such a type keeps the None of the nullable model it named when duplicate deletion points it at a model without one) write it; msgspec's _strip_null writes it on its own copies at L7. A decision before render preparation reads types.py:DataType.admits_none, which computes the rendered nullability with model/_decisions/nullability.py:rendered_nullability without writing it. A field of every built-in output model (Pydantic BaseModel, RootModel and dataclass, msgspec Struct, stdlib dataclass, TypedDict, enum, type alias) renders from one frozen render plan (model/_render_plan.py:FieldRenderPlan): its annotation form, its calls (Field(), field(), msgspec Meta()) with each argument and the declared items it writes, its default, the imports the calls need and every declared item it does not write (Omitted, with its reason), each with a Why. The field's backend builds it: model/pydantic_base.py:DataModelField (a Pydantic dataclass field adds the Field(...) of a forced assignment and the plain annotation of a call the dataclass must see, model/pydantic_v2/dataclass.py), model/msgspec.py:DataModelField (Meta(...) inside Annotated, then field(...) or the default alone), model/dataclass.py:DataModelField (field(...) or the default alone) and model/typed_dict.py:DataModelField (the ReadOnly[, Required[ and NotRequired[ qualifiers of the key); an enum member is a field of the output's backend, whose plan gives the member's imports. The last render preparation pass freezes one per field in the parse's RenderReady (B2), and field, annotated, type_hint, represented_default, has_default_factory_in_field, the import collection and the dropped-constraints warnings read the frozen plan, before B2 a plan built and not kept. Each frozen plan keeps what it read from its field (DataModelFieldBase._render_inputs: the field's attributes, and inside its types, constraints and containers), and when the model renders (DataModel._template_fields) the plan of a field where any of it changed, replaced or edited in place, is rebuilt (RenderReady.refreshed), so a model whose render changes its fields first writes the change, as a pass that changes a field after render preparation does. The plan holds values and writes its text when it is read, so the names it holds are the final ones. Custom templates get the raw fields, which answer from the same plan. DATAMODEL_CODE_GENERATOR_CHECK_RENDER_PLANS checks that each frozen or rebuilt plan writes or omits every item its field declares and that it renders as the plan rebuilt when the modules are written. Row legacy.L-NF: the nested models' default factories are decided when render preparation ends, but the import snapshot reads each field as if the factory were written (a second plan, RenderReady.import_view), and the models that render without frozen plans (GraphQL unions, custom output models) read the decision only once _set_nested_model_default_factory_metadata publishes it after the warnings. A RootModel's config items (its regex engine and freezing, the literal values it validates and the neutral extra of the validator helpers) are decided by pass decide_config_items once the helpers are planned (model/pydantic_v2/root_model.py:RootModel._decide_config_items); the ConfigDict import comes with the writer of each item's source, so the module imports collect it. A RootModel rendered outside a parse decides them, and its ConfigDict import, when it renders.

items.title: Pass Declarations
items.text:
Every pass is declared in parser/_pass_decls.py as a PassDecl: its name, phase, scope (once over every model, or once per output module over that module's models), kind (transform, plan, repair, check, setup, bookkeeping), the Fact and RenderFact members of parser/_facts.py it reads and writes, explicit order edges (after), the change that removes a repair (removed_by) and the phase it moves to (target). scripts/check_fact_finality.py (run by the test suite) checks that names are unique, phases never go back in execution order, a repair names what removes it, and setup, check and bookkeeping passes write no fact (a check pass may write the pseudo-fact STDERR, the warnings it emits, so that two passes that warn are ordered).

Parser.parse() runs the passes from class-level tables in parser/base.py (Parser.__PIPELINE, with the bodies of the overridable hooks _build_module_structure, _process_single_module and _finalize_modules), built from the steps of parser/_pipeline.py: a PassSpec runs one declared pass, when its condition holds; a ForEachModule runs passes module by module; a HookCall calls an overridable method whose default runs a sub-table; a Segment enters a phase on the store (GenerationStore.enter_phase, read as GenerationStore.phase) and the boundary before it (PARSED, B1, DECIDED, B2), then runs its steps. The Runner is the only caller of a pass, inside fact_pass(DECL) (parser/_finality.py) with the models the finality check compares; steps call passes through the parser instance, so overrides and --debug tracing apply as to any method. The two diagnostics warnings that name the code calling parse() find that frame however deep the pipeline is (stacklevel_at_parse_caller).

The order rule (parser/_pipeline.py:check_order): two passes of one segment conflict when one writes what the other reads or both write the same fact. Where only the earlier writes what the later reads, a derived edge orders them; every other conflicting pair needs explicit after edges, with their reasons, that connect it directly or through other edges. An explicit edge replaces the derived edge of its pair; one that runs a reader before a writer of what it reads is a provisional read, listed below the table. scripts/check_pass_pipeline.py (run by the test suite) checks that the tables run every declaration once in PASS_DECLS order, in the phase of its segment and with its scope, that the segments enter the boundaries in order and satisfy the order rule, that the repair set only shrinks, that every decision registry follows the rules of the Decision Phase, that only GenerationStore.seal_facts builds FinalFacts, that no code outside Parser reaches its name-mangled members, and lists the warnings whose stacklevel reaches past their caller. A pass trace (scripts/check_pass_pipeline.py --trace) records each pass that runs; the test suite keeps the traces of a few inputs and checks that some input runs every declared pass. The finality check (Fact Finality) compares the writes of fact rows with the declarations while the generator runs; reads and the writes of presentation rows are declared from the code. A new pass gets a declaration and a table entry.

Rendering the members' hints writes the import of the Any an empty union renders as. Runs when: use_default_factory_for_optional_nested_models. IMPORTS snapshot_model_imports global plan - every Fact, BACKEND_CONFIG, DEFAULT_EXPRESSION, IMPORT_ALIASES, QUOTING, TYPE_ALIAS_BODY Collects the imports of every model once; B2 precedes it. After snapshot_model_imports: the snapshot holds the imports of unused models, which leave with them. Runs when: additional properties reference classes. After name_final_classes_of_additional_properties: both write backend config; config items are decided last. After refresh_sequence_interface_after_renames: both write backend config; config items are decided last. After replan_schema_validators_after_renames: reads the neutral extra config that planning the validator helpers sets on root models. Runs when: use_default_factory_for_optional_nested_models. IMPORTS record_pydantic_floor global check - BACKEND_CONFIG, CONSTRAINTS, FIELD_ALIASES, FIELD_TYPES, MODEL_KIND, TYPE_ALIAS_BODY Runs when: an explicit target Pydantic version.
