items.title: behavior.naming-hint
items.text:
• Kind: behavior
  • Target: NamingHintWarning
  • Since: 0.86.0

The hint at --recommend-options that a command line generation shows when many class names are numbered collisions is experimental; when it is shown and its text may change.

A command line generation warns with datamodel_code_generator.NamingHintWarning when at least 10 class names, and at least one in five, are numbered collisions: names the model resolver numbered because the name without the number was taken, such as Pet1 beside Pet. It is shown at most once per command and never by generate(). An explicit --naming-strategy, --model-name-map, or deprecated --parent-scoped-naming, on the command line or in pyproject.toml, --check, --diff-against, --output-format json, --disable-warnings, and the options --recommend-options refuses (--watch, --all-jobs, and more than one --job) leave it out; a filter that turns warnings into errors drops it. It never changes the generated files, the result of --check, or the exit code.

items.title: behavior.batch-generation-jobs
items.text:
• Kind: behavior
  • Target: [tool.datamodel-codegen.jobs], --job, --all-jobs
  • Since: 0.72.3

Named batch jobs are experimental; their configuration schema, batch output, and transactional/watch execution contracts may change.

Define named generation jobs in [tool.datamodel-codegen.jobs] and select them with --job or --all-jobs. Each selected job has its own input and output, and the full selection is validated before generation begins.

items.title: behavior.remote-reference-lock
items.text:
• Kind: behavior
  • Target: datamodel-codegen.lock, --lockfile, --update-lock, and --locked
  • Since: 0.72.3

Remote reference integrity locking is experimental: the lock document schema and request-identity compatibility may evolve, but integrity mismatches remain fail-closed and credentials are never persisted.

The lock stores opaque SHA-256 request-identity digests and SHA-256 body digests, never response bodies or request values directly. Each saved display origin contains only the scheme, host, and explicit port—never a path, query, or request headers.

items.title: cli-option.generate-client
items.text:
• Kind: cli-option
  • Target: --generate-client httpx2 and the --client-* options (and their [tool.datamodel-codegen] keys and generate() options)
  • Since: 0.84.0

HTTPX2 client generation from the CLI is experimental; its options and generated package may change.

--generate-client httpx2 generates the models at --output and a client package at --client-output; --client-package and --client-model-package name their import paths, and the other --client-* options configure the package. Like model options, they can be set in [tool.datamodel-codegen] of pyproject.toml, in its profiles, and in its jobs. --check, --diff-against, --watch, --output-format json, and the uv add and next-step notice on stderr work as with --generate-server. generate() takes them as generate_client and the client_* options, and returns every generated file without an output. It needs Python 3.11 or later, both to run and as --target-python-version, --use-missing-sentinel for pydantic_v2.dataclass models, --target-pydantic-version 2.14 with --use-missing-sentinel, and --use-msgspec-tagged-unions and --use-msgspec-nullable-enum-alias for msgspec.Struct models; one left unset takes that value, as with --generate-server.

items.title: cli-option.generate-schema-validators
items.text:
• Kind: cli-option
  • Target: --generate-schema-validators
  • Since: 0.66.1

Schema-derived runtime validators are experimental and may change as JSON Schema coverage is expanded.

The option currently targets Pydantic v2 BaseModel output and covers selected object-level rules such as patternProperties, required-only oneOf/anyOf/not groups, and simple if/then/else required-property conditions.

items.title: cli-option.generate-server
items.text:
• Kind: cli-option
  • Target: --generate-server fastapi and the --server-* options (and their [tool.datamodel-codegen] keys and generate() options)
  • Since: 0.84.0

FastAPI server generation from the CLI is experimental; its options and generated package may change.

--generate-server fastapi generates the models at --output and a server package at --server-output, whose main.py serves the application with the implementations in the services package beside it; generation writes each missing module of services once, with stubs, and never overwrites one. --server-package and --server-model-package name their import paths, and the other --server-* options configure the package. Like model options, they can be set in [tool.datamodel-codegen] of pyproject.toml, in its profiles, and in its jobs. --check compares without writing, --diff-against compares the files two inputs render, --watch regenerates after input changes, --output-format json uses the model generation, check, and input-diff payloads, and generation prints a uv add command and the next steps to stderr. generate() takes them as generate_server and the server_* options, and returns every generated file without an output, writing no stubs. It needs Python 3.11 or later, both to run and as --target-python-version, --use-missing-sentinel for pydantic_v2.dataclass models, --target-pydantic-version 2.14 with --use-missing-sentinel, and --openapi-scopes with api. A setting left unset, by the options, pyproject.toml, generate(), and the preset, takes that value, and the command line prints how to set it; one set otherwise is refused.

items.title: cli-option.install-skill
items.text:
• Kind: cli-option
  • Target: --install-skill, --skill-scope, and --overwrite-skill
  • Since: 0.76.0

Bundled Agent Skill installation is experimental; supported clients, scopes, and installed skill contents may change.

Use --install-skill with codex or claude-code. --skill-scope selects a project or user installation, and --overwrite-skill safely replaces an existing regular skill directory.

items.title: cli-option.recommend-options
items.text:
• Kind: cli-option
  • Target: --recommend-options, its rule data, its candidate comparison, its JSON payload, and --generate-prompt --recommend-options with the prompt JSON field recommendation
  • Since: 0.86.0

Option recommendations are experimental; the rules, the schema signals they read, the class-name metrics, the report, and the JSON payload may change.

--recommend-options reads the input schema, measures naming-relevant signals of OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, and JSON Schema documents, and prints the latest dated preset to start from with the options to add, as a command and a pyproject.toml block. Options set on the command line or in pyproject.toml are kept. For schemas of up to 3000 estimated models, it also generates the candidate configurations in memory and recommends the one whose class names score best; nothing is written. With --generate-prompt, the prompt embeds the report, and its JSON output carries the recommend-options payload as recommendation.

items.title: cli-option.schema-validator-type
items.text:
• Kind: cli-option
  • Target: --schema-validator-type
  • Since: 0.66.1

Schema-derived runtime validator backend selection is experimental and may change as validation backends are added.

The only currently implemented backend is 'pydantic-v2', which preserves the existing generated Pydantic v2 validator behavior.

items.title: cli-option.use-missing-sentinel
items.text:
• Kind: cli-option
  • Target: --use-missing-sentinel
  • Since: 0.66.1

Pydantic MISSING sentinel output is experimental because it depends on pydantic.experimental.missing_sentinel, or on pydantic.MISSING for a 2.14 target.

The option requires Pydantic v2 BaseModel or dataclass output and a target Pydantic version that supports the MISSING sentinel. Server and client generation require it for Pydantic v2 dataclass output, and --target-pydantic-version 2.14 with it.

items.title: cli-option.use-type-alias
items.text:
• Kind: cli-option
  • Target: --use-type-alias
  • Since: 0.36.0

Type alias output is experimental and may change as Python typing support evolves.

The option replaces root model classes with type aliases where possible. Pydantic v2 output may use TypeAliasType or Python 3.12 type statements depending on the target Python version.

items.title: cli-option.use-type-alias-type
items.text:
• Kind: cli-option
  • Target: --use-type-alias-type
  • Since: 0.71.1

Runtime TypeAliasType output is experimental and may change as Python typing support evolves.

The option implies --use-type-alias and selects TypeAliasType for Python 3.10 and 3.11. Python 3.12 and newer continue to use native type statements.

items.title: extra.httpx2
items.text:
• Kind: extra
  • Target: datamodel-code-generator[httpx2]
  • Since: 0.71.1

The HTTPX2-backed HTTP client is experimental and may change as compatibility is validated.

datamodel-code-generator[http] remains the stable HTTPX backend and is not deprecated; datamodel-code-generator[httpx2] is experimental. The default HTTP backend policy is auto: stable httpx is selected when its client module is installed, including when both pairs are installed, and experimental httpx2 is selected only when that module is absent. Use --http-backend httpx2 or HTTPBackend.HTTPX2 to require the experimental pair. Explicit selections and paired dependency errors do not fall back.

items.title: formatter.builtin
items.text:
• Kind: formatter
  • Target: --formatters builtin
  • Since: 0.59.0

The internal formatter is experimental and may change as generated-output coverage is expanded.

The formatter is designed for generated model modules and is not a general-purpose Python formatter.

items.title: input-format.asyncapi
items.text:
• Kind: input-format
  • Target: --input-file-type asyncapi
  • Since: 0.59.0

AsyncAPI input support is experimental and may change as real-world usage is validated.

The parser focuses on message payload model generation from AsyncAPI documents.

items.title: input-format.avro
items.text:
• Kind: input-format
  • Target: --input-file-type avro
  • Since: 0.59.0

Apache Avro schema input support is experimental and may change as real-world usage is validated.

The parser generates Python models from Avro schemas; it does not provide Avro runtime validation.

items.title: input-format.mcp-tools
items.text:
• Kind: input-format
  • Target: --input-file-type mcp-tools
  • Since: 0.60.0

MCP tool schema profile input support is experimental and may change as MCP schemas evolve.

The input is converted from MCP tool inputSchema/outputSchema entries into JSON Schema definitions before model generation.

items.title: input-format.protobuf
items.text:
• Kind: input-format
  • Target: --input-file-type protobuf
  • Since: 0.59.0

Protocol Buffers input support is experimental and may change as real-world usage is validated.

The parser generates Python models from .proto schemas; it does not provide protobuf runtime validation or gRPC code generation.

items.title: input-format.xmlschema
items.text:
• Kind: input-format
  • Target: --input-file-type xmlschema
  • Since: 0.59.0

XML Schema input support is experimental and may change as real-world usage is validated.

The parser focuses on model generation from XSD documents, not full XML instance validation.

items.title: 🔀 oneOf/anyOf generates unexpected Union types
items.text:
When using oneOf or anyOf, the generated models may not match your expectations. Use --union-mode to control how unions are generated:

# Smart union (Pydantic v2 only) - validates against types in order
datamodel-codegen --union-mode smart --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel ...

# Left-to-right validation
datamodel-codegen --union-mode left_to_right ...

See CLI Reference: --union-mode for details.

items.title: 🔗 allOf doesn't merge properties as expected
items.text:
Control how allOf schemas merge fields:

# Merge only constraints (minItems, maxItems, pattern, etc.) - default
datamodel-codegen --allof-merge-mode constraints ...

# Merge constraints + annotations (default, examples)
datamodel-codegen --allof-merge-mode all ...

# Don't merge any fields
datamodel-codegen --allof-merge-mode none ...

When primitive allOf branches are merged, combining number and integer produces integer in every merge mode. Numeric type arrays may also include null; only types shared by every branch are retained, in their original order. An empty numeric/null intersection raises a schema error.

See CLI Reference: --allof-merge-mode for details.

📎 Related: #399

items.title: 📁 How to generate from multiple schema files?
items.text:
Use a directory as input, or use $ref to reference other files:

# Generate from directory containing multiple schemas
datamodel-codegen --input schemas/ --output models/

For schemas with remote cross-file $ref, install an HTTP extra:

pip install 'datamodel-code-generator[http]'

See HTTP backend selection for the stable and experimental choices.

📎 Related: #215

items.title: 🔤 YAML bool keywords (YES, NO, true, false) in string enums
items.text:
YAML 1.1 treats unquoted keywords like YES, NO, on, off, true, false as boolean values. This tool preserves them as strings to avoid unexpected conversions in schema contexts:

# Input YAML
enum:
  - YES
  - NO
  - NOT_APPLICABLE

# Generated code (strings preserved)
class MyEnum(Enum):
    YES = "YES"
    NO = "NO"
    NOT_APPLICABLE = "NOT_APPLICABLE"

This matches the expected behavior when type: string is specified in your schema. If you need the previous behavior where YAML bool keywords were converted to Python booleans, please open an issue describing your use case.

📎 Related: #1653, #1766, #2338

items.title: ⚠️ mypy complains about Field constraints
items.text:
If mypy reports errors about conint, constr, or other constrained types, use --field-constraints or --use-annotated:

# Use Field(..., ge=0) instead of conint(ge=0)
datamodel-codegen --field-constraints ...

# Use Annotated[int, Field(ge=0)]
datamodel-codegen --use-annotated ...

See Field Constraints for more information.

items.title: 🤔 Type checker doesn't understand generated types
items.text:
Ensure you're using the correct target Python version:

datamodel-codegen --target-python-version 3.11 ...

This affects type syntax generation (e.g., list[str] vs List[str], X | Y vs Union[X, Y]).

items.title: 🚫 Property names conflict with Python reserved words
items.text:
Properties like class, from, import are automatically renamed with a field_ prefix. Control this behavior:

# Custom prefix (default: "field")
datamodel-codegen --special-field-name-prefix my_prefix ...

# Remove special prefix entirely
datamodel-codegen --remove-special-field-name-prefix ...

items.title: 🔣 Field names have special characters
items.text:
JSON/YAML property names with spaces, dashes, or special characters are converted to valid Python identifiers. An alias is automatically generated to preserve the original name:

class Model(BaseModel):
    my_field: str = Field(..., alias="my-field")

To disable aliases:

datamodel-codegen --no-alias ...

See Field Aliases for custom alias mappings.

items.title: 🐍 Want snake_case field names from camelCase
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --snake-case-field ...

This generates snake_case field names with camelCase aliases:

class User(BaseModel):
    first_name: str = Field(..., alias="firstName")

items.title: ⏰ Generated output changes on every run
items.text:
The timestamp in the header changes on each run. Disable it for reproducible output:

datamodel-codegen --disable-timestamp ...

items.title: 🌍 Output differs between environments
items.text:
Ensure consistent formatting across environments:

# Explicitly set formatters
datamodel-codegen --formatters black isort ...

# Or disable formatting entirely for raw output
datamodel-codegen --formatters ...

Also ensure the same Python version and formatter configurations (pyproject.toml) are used.

items.title: 🤖 CI fails because generated code is different
items.text:
Use --check mode in CI to verify generated files are up-to-date:

datamodel-codegen --check --input schema.yaml --output models.py

This exits with code 1 if the output would differ, without modifying files.

items.title: 🧹 Files from earlier runs remain in the output directory
items.text:
Generation overwrites the files it writes and never deletes a file an earlier run wrote. Remove files that are no longer generated yourself; --check of a directory output lists them as EXTRA.

A stale package can hide a new module. When a schema change turns a package of a directory output into a module, for example models/pets/ into models/pets.py, or a directory output models/ gives way to a single-file output models.py, the old directory stays, and Python imports a directory that holds an __init__.py in preference to the module of the same name. Generation still writes the module and warns that the existing package directory shadows it, naming both paths; remove the stale directory. A directory whose only __init__ is a compiled __init__.pyc or an extension module hides the module in the same way but is not reported. --check and --diff-against write nothing and do not warn. --disable-warnings and Python warning filters silence the warning; a filter that turns it into an error, such as -W error::UserWarning, stops the run before it writes anything.

items.title: 🐢 Generation is slow for large schemas
items.text:
For very large schemas with many models:

  1. Use --reuse-model to deduplicate identical models
  2. Consider splitting schemas into multiple files
  3. Use --disable-warnings to reduce output
datamodel-codegen --reuse-model --disable-warnings ...

See Model Reuse and Deduplication for details.

items.title: 🤷 Which output model type should I use?
items.text:
• Pydantic v2 (pydantic_v2.BaseModel): ✨ Recommended for new projects. Better performance and modern API.
  • dataclasses: Simple data containers without validation.
  • TypedDict: Type hints for dict structures.
  • msgspec: High-performance serialization.

See Output Model Types for a detailed comparison.

# For new projects
datamodel-codegen --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel ...

See Output Model Types for more details.

📎 Related: #803

items.title: 💥 Generated code doesn't work with my Pydantic version
items.text:
Ensure the output model type matches your installed Pydantic version:

# Check your Pydantic version
python -c "import pydantic; print(pydantic.VERSION)"

# Generate for Pydantic v2
datamodel-codegen --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel ...

items.title: 📡 Cannot fetch schema from URL
items.text:
Install the HTTP extra:

pip install 'datamodel-code-generator[http]'

The http extra is the stable choice. See HTTP backend selection if you want to use the experimental HTTPX2 backend.

For authenticated endpoints:

datamodel-codegen --url https://api.example.com/schema.yaml \
    --http-headers "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" \
    --output model.py

items.title: 🔄 Which HTTP client backend is selected?
items.text:
The HTTP extras install separate, matched client and transport stacks:

Extra Status Client and transport datamodel-code-generator[http] Stable, supported, and not deprecated httpx + httpcore datamodel-code-generator[httpx2] Experimental httpx2 + httpcore2

datamodel-code-generator[all] includes the stable http extra but intentionally does not include the experimental httpx2 extra.

Select the backend with --http-backend {auto,httpx,httpx2}, the corresponding http_backend pyproject setting, or HTTPBackend in the public API:

  1. auto is the default. It selects stable httpx when its client module is installed, including when both pairs are installed.
  2. auto uses experimental httpx2 + httpcore2 only when the stable HTTPX client itself is unavailable.
  3. httpx and httpx2 require the selected pair. Explicit selections never fall back to a different backend.
  4. A missing paired transport or another broken dependency in a selected stack raises its import error instead of hiding an invalid environment.
  5. If auto finds neither client, the request fails with instructions to install an HTTP extra.

Selection and imports are lazy. Once auto selects a backend, it keeps that selection for the process. Restart the process to change an already selected backend after installing or removing an extra.

pyproject.toml
[tool.datamodel-codegen]
http-backend = "httpx2"

items.title: 🔒 SSL certificate errors
items.text:
For development/testing with self-signed certificates:

datamodel-codegen --url https://... --http-ignore-tls --output model.py

⚠️ Security Notice

Only use --http-ignore-tls in trusted environments.

items.title: 🌐 How can I request another HTTP library for generated API clients?
items.text:
The experimental Python client, generated with --generate-client httpx2, uses HTTPX2 for both synchronous and asynchronous requests. If you need aiohttp or another HTTP library, check existing issues, then start a discussion if your use case is not covered. Include the library you need, your use case, and whether you need synchronous or asynchronous support. For performance-related requests, include a reproducible benchmark and the Python and library versions.

This concerns requests made by generated API clients. HTTP backend selection controls fetching remote schemas during generation.

items.title: 📝 How to handle readOnly/writeOnly properties?
items.text:
Use --read-only-write-only-model-type to generate separate Request/Response models:

# Generate Request/Response models only
datamodel-codegen --read-only-write-only-model-type request-response ...

# Generate Base + Request + Response models
datamodel-codegen --read-only-write-only-model-type all ...

📎 Related: #727

items.title: ❓ Why are nullable fields not Optional?
items.text:
Use --strict-nullable to treat nullable fields as truly optional:

datamodel-codegen --strict-nullable ...

📎 Related: #327

items.title: 📦 How to use TypeAlias instead of RootModel?
items.text:
Use --use-type-alias (experimental) to generate type aliases instead of root models:

datamodel-codegen --use-type-alias --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel ...

See Root Models and Type Aliases for details.

📎 Related: #2505

items.title: Opt-in behaviour changes in 0.87.0
items.text:
This section lists every change in generated behaviour that is available as an option or as a dated preset, with the schema shapes it affects, a before/after example and the release it appeared in.

The default output stays as in the previous release. A change that alters generated behaviour is never the new default, even when it is a fix or an improvement: it ships behind its own option. The only changes to the default output are changes that do not alter behaviour (formatting, redundant lines, import order) and fixes for inputs that crashed or produced code that could not be imported; see Crash and import fixes in the default output.

items.title: How to opt in
items.text:
Pass the option of a section below to enable that change on its own:

datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --use-tuple-for-closed-arrays --output model.py

To enable every option in this section at once, use the 20261019 preset (see Presets); --use-typed-map-values-beside-other-types takes effect only together with --use-typed-nullable-map-values, which no preset sets. Explicit options override preset-supplied values, and options can be added on top of a preset.

Class

Every section below has the class opt-in: the option changes what the generated models accept or reject, how they are named or ordered, or which types they use. Without the option the output is byte-identical to 0.86.0.

See also: Presets, Deprecations, CLI Reference.

items.title: --filter-literal-values
items.text:
Option --filter-literal-values Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #5100

Affects: enum or const values that fail the constraints written beside them (for example maximum). --omit-redundant-constraints implies this option.

Schema: {"type": "object", "properties": {"level": {"type": "integer", "enum": [1, 5, 10, 50], "maximum": 10}}}.

Without the option (same as 0.86.0):

class Level(IntEnum):
    integer_1 = 1
    integer_5 = 5
    integer_10 = 10
    integer_50 = 50

With the option:

class Level(IntEnum):
    integer_1 = 1
    integer_5 = 5
    integer_10 = 10

items.title: --read-const-beside-enum
items.text:
Option --read-const-beside-enum Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #5101, #5102

Affects: a const written beside an enum. A value whose enum admits only some values is typed by the const; an enum that contains its const is generated as that const under --use-single-value-enum-as-const. --use-single-value-enum-as-const alone keeps its 0.86.0 output. A plain Enum and msgspec enums keep the enum type and warn that the other values are accepted.

Schema: levels is an array of {"type": "integer", "enum": [1, 2, 3], "const": 2}. A second case, kind: {"type": "string", "enum": ["a"], "const": "a"} with --use-single-value-enum-as-const, writes kind: Literal['a'] | None without the Kind enum class when --read-const-beside-enum is added.

Without the option (same as 0.86.0):

class Model(BaseModel):
    levels: list[Level] | None = None

With the option:

class Model(BaseModel):
    levels: list[Literal[Level.integer_2]] | None = None

items.title: --use-tuple-for-closed-arrays
items.text:
Option --use-tuple-for-closed-arrays Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #5103

Affects: prefixItems arrays closed by items: false, unevaluatedItems: false, a false position or contains, and items arrays closed by additionalItems: false. --use-tuple-for-fixed-items alone keeps its 0.86.0 output.

Schema: point is {"type": "array", "prefixItems": [{"type": "number"}, {"type": "string"}], "minItems": 2, "items": false}.

Without the option (same as 0.86.0):

class Model(BaseModel):
    point: list[float | str] = Field(..., max_length=2, min_length=2)

With the option:

class Model(BaseModel):
    point: tuple[float, str]

items.title: --pin-aliases-with-alias-generator
items.text:
Option --pin-aliases-with-alias-generator Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #5104

Affects: Pydantic v2 models and Pydantic dataclasses that use an alias_generator; with --target-pydantic-version older than 2.8, dataclasses whose config names a generator. Other output model types ignore the option.

Command: --output-model-type pydantic_v2.dataclass --snake-case-field --target-pydantic-version 2 --extra-template-data data.json with {"#all#": {"alias_generator": "to_camel"}}; the schema has the required properties firstName and foo_bar.

Without the option (same as 0.86.0):

@dataclass
class AliasGeneratorModel:
    first_name: str
    foo_bar: str = Field(..., alias="foo_bar")

With the option:

@dataclass
class AliasGeneratorModel:
    foo_bar: str
    first_name: str = Field(..., alias="firstName")

items.title: --tag-msgspec-by-payload-name
items.text:
Option --tag-msgspec-by-payload-name Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #5105

Affects: msgspec.Struct discriminated unions whose discriminator property has a name that differs from its Python name (for example pet-kind). --use-msgspec-tagged-unions already behaves this way. Other output model types ignore the option.

Schema (abridged): Cat and Dog each have a required property pet-kind with a const; pet is a oneOf of both with discriminator.propertyName: "pet-kind".

Without the option (same as 0.86.0):

class Cat(Struct, tag_field="pet_kind", tag="cat"):
    name: str | UnsetType = UNSET

With the option:

class Cat(Struct, tag_field="pet-kind", tag="cat"):
    name: str | UnsetType = UNSET

items.title: --order-constructor-fields-by-final-names
items.text:
Option --order-constructor-fields-by-final-names Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #5106

Affects: dataclasses.dataclass, pydantic_v2.dataclass and msgspec.Struct subclasses that override an inherited, renamed field as required (the override keeps the position of the inherited field instead of becoming keyword-only). Other output model types ignore the option.

Two modules: a.json defines Base with a property Bar, b.json defines Child as allOf: [{"$ref": "a.json"}] with Bar required. Command: --output-model-type pydantic_v2.dataclass --target-python-version 3.11.

Without the option (same as 0.86.0):

@dataclass
class Child(Base):
    Bar_1: a.Bar = Field(..., alias="Bar", kw_only=True)
    Zed: str | None = None

With the option:

@dataclass
class Child(Base):
    Bar_1: a.Bar = Field(..., alias="Bar")
    Zed: str | None = None

items.title: --use-site-models-for-constrained-refs
items.text:
Option --use-site-models-for-constrained-refs Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #5107

Affects: a $ref that carries more assertions beside it, or in an allOf with it (constraints, an enum or a type). The referenced definition itself stays unchanged.

Schema: quantity is allOf: [{"$ref": "#/$defs/Quantity"}] with maximum: 10, sizes holds items allOf: [{"$ref": "#/$defs/Size"}, {"enum": ["m", "l"]}]. In 0.86.0 maximum and the narrowed enum are not enforced.

Without the option (same as 0.86.0):

class Order(BaseModel):
    quantity: Quantity | None = None
    sizes: list[Size] | None = None

With the option:

class Quantity1(RootModel[conint(ge=1, le=10)]):
    root: conint(ge=1, le=10)


class Size2(Enum):
    m = "m"
    l = "l"


class Order(BaseModel):
    quantity: Quantity1 | None = None
    sizes: list[Size2] | None = None

items.title: --intersect-allof-keywords
items.text:
Option --intersect-allof-keywords Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #5108, #4951

Affects: keywords combined through allOf values, $ref siblings or inherited overrides. Numeric and length constraints are intersected, enums narrowed to the values every part accepts, patterns conjoined, and null members dropped beside a type that excludes null (for example kind: str | None becomes kind: str when the child requires a str).

Schema: Target is {"type": ["object", "null"], "additionalProperties": {"type": "string"}} and Holder is {"allOf": [{"$ref": "#/$defs/Target", "type": "object"}]}. type: object excludes null, so only the map remains.

Without the option (same as 0.86.0):

class Holder(BaseModel):
    pass

With the option:

class Holder(RootModel[dict[str, str]]):
    root: dict[str, str]

items.title: --use-single-dict-for-object-maps
items.text:
Option --use-single-dict-for-object-maps Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #5113

Affects: objects without properties whose keys are constrained by patternProperties or propertyNames. The key pattern joins every pattern, the value is the union of the value types, and keys outside the patterns are typed by additionalProperties. A warning names the cases one dict cannot express exactly. The stricter pattern-map checks of --generate-schema-validators are under --check-pattern-maps-strictly.

Schema: patternProperties with ^i- (string) and ^n- (integer).

Without the option (same as 0.86.0):

class Model(
    RootModel[dict[constr(pattern=r'^i-'), str] | dict[constr(pattern=r'^n-'), int]]
):

With the option:

class Model(RootModel[dict[constr(pattern=r'^i-|^n-'), str | int]]):

items.title: --check-pattern-maps-strictly
items.text:
Option --check-pattern-maps-strictly Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #5152

Affects: patternProperties checked by --generate-schema-validators; the option does nothing without it. A declared property is also checked against every matching pattern whose schema its own does not imply (x-id beside ^x- with maxLength: 3 rejects "abcd"), the dict root model of an object without properties counts every key a pattern admits and takes its keys from propertyNames, and the model of an object without properties keeps the other types of its type array.

Schema: labels is {"type": "object", "patternProperties": {"^l-": {"type": "integer"}}, "additionalProperties": false, "minProperties": 1}.

Without the option (same as 0.86.0; every non-empty object is rejected):

class Labels(_JsonSchemaRuntimeValidationBase, RootModel[dict[str, Any]]):
    root: dict[str, Any] = Field(..., max_length=0, min_length=1)

With the option:

class Labels(_JsonSchemaRuntimeValidationBase, RootModel[dict[str, Any]]):
    root: dict[str, Any] = Field(..., min_length=1)

items.title: --read-unevaluated-properties
items.text:
Option --read-unevaluated-properties Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #5114

Affects: a schema-valued unevaluatedProperties on a schema that no applicator (allOf, anyOf, oneOf, not, if, dependentSchemas, dependencies or a reference) evaluates in place. It is read like additionalProperties: extra keys are typed, and an object without properties becomes a typed map.

Schema: Resource has a required name and unevaluatedProperties: {"type": "string"}.

Without the option (same as 0.86.0):

class Resource(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="allow")
    name: str

With the option:

class Resource(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="allow")
    __annotations__ = {"__pydantic_extra__": Dict[str, str]}
    name: str

items.title: --dedupe-request-response-variants
items.text:
Option --dedupe-request-response-variants Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #5115

Affects: --read-only-write-only-model-type request-response and all. The read and write variants are decided from the schema graph: no unreferenced duplicate variants, stable numbering, and the inline models of an allOf parent are written once. Some recursive schemas cannot be generated without the option, and the error names it.

Schema (OpenAPI): Child inherits Parent through allOf, Parent.id is readOnly, and Parent.payload is an inline object. Command: --read-only-write-only-model-type request-response. Payload1 is written but never referenced in the first block.

Without the option (same as 0.86.0):

class Payload1(BaseModel):
    value: Value | None = None


class Payload2(BaseModel):
    value: Value | None = None


class ParentRequest(BaseModel):
    payload: Payload2 | None = None

With the option:

class Payload1(BaseModel):
    value: Value | None = None


class ParentRequest(BaseModel):
    payload: Payload1 | None = None

items.title: --order-constructor-fields-by-written-defaults
items.text:
Option --order-constructor-fields-by-written-defaults Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #5116

Affects: msgspec.Struct output under --strip-default-none. Every optional field goes after the required fields in schema order, which changes the order of the positional constructor arguments. Without the option a struct is reordered only where a required field would otherwise follow a default. Other output model types, and runs without --strip-default-none, ignore the option.

Command: --output-model-type msgspec.Struct --strip-default-none. Schema: optional d (string, default "x"), t ([string, null]) and q (string).

Without the option (same as 0.86.0):

class Spelling(Struct):
    t: str | None | UnsetType = UNSET
    q: str | UnsetType = UNSET
    d: str | UnsetType = "x"

With the option:

class Spelling(Struct):
    d: str | UnsetType = "x"
    t: str | None | UnsetType = UNSET
    q: str | UnsetType = UNSET

items.title: --read-nullable-beside-type-list
items.text:
Option --read-nullable-beside-type-list Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #5117, #5052

Affects: a type list that holds an object and another type, with nullable: true beside it (OpenAPI 3.0), under --strict-nullable or --use-missing-sentinel. The root model admits None, as it does when the list holds "null".

Schema: U: {type: [object, string], nullable: true, properties: {x: {type: integer}}}, with --use-missing-sentinel.

Without the option (same as 0.86.0):

class U1(RootModel[U | str | MISSING]):
    root: U | str | MISSING = MISSING

With the option:

class U1(RootModel[U | str | None | MISSING]):
    root: U | str | None | MISSING = MISSING

items.title: --keep-field-defaults-off-branch-roots
items.text:
Option --keep-field-defaults-off-branch-roots Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #5118, #4987

Affects: an anyOf or oneOf branch with constraints (for example {type: number, minimum: 0} beside {type: "null"}) in a property with default: null, under --field-constraints or --use-annotated. The default stays with the property and the branch's root model requires its value.

Schema (OpenAPI 3.1): weight: {anyOf: [{type: number, minimum: 0}, {type: "null"}], default: null}, with --field-constraints.

Without the option (same as 0.86.0):

class Weight(RootModel[float]):
    root: float = Field(None, ge=0.0)

With the option:

class Weight(RootModel[float]):
    root: float = Field(..., ge=0.0)

items.title: --omit-redundant-reference-null
items.text:
Option --omit-redundant-reference-null Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #5120, #5081

Affects: a field, array item, map value or union member that refers to a model whose own type already admits None (a RootModel whose root admits None, or a type: "null" model). | None is written at the use only when the target's class cannot hold null. A null item is then parsed to Name(root=None) instead of None. Type aliases, enums with a None member and plain object models are unchanged.

Command: --input-file-type openapi --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel --strict-nullable, with Name: {type: [string, "null"]} (RootModel[str | None]) used as array items.

Without the option (same as 0.86.0):

class Model(BaseModel):
    names: list[Name | None]

With the option:

class Model(BaseModel):
    names: list[Name]

items.title: --use-typed-map-values-beside-other-types
items.text:
Option --use-typed-map-values-beside-other-types Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #5094, #5127

Affects: a schema whose type array lists object together with other types than null (for example [object, string]) and has additionalProperties, under --use-typed-nullable-map-values. With both options its object member is typed as its schema says, as --use-typed-nullable-map-values already types it for [object, null]. --use-typed-nullable-map-values alone keeps the object member dict[str, Any], as in 0.86.0, and the option changes nothing without --use-typed-nullable-map-values.

Schema: tags is {"type": ["object", "string"], "additionalProperties": {"type": "integer"}}.

With --use-typed-nullable-map-values alone (same as 0.86.0):

class Model(BaseModel):
    tags: dict[str, Any] | str | None = None

With --use-typed-nullable-map-values --use-typed-map-values-beside-other-types:

class Model(BaseModel):
    tags: dict[str, int] | str | None = None

items.title: --keep-enum-member-values
items.text:
Option --keep-enum-member-values Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #5133

Affects: an enum whose class gets a value base from its schema type, an IntEnum or StrEnum (--use-specialized-enum) or a (T, Enum) (--use-subclass-enum), while that base changes a member value: 2.5 beside integer members becomes 2, and 1 in a (str, Enum) becomes '1'. With the option such an enum is a plain Enum that keeps every value as written; members the base keeps, such as 1.0 in an IntEnum, keep the base, and msgspec keeps the 0.86.0 class where it could not decode the plain Enum.

Schema: {"type": "object", "properties": {"level": {"type": "integer", "enum": [1, 2.5]}}}.

Without the option (same as 0.86.0; the member 2.5 is 2, so the model rejects 2.5 and accepts 2):

class Level(IntEnum):
    integer_1 = 1
    integer_2_5 = 2.5

With the option:

class Level(Enum):
    integer_1 = 1
    integer_2_5 = 2.5

items.title: --omit-redundant-constraints
items.text:
Option --omit-redundant-constraints Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #4525, #4875

Affects: a constraint written again beside a type that already enforces it: the bound of a zero-bound class such as NonNegativeInt (also needs --use-non-positive-negative-number-constrained-types, which no preset sets), and the length and number constraints a const or enum Literal meets by its values. It implies --filter-literal-values.

Schema: {"title": "Model", "type": "object", "properties": {"count": {"type": ["integer", "null"], "minimum": 0}, "code": {"type": "string", "const": "abc", "minLength": 1}}}. Command: --use-annotated --use-non-positive-negative-number-constrained-types.

Without the option (same as 0.86.0):

class Model(BaseModel):
    count: Annotated[NonNegativeInt | None, Field(ge=0)] = None
    code: Annotated[Literal["abc"] | None, Field(min_length=1)] = None

With the option:

class Model(BaseModel):
    count: NonNegativeInt | None = None
    code: Literal["abc"] | None = None

items.title: --openapi-paths-bodies-as-definitions
items.text:
Option --openapi-paths-bodies-as-definitions Preset 20261019 Class opt-in Release 0.87.0 Issue #5155

Affects: request and response bodies in the paths and webhooks scopes (they need --openapi-scopes paths / webhooks, which no preset sets). The body gets the model a schema definition of the same body gets: an object body with a type array such as [object, null], or with map keywords and no type, becomes a model instead of an inline type. This is separate from the crash fix for object bodies in the legacy paths scope (#5024).

Schema (abridged): the POST /pets request body is {"type": ["object", "null"], "additionalProperties": {...}}. Command: --input-file-type openapi --openapi-scopes paths --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel.

Without the option (same as 0.86.0), the body is typed inline and a document whose only bodies are such schemas fails:

Models not found in the input data; request or response bodies of the paths or webhooks scope are typed inline, and --openapi-paths-bodies-as-definitions gives them the models their schema definitions get

With the option:

class PetsPostRequest(RootModel[dict[str, Any] | None]):
    root: dict[str, Any] | None

items.title: Crash and import fixes in the default output
items.text:
These fixes apply without any option: the old result could not be generated or imported, so nothing could depend on it.

  • Map keys that reference a root model are typed by the root type instead of failing (#5017).
  • Object bodies in the paths scope of the legacy parser now get models (#5024).
  • TypedDict extra_items names the final class, so the module imports (#5022).
  • Non-finite float enum members are written importably (#4954).
  • GraphQL subclass enums are written as importable StrEnum (#4970).
  • An enum whose value base cannot construct one of its members, such as 'a' in an IntEnum or the strings of a format: byte enum in a (bytes, Enum), is written as a plain Enum instead of a class that fails at import (#4973).
  • Discriminator tags with float values, and bool values for msgspec, no longer crash generation or import; the union is written without a discriminator (#5053, #5086).
  • Schemas merged from another document resolve their $refs in their own document: "A Parser can not resolve classes" (#5046) and $ref file not found for an inherited property narrowed in another directory (#5068).
  • A $ref to an $anchor inside a oneOf branch resolves instead of failing with Unresolved $id reference (#5056, fixed by #5092).
  • A ValidationError for an allOf child and parent that both declare a property named like a schema keyword is fixed (#5069).
  • Long $ref alias chains no longer depend on the Python recursion limit; schemas nested too deeply stop with a clear error (#5076).

items.title: Migrating from fastapi-code-generator
items.text:
This guide is for projects that generate a FastAPI application with fastapi-code-generator (fcg, the fastapi-codegen command) and want to generate it with datamodel-codegen --generate-server fastapi instead. It maps each fcg option and habit to its counterpart, and lists what has no counterpart yet.

Experimental

FastAPI server generation is experimental. Its options, generated package, template values, and served OpenAPI document may change. See Experimental Features.

Both tools read one OpenAPI document and generate the models with datamodel-code-generator. fcg 0.8.1 requires datamodel-code-generator>=0.61,<0.66, so a project that generates with fcg gets the model generation of those releases; later model fixes and options reach it through datamodel-codegen only.

This page assumes the FastAPI Server Generation tutorial: it links to the tested examples there instead of repeating them.

items.title: What changes
items.text:
• Generated code and your code are separate. fcg writes a main.py whose function bodies you fill in. dcg writes a app/server/ package with the routes, the request handling, and one service Protocol (a typing.Protocol class) per group of operations. You implement the Protocols in a module of your own and pass the objects to create_app.
  • You can regenerate at any time. Every file of the package is overwritten on each run and nothing in it is meant to be edited, so there is nothing to merge when the document changes.
  • The settings live in pyproject.toml. Every option has a [tool.datamodel-codegen] key of the same name, so datamodel-codegen without arguments repeats the run.

items.title: Translate the command
items.text:
Before: fastapi-codegenAfter: datamodel-codegen 
fastapi-codegen \
  --input openapi.yaml \
  --output app \
  --generate-routers \
  --python-version 3.12

The run writes app/main.py, app/routers/<tag>.py, app/dependencies.py, and app/models.py.

datamodel-codegen \
  --input openapi.yaml \
  --input-file-type openapi \
  --openapi-scopes schemas api \
  --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel \
  --preset standard-py312-20261019 \
  --output app/models.py \
  --generate-server fastapi \
  --server-output app/server \
  --server-package app.server \
  --server-model-package app.models

The run writes app/models.py and the app/server/ package, as the tutorial shows. The same settings fit in pyproject.toml, which is also on that page.

fcg's one --output directory splits into three settings: --server-output is the directory of the package, --server-package its import path, and --server-model-package the import path of the models that --output generates. fcg imported its models with from .models; the package imports them by this absolute path.

The command also needs:

  • Python 3.11 or later, both to run datamodel-codegen and as the target of the generated code. The preset in the command targets 3.12.
  • A Pydantic v2 backend: pydantic_v2.BaseModel, or pydantic_v2.dataclass with --use-missing-sentinel and --target-pydantic-version 2.14.
  • The api scope: --openapi-scopes schemas api, so that the models cover the parameters, bodies, and responses of the operations.

Requirements lists all of them. The dcg command line has no short options such as -i and -o.

items.title: Option mapping
items.text:
fcg dcg Notes -i, --input --input with --input-file-type openapi One document; a directory or a list of files is refused. -o, --output --server-output and --server-package Both are required with --generate-server. -m, --model-file --output and --server-model-package --output is a file or a directory. A document with references between modules needs a directory. -r, --generate-routers --server-layout routers, the default One router module per group. fcg's default, a single main.py, corresponds to --server-layout single: one routes.py and one Service Protocol. -t, --template-dir --custom-template-dir, templates in its fastapi/ directory Roles differ from fcg's files; see Custom templates and visitors. --model-template-dir --custom-template-dir, templates in its pydantic_v2/ directory The model templates are datamodel-code-generator's own. -c, --custom-visitor none --extra-template-data passes static values to templates. --specify-tags none Include the router of one group in your own app, or filter paths with --openapi-include-paths. -d, --output-model-type --output-model-type Only pydantic_v2.BaseModel and pydantic_v2.dataclass, which needs --use-missing-sentinel and --target-pydantic-version 2.14. -p, --python-version (default 3.10) --target-python-version, or a preset that sets it 3.11 or later. --include-request-argument --server-include-request For the raw body, use --server-body-mode request, or --server-body-modes per operation. -e, --encoding, --enum-field-as-literal, --strict-nullable, --use-annotated, --reuse-model, --enable-faux-immutability, --disable-timestamp, --allow-remote-refs, --allow-private-network the same options Every model option of dcg applies to the server's models.

Options that dcg adds are described in Server options. The server target also brings --check, --watch, --diff-against, batch jobs, the generate() function, and, from the same document, a Python client.

items.title: Move your handlers
items.text:
In fcg, the generated main.py holds a function for each operation, and you replace its pass with your logic. For the tutorial's getPet, fcg 0.8.1 generates this main.py, shown without its other operations; the HTTPException import, PETS, and the body of get_pet are yours:

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Union

from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Path

from .models import Error, Pet

app = FastAPI(
    title='Pets',
    version='1.0',
    servers=[{'url': 'http://localhost:8000'}],
)

PETS: dict[int, Pet] = {}


@app.get(
    '/pets/{petId}',
    response_model=Pet,
    responses={'404': {'model': Error}},
    tags=['pets'],
)
def get_pet(pet_id: int = Path(..., alias='petId')) -> Union[Pet, Error]:
    if (pet := PETS.get(pet_id)) is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f'Pet {pet_id} not found')
    return pet

In dcg, the same logic is the method PetStore.get_pet of a class in your own module, which the quick start shows next to list_pets and create_pet. Moving a function takes these steps:

  • Collect the methods in a class. Subclass the Protocol of the group, PetsService for the pets tag, and pass an object of it to create_app(pets=...). The decorator, the path, response_model, and tags are generated.
  • Keep the names. A method is named after its operationId in snake case, as fcg names a function. See How methods and arguments are named.
  • Drop the FastAPI defaults. A method takes the parameters and the body as keyword arguments, already validated by the models, so Path(...), Query(...), and Depends(...) disappear from the signature. The arguments follow the naming of model fields: the quick start's preset turns on snake case, and without it you pass --snake-case-field.
  • Return the primary response, or an HTTPResult. A bare return value is the model of the primary response. For another declared status, such as the 404 above, return an HTTPResult, which the package validates with the response's model; see Return values and HTTPResult.
  • Keep HTTPException for undocumented errors. It answers FastAPI's {"detail": ...} body, as in fcg; see Raise errors.
  • Choose the handler mode in the settings. fcg users turn a function into a coroutine function by editing it. In dcg, --server-handler-mode async or --server-handler-modes makes the method a coroutine function; see Async methods.

The method's docstring is Handle GET /pets/{petId}. by default, where fcg used the operation's summary. --use-schema-description writes the summary and description of the operation instead.

items.title: Dependencies, security, uploads, and raw requests
Per-request dependencies
items.text:
fcg handlers declare what they need in their signature, such as db: Session = Depends(get_db). A generated method has a fixed signature, and the values that the dependencies and operation_dependencies of create_app and build_router return never reach it.

Pass long-lived objects, such as a database client, to the constructor of your service class. For a value of the request, generate with --server-include-request and let a dependency put it in request.state; the how-to shows both. Dependencies still run before the method, so they fit checks and side effects such as auditing.

items.title: Security
items.text: fcg projects secure operations in their templates, with a Depends in each function. In dcg, the document describes the security: declare securitySchemes and security in it, and the package gets a security.py with one FastAPI dependency for each scheme. create_app then takes an authorize(requirement_sets, credentials) callback, and what it returns reaches the method as the keyword principal. Authenticate requests walks through it with a bearer token.

items.title: Uploads
items.text: fcg passes a file part of a multipart/form-data body as an UploadFile. In dcg, the part arrives as bytes in the body model, so the file name and the content type are lost; see Accept uploads. When you need them, generate the operation with --server-body-modes set to request (or --server-body-mode request for every operation) and read the form from the raw request.

items.title: The raw request
items.text: --include-request-argument of fcg corresponds to --server-include-request: every method receives the Starlette request as the keyword request. To receive the request instead of a validated body, use --server-body-mode request or --server-body-modes, whose keys are operation references; see Per-operation settings.

items.title: Custom templates and visitors
items.text:
dcg's model templates are the same mechanism that --model-template-dir of fcg used, so a template that overrides a model usually carries over: put it in pydantic_v2/ of the directory that --custom-template-dir names, and compare it with the current builtin template. Model templates must keep the class and field names, because the server binds each operation to them.

The server templates cannot be ported one to one. fcg renders one template with a list of operations. dcg renders a fixed set of roles, each a file of the fastapi/ directory of the template directory, with the values of that role:

Role Generates application.jinja2 application.py: create_app, build_router router.jinja2 the routes module, or each router module services.jinja2 services.py: the service Protocols security.jinja2 security.py contract.jinja2 _generated/contract.py facade.jinja2 the package initializers openapi.jinja2 _generated/openapi.py readme.jinja2 README.md

A role the directory does not hold keeps its builtin template. A file in fastapi/ that is not a role is ignored without a message, so check the file name when an override has no effect. The values of every role, which can change while the target is experimental, are in Templates.

Most reasons to customize an fcg template have a built-in answer: security is generated from the document, async is a setting, and the request is an option. For the rest, rewrite the override from the builtin template of the role.

fcg's custom visitors compute extra variables for the templates from the parsed document. dcg has no visitors. --extra-template-data passes static values to every role under the #all# key, so a script of your own can compute them and write the JSON file before the run.

items.title: Migrate incrementally
items.text:
You do not have to move an application at once. Generate the package beside the old code, with another --server-output and --server-package than any module that you already have, and include the router of a group in your existing FastAPI application. With the default routers layout, each router module app/server/routers/<group>.py has its own build_router, which takes the service of that group only, so you move one group at a time. The old routes keep working. fcg wrote models.py into its --output directory too: if that is app, point --output and --server-model-package at another module so that the two models do not overwrite each other.

Use your own FastAPI app shows build_router in an application of your own. Three things apply while old and new routes share an application:

  • Registration order decides. FastAPI uses the first route that matches a request, so remove the old function of an operation, or register the new router first, when the router takes it over.
  • Leave serve_source_openapi for the end. It makes /openapi.json serve the generated document, which lists every generated path and none of the old routes. Until the old routes are gone, FastAPI's own document describes both.
  • Register validation_error_handler last. It applies to the whole application, so it also changes the 422 bodies of the old routes.

To generate only the operations that you moved, pass --openapi-include-paths; see Server options.

items.title: Regenerate in CI
items.text:
Run the generation command again whenever the document changes. The Protocols change with the operations, and type checkers point at the implementations to update.

  • Check in CI. --check renders everything without writing it and exits with 0 when nothing would change, 1 when a file would change, and 2 for an error. A run without a timestamp, which --disable-timestamp or a preset gives you, reproduces every byte; see Check in CI.
  • Delete stale router modules. Generation overwrites every generated file but does not delete one. After you remove a tag from the document, its app/server/routers/<group>.py stays, and --check lists it as no longer generated. Delete it by hand.
  • Keep your code outside the package, in the app/services modules that app/server/main.py imports, which generation writes once with stubs. --check also reports any other .py file under --server-output.
  • Watch the document. --watch regenerates on every change of the input and needs the watch extra, datamodel-code-generator[watch]; see Compare and watch.

items.title: Behaviour differences
items.text:
• Nothing generated is editable. Every file under --server-output is overwritten, so your code lives outside the package.
  • Methods are keyword-only and return the primary response model, an HTTPResult, or a Starlette Response.
  • Operations are grouped by their first tag. An operation without a tag goes to the default group, which makes DefaultService and the default= argument of create_app. fcg's modular output dropped such operations.
  • There is no GET / route. fcg's modular main.py added a "Gateway of the App" route; the package serves only the paths of the document.
  • /openapi.json serves your document, not the one FastAPI derives from the routes. create_app(..., source_openapi=False) serves FastAPI's again. See Served OpenAPI document.
  • 422 bodies omit input and ctx, so the response does not return the rejected value; see Production settings.
  • Literal paths come before templated paths, so /pets/me is registered before /pets/{petId}. fcg sorted the routes by path.
  • The models file has more names. A schema written inline takes a derived name such as PetsGetResponse, and parameters get type aliases. Declare schemas under components to name them yourself, as the tutorial does.
  • Generation is stricter. A path placeholder without a declared path parameter stops the run, where fcg ignored it. A path parameter that names no placeholder of its operation's path is refused with an error instead of being generated, and every other path parameter is required even when the document leaves out required or declares it false.
  • Modular references need a directory. When the document references schemas in other modules, --output must name a directory, not a file.

items.title: Not available yet
items.text:
• Tag filtering (--specify-tags). Include the router of a group in your own app with its build_router, or leave paths out with --openapi-include-paths. create_app takes every group.
  • Custom visitors (--custom-visitor). Pass static values with --extra-template-data.
  • UploadFile. A file part is bytes. Use --server-body-mode request or --server-body-modes and read the form yourself.
  • Python 3.10 targets. A target below 3.11, and running datamodel-codegen on 3.10, are refused. Keep fcg for such a project until it moves to 3.11.
  • Backends other than Pydantic v2. fcg also accepts dataclasses.dataclass, typing.TypedDict, and msgspec.Struct; the server target does not, and has no workaround.

items.title: FastAPI Server Generation
items.text:
TLS is configured by the server or reverse proxy that hosts the generated application. Update its trust store when it verifies client certificates, and update any outbound HTTP clients used by your service or authentication callbacks. Generating a server from a remote schema also uses the generator's TLS certificate settings. Generated routers do not maintain a CA bundle.

Experimental

FastAPI server generation is experimental. Its options, generated package, template values, and served OpenAPI document may change. See Experimental Features.

--generate-server fastapi turns one OpenAPI document into the models and a FastAPI server package in the same run. The package holds everything the document decides: the routes, a service Protocol that lists the operations you implement, the code that reads requests and writes responses, authentication, and the OpenAPI document the server publishes.

You write only the business logic, in the services modules beside the package, which the generator writes once with stubs and never overwrites. Type checkers and Python check that your code implements every operation, so when the document changes, you regenerate the package and fix what they report.

openapi.yaml ──► datamodel-codegen ──► app/models.py, app/server/    generated, overwritten on every run
                         │                  ▲  app/server/main.py imports app/services/
                         │ once, with stubs │ import, subclass the service Protocols
                         └─────────────► app/services/               yours, never overwritten

Coming from fastapi-code-generator? See Migrating from fastapi-code-generator.

This page covers a tutorial, how-tos for implementing the services, and the reference of the generated package. For the client of the same document, see Python Client Generation; for every option with examples, see CLI Reference: Target Generation Options.

items.title: Quick start
items.text: This tutorial builds a small pet store that lists, creates, and finds pets. Start in an empty directory of a uv project, with datamodel-codegen installed. Server generation needs Python 3.11 or later; the preset below targets Python 3.12.

items.title: 1. Describe the API
items.text:
Save the document as openapi.yaml:

openapi.yaml 
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Pets
  version: "1.0"
servers:
  - url: http://localhost:8000
paths:
  /pets:
    get:
      operationId: listPets
      tags: [pets]
      parameters:
        - name: limit
          in: query
          schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 100, default: 20}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The pets.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Pets"}
    post:
      operationId: createPet
      tags: [pets]
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/NewPet"}
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Created.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Pet"}
  /pets/{petId}:
    get:
      operationId: getPet
      tags: [pets]
      parameters:
        - name: petId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema: {type: integer}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The pet.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Pet"}
        "404":
          description: No pet has this ID.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Error"}
components:
  schemas:
    NewPet:
      type: object
      required: [name]
      properties:
        name: {type: string}
        tag: {type: string}
    Pet:
      type: object
      required: [id, name]
      properties:
        id: {type: integer}
        name: {type: string}
        tag: {type: string}
    Pets:
      type: array
      items: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Pet"}
    Error:
      type: object
      required: [message]
      properties:
        message: {type: string}

Each operation has an operationId, which names the Python method that implements it, and a tag. Operations that share their first tag form a router group: here the three pets operations, which the server registers on one FastAPI router.

The bodies and responses refer to schemas under components, so their models take the names you chose, such as Pet and NewPet.

items.title: 2. Generate the server
items.text:
Everything goes into one application package, app. Create it with an empty app/__init__.py, which makes app a package; keeping the generated packages inside your application package, instead of as top-level packages such as models or server, avoids generic top-level names that collide easily with other projects and libraries, and shows at a glance what is generated and what is yours:

mkdir -p app && touch app/__init__.py

Put the settings in pyproject.toml and run datamodel-codegen without arguments, or pass them as options:

pyproject.tomlCommand line 

[tool.datamodel-codegen]
input = "openapi.yaml"
input-file-type = "openapi"
openapi-scopes = ["schemas", "api"]
output-model-type = "pydantic_v2.BaseModel"
preset = "standard-py312-20261019"
output = "app/models.py"
generate-server = "fastapi"
server-output = "app/server"
server-package = "app.server"
server-model-package = "app.models"


datamodel-codegen \
  --input openapi.yaml \
  --input-file-type openapi \
  --openapi-scopes schemas api \
  --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel \
  --preset standard-py312-20261019 \
  --output app/models.py \
  --generate-server fastapi \
  --server-output app/server \
  --server-package app.server \
  --server-model-package app.models

The preset supplies the model options, as in the model quick start, and --openapi-scopes schemas api makes models for the parameters, bodies, and responses of the operations too.

Generation ends by printing the command that adds the package's runtime dependencies to your project, and the next steps:

Add the runtime dependencies of app.server to your project:
  uv add "fastapi>=0.141.1" "pydantic>=2.14.0" "typing-extensions>=4.16"
Next steps: implement the stubs in app/services/pets.py, then run the server:
  uv add uvicorn && uv run uvicorn app.server.main:app --reload
or: uv add "fastapi[standard]" && uv run fastapi dev --entrypoint app.server.main:app
See app/server/README.md.

Run the uv add command. It names only the minimum version of each package, so uv adds the latest release, and it grows with what the document uses: python-multipart for forms, email-validator for format: email, and python-ulid for format: ulid. An explicit --target-pydantic-version older than the pydantic minimum (2, 2.11 or 2.12) is refused with Error: and exit code 2; leave it unset or use 2.14, which --use-missing-sentinel requires (see Requirements).

The run wrote the models, the app.server package, and, once, the app.services package with a stub for you to implement:

app/
├── __init__.py
├── models.py
├── server/
│   ├── README.md
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── _generated/
│   ├── _runtime/
│   ├── application.py
│   ├── main.py
│   ├── py.typed
│   ├── routers/
│   │   ├── __init__.py
│   │   └── pets.py
│   └── services.py
└── services/
    ├── __init__.py
    └── pets.py

app/models.py holds the models, app/server/services.py the service Protocol you implement next, app/server/routers/ the routes, and app/server/main.py the application. The rest is described in The generated package. Every file of app/models.py and app/server/ is overwritten on each run, so keep your own code outside app/server/: generation writes app/services/pets.py only while it is missing, and never overwrites or deletes it.

items.title: 3. Read the service Protocol
items.text:
app/server/services.py declares one service Protocol for each router group: a typing.Protocol class with an abstract method for each operation.

"""Service interfaces of this package's router groups; regenerate them instead of editing."""

from __future__ import annotations

from abc import abstractmethod
from typing import Protocol

from app import models
from fastapi.responses import Response

from ._runtime.server.responses import HTTPResult


class PetsService(Protocol):
    """Implement the pets operations: subclass this Protocol, or give an object its methods."""

    @abstractmethod
    def list_pets(
        self,
        *,
        limit: int,
    ) -> models.Pets | HTTPResult[models.Pets] | Response:
        """
        Handle GET /pets.
        """

    @abstractmethod
    def create_pet(
        self,
        *,
        body: models.NewPet,
    ) -> models.Pet | HTTPResult[models.Pet] | Response:
        """
        Handle POST /pets.
        """

    @abstractmethod
    def get_pet(
        self,
        *,
        pet_id: int,
    ) -> models.Pet | HTTPResult[models.Pet | models.Error] | Response:
        """
        Handle GET /pets/{petId}.
        """

Each method takes the operation's parameters and body as keyword arguments, already validated by the models. limit arrives as 20 when the request omits it, the default its schema declares, and the petId path parameter arrives as pet_id, since the preset turns on snake-case field names.

A method returns one of three things:

  • the model of its primary response, the response a bare return value takes: 200 when the operation declares it, or else its lowest success status, such as 201 for create_pet, or else its 2XX or default response (see Responses for the full rule);
  • an HTTPResult for another status or extra headers, such as the 404 that get_pet declares;
  • a Starlette Response, sent as it is.

items.title: 4. Implement the operations
items.text:
Generation wrote app/services/pets.py with a class Pets that subclasses PetsService and a stub for each method, which raises NotImplementedError. Replace the stubs with the business logic:

from app import models
from app.server import HTTPResult
from app.server.services import PetsService


class Pets(PetsService):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.pets: dict[int, models.Pet] = {}

    def list_pets(self, *, limit: int) -> models.Pets:
        return models.Pets(list(self.pets.values())[:limit])

    def create_pet(self, *, body: models.NewPet) -> models.Pet:
        pet = models.Pet(id=len(self.pets) + 1, name=body.name, tag=body.tag)
        self.pets[pet.id] = pet
        return pet

    def get_pet(self, *, pet_id: int) -> models.Pet | HTTPResult[models.Error]:
        if (pet := self.pets.get(pet_id)) is None:
            return HTTPResult(404, models.Error(message=f"Pet {pet_id} not found"))
        return pet

Pets subclasses PetsService, so type checkers report a missing method or one whose arguments or result do not match its operation, and Python refuses to create Pets() while a method is missing. HTTPResult(404, models.Error(...)) sends the 404 response that get_pet declares, validated by its Error model.

Each router group has its module in app/services, named after the group's router module, with a class named after its Protocol without the Service suffix; a document with security schemes adds app/services/authorize.py with the authorize function. The package README lists them under Next steps. app/server/main.py imports them and calls create_app, which takes one service for each router group, under the group's name, and returns a FastAPI application. In short, it does this:

from app.server import create_app
from app.services.pets import Pets

app = create_app(pets=Pets())

items.title: 5. Run it
items.text:
uv add uvicorn
uv run uvicorn app.server.main:app --reload

Run it from the directory that holds the top-level package, app; for a src layout, add --app-dir src, which the next steps printed after generation add for you. FastAPI's own command runs it too, after uv add "fastapi[standard]". For a nested package such as app.server, it takes the import string: uv run fastapi dev --entrypoint app.server.main:app, which the next steps printed too, with uv run --directory src for a src layout.

A missing app.services module or class stops the start with an ImportError that names the file to write where it belongs, a package's __init__.py for a group you implement as a package; an import error inside your module, such as a missing dependency, is raised as it is. A method whose signature cannot take the keyword arguments of its operation stops the start with a TypeError that names the class, the method, and the argument; the check reads the method's own signature, not that of a function a decorator wraps, and leaves its annotations unevaluated.

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs. The page shows your openapi.yaml, not a document FastAPI derives from the routes: the application serves the parts of the source document its operations use, the served document, at /openapi.json.

items.title: 6. Test it
items.text:
FastAPI's TestClient calls the application without a server:

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app.server.main import app

client = TestClient(app)


def test_create_and_get_pet() -> None:
    created = client.post("/pets", json={"name": "Mimi", "tag": "cat"})
    assert created.status_code == 201
    assert client.get(f"/pets/{created.json()['id']}").json() == created.json()


def test_missing_pet() -> None:
    response = client.get("/pets/99")
    assert response.status_code == 404
    assert response.json() == {"message": "Pet 99 not found"}

uv add --dev pytest httpx2
uv run pytest test_app.py

items.title: Recap
items.text:
• The OpenAPI document is the source: the models, the routes, and the service Protocols come from it.
  • datamodel-codegen regenerates every file of app/models.py and app/server/ on each run.
  • Your code lives in app/services/, outside the generated package, and subclasses the service Protocols, so type checkers keep it in step with the document; generation writes a missing module once, with stubs.
  • app/server/main.py builds the application from your services with create_app, which tests and applications of your own can call with other instances.
  • To call the server from Python, generate a client from the same document; see the overview and Python Client Generation.

items.title: Implement the services
items.text:
The how-tos below build on a second project, a photo service, whose upload needs a bearer token:

openapi.yaml 
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Pet photos
  version: "1.0"
paths:
  /pets/{petId}/photo:
    put:
      operationId: uploadPhoto
      tags: [photos]
      security:
        - bearer: []
      parameters:
        - name: petId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema: {type: integer}
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          multipart/form-data:
            schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/PhotoUpload"}
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Stored.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Photo"}
    get:
      operationId: getPhoto
      tags: [photos]
      parameters:
        - name: petId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema: {type: integer}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The photo.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Photo"}
components:
  securitySchemes:
    bearer:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer
  schemas:
    PhotoUpload:
      type: object
      required: [file]
      properties:
        file: {type: string, format: binary}
        caption: {type: string}
    Photo:
      type: object
      required: [petId, size, owner]
      properties:
        petId: {type: integer}
        size: {type: integer}
        owner: {type: string}
        caption: {type: string}

It adds two settings to the quick start's table, explained in Async methods and The request and per-request dependencies:

[tool.datamodel-codegen]
server-include-request = true
server-handler-modes = '{"/paths/~1pets~1{petId}~1photo/put": "async"}'

Its service Protocol takes the request, the authenticated principal, and an async upload:

"""Service interfaces of this package's router groups; regenerate them instead of editing."""

from __future__ import annotations

from abc import abstractmethod
from typing import Protocol

from app import models
from fastapi import Request
from fastapi.responses import Response
from typing_extensions import TypeVar

from ._runtime.server.responses import HTTPResult

PrincipalT_contra = TypeVar("PrincipalT_contra", contravariant=True)


class PhotosService(Protocol[PrincipalT_contra]):
    """Implement the photos operations: subclass this Protocol, or give an object its methods."""

    @abstractmethod
    async def upload_photo(
        self,
        *,
        request: Request,
        principal: PrincipalT_contra,
        pet_id: int,
        body: models.PhotoUpload,
    ) -> models.Photo | HTTPResult[models.Photo] | Response:
        """
        Handle PUT /pets/{petId}/photo.
        """

    @abstractmethod
    def get_photo(
        self,
        *,
        request: Request,
        pet_id: int,
    ) -> models.Photo | HTTPResult[models.Photo] | Response:
        """
        Handle GET /pets/{petId}/photo.
        """

items.title: How methods and arguments are named
items.text:
Methods and router modules are named in snake case, and Protocols in PascalCase, whatever the model naming options say: a method after its operationId, or after its method and path without one, such as get_pets_by_pet_id.

A method's arguments are named after their wire names as model fields are, so the quick start's preset, which turns on --snake-case-field for Pydantic models, names the petId path parameter pet_id. Without the preset, pass --snake-case-field explicitly for snake_case arguments, or the argument keeps the wire name, petId. --aliases and the special-field prefix options apply to arguments too.

A derived name that its namespace already holds takes the model's suffix, such as id_1 for a query id beside a path id, body_1 for a parameter named body, or pets_1 for a second tag that also becomes pets. The model's --naming-strategy rules apply to these names too, with the router group as the parent of a method and the method as the parent of an argument.

An explicit name of --server-operation-names, --server-router-names, or --server-parameter-names must be new and is never renamed.

A schema written inline, rather than under components, takes a model name derived from where it is: its path, its method, and its location. The path's words are joined in PascalCase without its separators, so /pets/{petId} gives PetsPetId, the root path / gives Root, and only a path that starts with a digit, such as /2fa, is prefixed with Field to stay a valid name. The tutorial's inline parameter schemas become these type aliases in app/models.py:

type PetsGetQueryLimitParameter = Annotated[int, Field(ge=1, le=100)]


type PetsPetIdGetPathPetIdParameter = int

An inline response schema of GET /pets would likewise become PetsGetResponse. The method arguments keep their own names, limit and pet_id, but a body or response model is a class you import.
