items.title: Module Structure and Exports
items.text: When generating models to a directory structure, datamodel-code-generator can automatically create __init__.py files with __all__ exports. This page explains how to control this behavior.

items.title: Quick Overview
items.text: Option Description --all-exports-scope Control which modules get __all__ exports --all-exports-collision-strategy Handle name collisions in recursive exports --treat-dot-as-module Convert dots in names to nested modules --strict-dotted-module-names Restrict automatic dotted-name inference to canonical Python identifiers

items.title: --all-exports-scope
items.text:
Controls the scope of __all__ generation in __init__.py files.

Value Description none No __all__ generation (default) local Export only the module's own definitions recursive Export all definitions from child modules

items.title: Example: none (default)
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input schemas/ --output models/

# models/__init__.py
# (empty or minimal imports)

items.title: Example: local
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input schemas/ --output models/ --all-exports-scope children

# models/__init__.py
from .user import User
from .order import Order

__all__ = ["User", "Order"]

items.title: Example: recursive
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input schemas/ --output models/ --all-exports-scope recursive

# models/__init__.py
from .user import User
from .order import Order
from .common.status import Status
from .common.types import ID, Timestamp

__all__ = ["User", "Order", "Status", "ID", "Timestamp"]

items.title: --all-exports-collision-strategy
items.text:
When using --all-exports-scope recursive, name collisions can occur if multiple modules define the same class name. This option controls how to handle them.

Value Description minimal-prefix Add minimum module path prefix to disambiguate full-prefix Use complete module path for all exports

items.title: The Problem
items.text:
models/
├── user/
│   └── types.py      # defines `ID`
└── order/
    └── types.py      # also defines `ID`

Both modules define ID, causing a collision when exporting recursively.

items.title: Solution: minimal-prefix
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input schemas/ --output models/ \
  --all-exports-scope recursive \
  --all-exports-collision-strategy minimal-prefix

# models/__init__.py
from .user.types import ID as user_ID
from .order.types import ID as order_ID

__all__ = ["user_ID", "order_ID"]

Only colliding names get prefixed.

items.title: Solution: full-prefix
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input schemas/ --output models/ \
  --all-exports-scope recursive \
  --all-exports-collision-strategy full-prefix

# models/__init__.py
from .user.types import ID as user_types_ID
from .order.types import ID as order_types_ID

__all__ = ["user_types_ID", "order_types_ID"]

All names use the full module path prefix.

items.title: --treat-dot-as-module
items.text: Converts dots in schema names to nested module directories.

items.title: Without --treat-dot-as-module
items.text:
Schema with title: "api.v1.User" generates:

# models.py
class ApiV1User(BaseModel): ...

items.title: With --treat-dot-as-module
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output models/ --treat-dot-as-module

Schema with title: "api.v1.User" generates:

models/
├── __init__.py
└── api/
    ├── __init__.py
    └── v1/
        ├── __init__.py
        └── user.py      # contains class User

This is useful for:

  • Organizing large schemas by namespace
  • Mirroring API versioning structure
  • Keeping related models together

When writing plain Python text to stdout with the standard renderer and without an explicit --treat-dot-as-module setting, historical automatic module inference is preserved whenever the final concatenated result remains usable. A retry coalesces the stdout models into one flat namespace only when a non-canonical inferred module boundary leaves conflicting generated definitions, repeats a future import after generated code, hides a generated model with a later import, or emits a relative import that cannot resolve in standalone stdout. Existing root and canonical model names are reserved first. Directory output, JSON output, schema runtime validator or generic-base generation, custom rendering, and the Python API retain their existing default inference. Use directory or JSON output when module paths must be preserved.

items.title: --strict-dotted-module-names
items.text:
By default, automatic inference retains the historical behavior of treating dots as module separators. Enable --strict-dotted-module-names to infer a module path only when every raw segment, including the model name, is a canonical Python identifier. Hard keywords, numeric or empty segments, punctuation, and names that change under NFKC normalization fall back to a flat model name.

datamodel-codegen \
  --input schema.json \
  --output models.py \
  --strict-dotted-module-names

This option affects automatic inference only. Explicit --treat-dot-as-module or --no-treat-dot-as-module takes precedence. The negative form, --no-strict-dotted-module-names, can disable a value enabled in pyproject.toml; it does not disable the narrow unusable-stdout repair described above. Use explicit --treat-dot-as-module when module boundaries must be kept.

items.title: Pattern 1: Flat directory output with child exports
items.text:
Best for small to medium projects with a single generated package or simple directory structure.

datamodel-codegen --input schema.yaml --output models/ --all-exports-scope children

items.title: Pattern 2: Hierarchical with recursive exports
items.text:
Best for large projects with many schemas organized by domain.

datamodel-codegen --input schemas/ --output models/ \
  --all-exports-scope recursive \
  --all-exports-collision-strategy minimal-prefix \
  --treat-dot-as-module

items.title: Pattern 3: OpenAPI with module structure
items.text:
Best for OpenAPI schemas with versioned endpoints.

datamodel-codegen --input openapi.yaml --output models/ \
  --treat-dot-as-module \
  --all-exports-scope recursive

items.title: Import errors after generation
items.text:
If you see ImportError: cannot import name 'X':

  1. Check if __all__ is generated correctly
  2. Verify the module structure matches your imports
  3. Try --all-exports-scope children first, then recursive

items.title: Name collisions
items.text:
If you see duplicate class names:

  1. Use --all-exports-collision-strategy minimal-prefix
  2. Or use --all-exports-collision-strategy full-prefix for maximum clarity
  3. Consider restructuring your schemas to avoid collisions

items.title: Circular imports
items.text:
If you encounter circular import errors:

  1. Check the generated __init__.py files
  2. Consider using --all-exports-scope children instead of recursive
  3. Use lazy imports in your application code

items.title: One-liner Usage
items.text:
This guide covers how to use datamodel-code-generator with pipes and clipboard tools for quick, one-time code generation without permanent installation.

Note

The package name is datamodel-code-generator, and the CLI command is datamodel-codegen. Because the names differ, pass the package explicitly with uvx --from or pipx run --spec.

items.title: One-liner Execution with uvx/pipx
items.text: You don't need to install datamodel-code-generator permanently. Use uvx or pipx run to execute it directly.

items.title: Using uvx (Recommended)
items.text:
uvx runs Python tools without installation:

# Basic usage
uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output model.py

# With extras (e.g., HTTP support)
uvx --from 'datamodel-code-generator[http]' datamodel-codegen --url https://example.com/api.yaml --output model.py

# With GraphQL support
uvx --from 'datamodel-code-generator[graphql]' datamodel-codegen --input schema.graphql --output model.py

items.title: Using pipx run
items.text:
pipx also supports one-shot execution:

pipx run --spec datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output model.py

items.title: Reading from stdin
items.text:
datamodel-code-generator can read schema input from stdin, enabling powerful pipeline workflows:

# Pipe JSON directly
echo '{"type": "object", "properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}}}' | \
  uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input-file-type jsonschema

# Pipe from another command
curl -s https://example.com/schema.json | \
  uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input-file-type jsonschema --output model.py

items.title: Clipboard Integration
items.text: Combine stdin support with clipboard tools to quickly generate models from copied schema definitions.

items.title: macOS (pbpaste/pbcopy)
items.text:
# Generate from clipboard and print to stdout
pbpaste | uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input-file-type jsonschema

# Generate from clipboard and save to file
pbpaste | uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input-file-type jsonschema --output model.py

# Generate from clipboard and copy result back to clipboard
pbpaste | uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input-file-type jsonschema | pbcopy

items.title: Linux (xclip/xsel)
items.text:
xclipxsel 
# Generate from clipboard and print to stdout
xclip -selection clipboard -o | uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input-file-type jsonschema

# Generate and copy result to clipboard
xclip -selection clipboard -o | uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input-file-type jsonschema | xclip -selection clipboard

# Generate from clipboard and print to stdout
xsel --clipboard --output | uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input-file-type jsonschema

# Generate and copy result to clipboard
xsel --clipboard --output | uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input-file-type jsonschema | xsel --clipboard --input

Installing clipboard tools on Linux

# Debian/Ubuntu
sudo apt install xclip
# or
sudo apt install xsel

# Fedora
sudo dnf install xclip
# or
sudo dnf install xsel

items.title: Windows (clip/PowerShell)
items.text:
PowerShellCommand Prompt 
# Generate from clipboard and print to stdout
Get-Clipboard | uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input-file-type jsonschema

# Generate and copy result to clipboard
Get-Clipboard | uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input-file-type jsonschema | Set-Clipboard

REM Windows Command Prompt doesn't have a built-in paste command
REM Use PowerShell from cmd:
powershell -command "Get-Clipboard" | uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input-file-type jsonschema

Windows clip command

The clip command on Windows only supports copying to the clipboard, not reading from it. Use PowerShell's Get-Clipboard and Set-Clipboard for full clipboard integration.

items.title: Quick model generation workflow
items.text:
1. Copy a JSON Schema from documentation or an API response
  2. Run the generator from clipboard:
# macOS
pbpaste | uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input-file-type jsonschema --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel

# Linux
xclip -selection clipboard -o | uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input-file-type jsonschema --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel

# Windows PowerShell
Get-Clipboard | uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input-file-type jsonschema --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel

items.title: Generating from API documentation
items.text:
# Fetch OpenAPI spec and generate models
curl -s https://petstore3.swagger.io/api/v3/openapi.json | \
  uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input-file-type openapi --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel --output petstore.py

items.title: Generating from GitHub raw URLs
items.text:
You can directly fetch schemas from GitHub repositories using raw URLs:

# Fetch JSON Schema from GitHub and generate models
curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OAI/OpenAPI-Specification/main/schemas/v3.0/schema.json | \
  uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input-file-type jsonschema --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel

# Fetch OpenAPI spec from a GitHub repository
curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/rest-api-description/main/descriptions/api.github.com/api.github.com.json | \
  uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input-file-type openapi --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel --output github_api.py

Using the --url option

If you have the http extra installed, you can use --url directly without curl:

uvx --from 'datamodel-code-generator[http]' datamodel-codegen \
  --url https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OAI/OpenAPI-Specification/main/schemas/v3.0/schema.json \
  --input-file-type jsonschema \
  --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel

items.title: Using with jq for JSON manipulation
items.text:
# Extract a specific schema definition and generate a model
cat openapi.yaml | yq '.components.schemas.User' | \
  uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen --input-file-type jsonschema

items.title: Comparison: Installation Methods
items.text:
Method Command Use Case uvx uvx --from datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen One-liner usage, no installation pipx run pipx run --spec datamodel-code-generator datamodel-codegen One-liner usage, alternative to uvx uv tool install uv tool install datamodel-code-generator Standalone CLI installation pipx install pipx install datamodel-code-generator Global installation, frequent usage uv add --dev uv add --dev datamodel-code-generator Pinned project/CI dependency pip install pip install datamodel-code-generator Traditional installation

When to use each method

  • uvx/pipx run: Quick one-liner generation, testing different versions
  • uv tool install/pipx install: Frequent CLI usage across multiple projects
  • uv add --dev/pip install: Project dependency, CI/CD pipelines, programmatic usage

items.title: OpenAPI Options
items.text:
When working with OpenAPI specifications, datamodel-code-generator provides several options to control how schemas, operations, and special properties are handled. This page explains when and how to use each option.

This page is a task-oriented guide for OpenAPI-specific generation behavior. For input format basics, see Generate from OpenAPI. For every flag, choice, and generated example, see CLI Reference: OpenAPI-only Options.

items.title: Quick Overview
items.text: Option Description --openapi-scopes Select which parts of the spec to generate models from --include-path-parameters Include path parameters in generated models --use-operation-id-as-name Name models using operation IDs --read-only-write-only-model-type Generate separate models for request/response contexts --validation Enable OpenAPI validation constraints (deprecated)

items.title: --openapi-scopes
items.text:
Controls which sections of the OpenAPI specification to generate models from.

Scope Description schemas Generate from #/components/schemas (default) api Generate schema declarations throughout the API, including typed components, parameters, headers, callbacks, and webhooks parameters Include parameter models for operations selected by paths or webhooks paths Generate models from path operation request bodies and responses webhooks Generate models from webhook operation request bodies and responses

items.title: Default behavior (schemas only)
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input openapi.yaml --output models.py

Generates models only from #/components/schemas.

items.title: Generate all API declarations
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input openapi.yaml --output models.py --openapi-scopes api

The api scope collects component schemas, typed parameter/request-body/response/header components, root paths, webhooks, reusable Path Items, and callbacks. It includes all request and response media, response headers, and applicable multipart encoding headers. OpenAPI version rules determine which declarations apply. Repeated references share one declaration's generated models, and callback cycles terminate without expanding models indefinitely.

Parameters generate individual schema types, including path parameters regardless of --include-path-parameters. The legacy aggregate parameter wrapper is specific to the parameters scope without api.

Parameter schemas (path, query, header, and cookie parameters) that would be emitted as root models are emitted exactly as --use-type-alias emits them, for every output model type and option combination: type LimitParameter = Annotated[int, Field(ge=1, le=100)] on Python 3.12+ and TypeAliasType below 3.12. Object parameters stay models. Anything that references a parameter schema, including another schema, references its alias. An alias has no default value, so the model no longer applies a parameter schema's scalar default. Component schemas, response headers, and the other scopes keep their usual models.

Changed in 0.84.0

With --openapi-scopes api, parameter schemas that 0.83.0 generated as root models, such as a Pydantic RootModel, are now type aliases, as --use-type-alias emits them. Code that constructed one, such as LimitParameter(5), or read its .root uses the plain value instead. See Root Models and Type Aliases.

Changed in 0.84.0

With --openapi-scopes api, a model derived from a schema inside paths is named after the operation without the Field prefix 0.83.0 put before it: FieldPetsGetResponse is now PetsGetResponse. The separators of a path are dropped, / alone becomes Root (RootGetResponse), and a name that starts with a digit keeps Field (Field2faCodesGetResponse for /2fa/codes). A derived name that a component schema already holds takes a numeric suffix, so a component OrdersGetResponse keeps its name and the model of GET /orders becomes OrdersGetResponse1. Code that imports a derived model by its old name uses the new one instead. Component schemas and $ref targets keep their names.

Changed in 0.84.0

With --openapi-scopes api, a $ref beside only annotations in a parameter, request body, or response schema is the referenced model itself, not a derived RootModel that wraps it, as it is for a property. The siblings that count as annotations are description, title, examples, example, default, deprecated, readOnly, writeOnly, externalDocs, $comment, and x- extensions. A $ref beside a keyword that changes its values, such as minLength, maxItems, or properties, still has a derived model, and so does one beside only nullable: true, unlike a property where it becomes Optional. See Root Models and Type Aliases.

Adding other scopes alongside api does not repeat schema generation. --openapi-include-paths filters root paths and their reachable callbacks; webhooks and standalone components retain their declarations.

Use standard JSON Pointer escaping in references: ~1 represents a slash in a key and ~0 represents a tilde. API scope rejects malformed or ambiguous pointer spellings. An API with no model declarations emits no model artifact and preserves an existing output file. Explicit model metadata can still describe an empty inventory.

For Python generation, pass openapi_scopes=[OpenAPIScope.Api] to generate() or GenerateConfig. Direct parser consumers use datamodel_code_generator.parser.openapi_scope.ApiOpenAPIParser with an OpenAPIParserConfig that explicitly includes OpenAPIScope.Api. Existing scopes continue to use OpenAPIParser; the default remains schemas.

items.title: Include operation schemas
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input openapi.yaml --output models.py \
  --openapi-scopes schemas paths

Also generates models from operation request bodies and responses.

items.title: Include operation parameter models
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input openapi.yaml --output models.py \
  --openapi-scopes schemas parameters paths

Also generates a query parameter model for each operation that has query parameters. Add --include-path-parameters to include URL path parameters in these models. Parameters can be declared inline or referenced from #/components/parameters. Unreferenced entries in components.parameters do not generate standalone models, and the parameters scope alone does not select operations.

items.title: When to use each scope
items.text: Use Case Recommended Scopes Basic model generation schemas (default) Request and response models schemas paths Request, response, and query parameter models schemas paths parameters

items.title: --include-path-parameters
items.text: Includes path parameters as fields in generated operation parameter models. Use this with --openapi-scopes paths parameters.

items.title: OpenAPI Example
items.text:
openapi: "3.0.3"
info:
  title: Orders API
  version: "1.0"
paths:
  /users/{user_id}/orders/{order_id}:
    get:
      operationId: getOrder
      parameters:
        - name: user_id
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
        - name: order_id
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: integer
      responses:
        '204':
          description: No content

items.title: Without --include-path-parameters
items.text: Only query parameters are included in operation parameter models. This example has only path parameters, so it does not generate a parameter model without the flag.

items.title: With --include-path-parameters
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input openapi.yaml --output models.py \
  --openapi-scopes paths parameters --include-path-parameters --use-operation-id-as-name

class GetOrderParameters(BaseModel):
    user_id: str
    order_id: int

items.title: When to use
items.text:
• Building request validation models that include URL parameters
  • Grouping query and URL path parameters in one operation parameter model

items.title: --use-operation-id-as-name
items.text: Uses the operationId from OpenAPI operations to name generated models instead of deriving names from paths.

items.title: OpenAPI Example
items.text:
paths:
  /users/{id}:
    get:
      operationId: getUserById
      responses:
        '200':
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  id: { type: integer }
                  name: { type: string }

items.title: Without --use-operation-id-as-name
items.text:
class UsersIdGetResponse(BaseModel):  # Derived from path
    id: int
    name: str

items.title: With --use-operation-id-as-name
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input openapi.yaml --output models.py --use-operation-id-as-name

class GetUserByIdResponse(BaseModel):  # Uses operationId
    id: int
    name: str

items.title: When to use
items.text:
• When operationId values are well-designed and descriptive
  • For consistency with generated API clients (e.g., OpenAPI Generator)
  • When path-derived names are too verbose or unclear

items.title: --read-only-write-only-model-type
items.text:
Generates separate request/response model variants for properties marked as readOnly or writeOnly in OpenAPI.

See CLI Reference: --read-only-write-only-model-type for the full option reference.

items.title: OpenAPI Example
items.text:
components:
  schemas:
    User:
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: integer
          readOnly: true        # Only in responses
        password:
          type: string
          writeOnly: true       # Only in requests
        name:
          type: string          # In both

items.title: Without --read-only-write-only-model-type
items.text:
class User(BaseModel):
    id: Optional[int] = None  # Both included
    password: Optional[str] = None
    name: Optional[str] = None

items.title: With --read-only-write-only-model-type request-response
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input openapi.yaml --output models.py \
  --read-only-write-only-model-type request-response

class UserRequest(BaseModel):
    """For requests - excludes readOnly fields."""

    password: Optional[str] = None
    name: Optional[str] = None


class UserResponse(BaseModel):
    """For responses - excludes writeOnly fields."""

    id: Optional[int] = None
    name: Optional[str] = None

Use all instead of request-response when you also need the base model with all fields.

items.title: Values
items.text: Value Description request-response Generate request and response variants all Generate the base model plus request and response variants

items.title: When to use
items.text:
• APIs with distinct request/response schemas
  • Strict type checking for API clients
  • When readOnly/writeOnly properties are heavily used

items.title: --validation (Deprecated)
items.text:
Deprecated

Use --field-constraints instead. The --validation option is maintained for backward compatibility.

Enables validation constraints from OpenAPI schemas.

# Deprecated
datamodel-codegen --input openapi.yaml --output models.py --validation

# Recommended
datamodel-codegen --input openapi.yaml --output models.py --field-constraints

See Field Constraints for details.

items.title: Pattern 1: Basic API models
items.text:
For simple APIs where you only need schema models:

datamodel-codegen --input openapi.yaml --output models.py

items.title: Pattern 2: Full API client models
items.text:
For generating complete models for an API client:

datamodel-codegen --input openapi.yaml --output models/ \
  --openapi-scopes schemas parameters paths \
  --use-operation-id-as-name \
  --include-path-parameters

items.title: Pattern 3: Strict request/response separation
items.text:
For APIs with distinct input/output shapes:

datamodel-codegen --input openapi.yaml --output models/ \
  --read-only-write-only-model-type request-response \
  --field-constraints

items.title: Pattern 4: Versioned API structure
items.text:
For large APIs with versioned endpoints:

datamodel-codegen --input openapi.yaml --output models/ \
  --treat-dot-as-module \
  --use-operation-id-as-name \
  --all-exports-scope recursive

items.title: OpenAPI Version Support
items.text: OpenAPI Version Support 3.0.x Full support 3.1.x Full support 3.2.x Full support 2.0 (Swagger) Partial support

items.title: See Also
items.text:
• CLI Reference: OpenAPI-only Options
  • Field Constraints
  • Module Structure and Exports
  • OpenAPI Input Format

items.title: 📘 Generate from OpenAPI
items.text:
Generate Pydantic models from OpenAPI 3 schema definitions.

This page covers OpenAPI input behavior and examples. For task-oriented OpenAPI options, see OpenAPI Options. For the generated option reference, see CLI Reference: OpenAPI-only Options.

items.title: 🚀 Quick Start
items.text: datamodel-codegen --input api.yaml --input-file-type openapi --output model.py

items.title: 📝 Example
items.text:
api.yaml 
openapi: "3.0.0"
info:
  version: 1.0.0
  title: Swagger Petstore
  license:
    name: MIT
servers:
  - url: http://petstore.swagger.io/v1
paths:
  /pets:
    get:
      summary: List all pets
      operationId: listPets
      tags:
        - pets
      parameters:
        - name: limit
          in: query
          description: How many items to return at one time (max 100)
          required: false
          schema:
            type: integer
            format: int32
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A paged array of pets
          headers:
            x-next:
              description: A link to the next page of responses
              schema:
                type: string
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Pets"
        default:
          description: unexpected error
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error"
                x-amazon-apigateway-integration:
                  uri:
                    Fn::Sub: arn:aws:apigateway:${AWS::Region}:lambda:path/2015-03-31/functions/${PythonVersionFunction.Arn}/invocations
                  passthroughBehavior: when_no_templates
                  httpMethod: POST
                  type: aws_proxy
    post:
      summary: Create a pet
      operationId: createPets
      tags:
        - pets
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Null response
        default:
          description: unexpected error
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error"
                x-amazon-apigateway-integration:
                  uri:
                    Fn::Sub: arn:aws:apigateway:${AWS::Region}:lambda:path/2015-03-31/functions/${PythonVersionFunction.Arn}/invocations
                  passthroughBehavior: when_no_templates
                  httpMethod: POST
                  type: aws_proxy
  /pets/{petId}:
    get:
      summary: Info for a specific pet
      operationId: showPetById
      tags:
        - pets
      parameters:
        - name: petId
          in: path
          required: true
          description: The id of the pet to retrieve
          schema:
            type: string
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Expected response to a valid request
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Pets"
        default:
          description: unexpected error
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error"
    x-amazon-apigateway-integration:
      uri:
        Fn::Sub: arn:aws:apigateway:${AWS::Region}:lambda:path/2015-03-31/functions/${PythonVersionFunction.Arn}/invocations
      passthroughBehavior: when_no_templates
      httpMethod: POST
      type: aws_proxy

✨ Generated model.py:

from __future__ import annotations

from pydantic import AnyUrl, BaseModel, Field, RootModel


class Pet(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    tag: str | None = None


class Pets(RootModel[list[Pet]]):
    root: list[Pet]


class User(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    tag: str | None = None


class Users(RootModel[list[User]]):
    root: list[User]


class Id(RootModel[str]):
    root: str


class Rules(RootModel[list[str]]):
    root: list[str]


class Error(BaseModel):
    code: int
    message: str


class Api(BaseModel):
    apiKey: str | None = Field(
        None, description='To be used as a dataset parameter value'
    )
    apiVersionNumber: str | None = Field(
        None, description='To be used as a version parameter value'
    )
    apiUrl: AnyUrl | None = Field(
        None, description="The URL describing the dataset's fields"
    )
    apiDocumentationUrl: AnyUrl | None = Field(
        None, description='A URL to the API console for each API'
    )


class Apis(RootModel[list[Api]]):
    root: list[Api]


class Event(BaseModel):
    name: str | None = None


class Result(BaseModel):
    event: Event | None = None

items.title: 📖 readOnly / writeOnly Properties
items.text:
OpenAPI 3.x supports readOnly and writeOnly property annotations:

  • 📤 readOnly: Property is only returned in responses (e.g., id, created_at)
  • 📥 writeOnly: Property is only sent in requests (e.g., password)

items.title: ⚙️ Option: --read-only-write-only-model-type
items.text:
This option generates separate Request/Response models based on these annotations.

Value Description (not set) Default. No special handling (backward compatible) request-response Generate only Request/Response models (no base model) all Generate base model + Request + Response models

items.title: 📋 Example Schema
items.text:
openapi: "3.0.0"
info:
  title: Read Only Write Only Test API
  version: "1.0"
paths: {}
components:
  schemas:
    User:
      type: object
      required:
        - id
        - name
        - password
      properties:
        id:
          type: integer
          readOnly: true
        name:
          type: string
        password:
          type: string
          writeOnly: true
        created_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          readOnly: true
        secret_token:
          type: string
          writeOnly: true

items.title: ✨ Generated Output
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input user.yaml --input-file-type openapi \
    --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel \
    --read-only-write-only-model-type all

from __future__ import annotations

from pydantic import AwareDatetime, BaseModel


class UserRequest(BaseModel):
    name: str
    password: str
    secret_token: str | None = None


class UserResponse(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    created_at: AwareDatetime | None = None


class User(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    password: str
    created_at: AwareDatetime | None = None
    secret_token: str | None = None

items.title: 🎯 Usage Patterns
items.text: Use Case Recommended Option Generated Models API client validation request-response UserRequest, UserResponse Database ORM mapping (not set) User Both client & ORM all User, UserRequest, UserResponse

items.title: 🔗 Behavior with allOf Inheritance
items.text:
When using allOf with $ref, fields from all referenced schemas are flattened into Request/Response models:

openapi: "3.0.0"
info:
  title: Read Only Write Only AllOf Test API
  version: "1.0"
paths: {}
components:
  schemas:
    Timestamps:
      type: object
      properties:
        created_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          readOnly: true
        updated_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          readOnly: true

    Credentials:
      type: object
      properties:
        password:
          type: string
          writeOnly: true
        api_key:
          type: string
          writeOnly: true

    User:
      allOf:
        - $ref: "#/components/schemas/Timestamps"
        - $ref: "#/components/schemas/Credentials"
        - type: object
          required:
            - id
            - name
          properties:
            id:
              type: integer
              readOnly: true
            name:
              type: string
            email:
              type: string

Generated UserRequest will exclude created_at, updated_at, and id because they are readOnly fields from the flattened Timestamps/User schemas. Generated UserResponse will exclude password and api_key because they are writeOnly fields from Credentials.

items.title: ⚠️ Collision Handling
items.text: If a schema named UserRequest or UserResponse already exists, the generated model will be named UserRequestModel or UserResponseModel to avoid conflicts.

items.title: 📤 Supported Output Formats
items.text:
This option works with all output formats:

  • pydantic_v2.BaseModel
  • pydantic_v2.dataclass
  • dataclasses.dataclass
  • typing.TypedDict
  • msgspec.Struct

items.title: 🔗 Supported $ref Types
items.text:
readOnly/writeOnly resolution works with local and file reference types:

Reference Type Example Support Local #/components/schemas/User ✅ Supported File ./common.yaml#/User ✅ Supported

items.title: Supported OpenAPI Features
items.text: Feature Generation behavior components.schemas Default model generation scope components.parameters Resolved when referenced by selected operations; no standalone models for unreferenced entries paths operation schemas Generated with --openapi-scopes paths Operation query parameters Included with --openapi-scopes paths parameters; add --include-path-parameters for URL path parameters readOnly / writeOnly Request/response variants with --read-only-write-only-model-type Discriminators and combined schemas Converted into Python unions and inheritance-aware models where possible Local and file $ref Resolved before model generation

items.title: Limitations
items.text: OpenAPI input is used for model generation. Without the experimental --generate-server fastapi or --generate-client httpx2 options, it does not generate HTTP clients, server handlers, route definitions, or runtime request dispatch logic; with them, it also generates a FastAPI server package or a Python client package on top of the models. Full OpenAPI document validation is outside the generation path unless you explicitly enable validation-related options.

items.title: 📖 See Also
items.text:
• 🚀 Getting Started - Installation and first model
  • 🖥️ CLI Reference: OpenAPI-only Options - All OpenAPI-specific CLI options
  • ⚙️ CLI Reference: Base Options - Input/output configuration options

items.title: Output Model Types
items.text: datamodel-code-generator supports multiple output model types. This page compares them to help you choose the right one for your project.

items.title: Quick Comparison
items.text: Model Type Validation Serialization Performance Use Case Pydantic v2 Runtime Built-in Fast New projects, APIs, data validation Pydantic v2 dataclass Runtime Built-in Fast Pydantic validation with dataclass syntax dataclasses None Manual Fastest Simple data containers, no validation needed TypedDict Static only Dict-compatible N/A Type hints for dicts, JSON APIs msgspec Runtime Built-in Fastest High-performance serialization

items.title: Pydantic v2 (Recommended)
items.text:
Use --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel

Pydantic v2 is recommended for new projects. It offers better performance and a modern API.

datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel --output model.py

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, RootModel


class Pet(BaseModel):
    id: int = Field(..., ge=0)
    name: str = Field(..., max_length=256)
    tag: str | None = None


class Pets(RootModel[list[Pet]]):
    root: list[Pet]

items.title: When to use
items.text:
• New projects requiring data validation
  • APIs requiring data validation
  • Projects needing JSON Schema generation from models

items.title: Pydantic v2 dataclass
items.text:
Use --output-model-type pydantic_v2.dataclass

Pydantic v2 dataclass combines the familiar dataclass syntax with Pydantic's validation capabilities.

datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output-model-type pydantic_v2.dataclass --output model.py

from pydantic.dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional


@dataclass
class Pet:
    id: int
    name: str
    tag: Optional[str] = None

items.title: When to use
items.text:
• Want to use dataclass syntax with Pydantic validation
  • Migrating from dataclasses but need validation
  • Prefer decorator-based class definition

items.title: Targeting a Pydantic version
items.text:
Pydantic output depends only on the inputs and options, never on the Pydantic version installed next to datamodel-codegen. Use --target-pydantic-version to choose the oldest Pydantic release the generated code must run on. Pass --target-pydantic-version 2 when the generated code must also run on older Pydantic 2 releases. 2 means Pydantic 2.0.3 or later: generated code is not checked on 2.0.0 to 2.0.2.

When the target is unset:

  • Feature forms use the newest supported forms, the same as 2.12.
  • Config key naming is unchanged: --allow-population-by-field-name emits populate_by_name=True, as with 2. Only an explicit 2.11, 2.12 or 2.14 emits validate_by_name=True.
  • --use-missing-sentinel keeps the experimental pydantic.experimental.missing_sentinel import, as with 2.12.
Generated form 2 (Pydantic 2.0.3+) Unset, 2.11, 2.12, 2.14 Constrained strings with --use-annotated (2.1+) Annotated[str, Field(...)] Annotated[str, StringConstraints(...)] pydantic_v2.dataclass aliases that are not identifiers (2.4+) Field(validation_alias=..., serialization_alias=...) assignment Field(alias=...) Deprecated fields (2.7+) Field(json_schema_extra={'deprecated': True}) Field(deprecated=True) Models used as dictionary keys (2.8+) Defined before the models that use them as keys Schema order --alias-generator field aliases (2.8+) alias= on every BaseModel field alias= only where the generated alias differs Type alias patterns that need Python's regex engine (2.8+) String pattern; every model that reaches the alias, directly or through other models, sets regex_engine="python-re" Compiled re.compile(...) pattern pydantic_v2.dataclass aliases of other models (2.10+) Alias: TypeAlias = Model Alias = TypeAliasType("Alias", Model) Explicit aliases naming a BaseModel attribute (2.10+) Rejected when the attribute starts with model_ Rejected only when it starts with model_validate or model_dump --use-annotated fields whose type is defined later in the module (2.11+) name: Type = Field(...) assignment name: Annotated[Type, Field(...)]

Some constructs have no older form and are written for every target. When the target is older than the release that accepts and applies such a construct, the generation warns once, for the output it writes, with the release the generated models need and the models and fields that need it:

UserWarning: The generated models need pydantic>=2.5, newer than the target Pydantic version 2: regex_engine needs 2.5
(Model).

The warning does not change the output or the exit status. An unset target, which stands for the newest release, never warns, and 2.14 has nothing to warn about.

Written for every target Needs Pydantic Written when Field(union_mode=...) 2.2; 2.0 and 2.1 ignore it --union-mode on a union field A pattern on a union of str and bytes 2.2; 2.0 and 2.1 reject it at import --use-annotated or --field-constraints with a pattern beside string and format: binary branches that --collapse-root-models inlines coerce_numbers_to_str config key 2.4; older releases ignore it config in --extra-template-data regex_engine config key 2.5; older releases ignore it a pattern needs Python's regex engine, or config in --extra-template-data use_attribute_docstrings config key 2.7; older releases ignore it --use-attribute-docstrings, or config in --extra-template-data A pattern compiled with re.compile 2.8 the combined pattern facets of XML Schema input A type statement 2.10 --use-type-alias and the other aliases of pydantic_v2.BaseModel output with --target-python-version 3.12 or later A TypeAliasType alias of a model or alias 2.10 --use-type-alias with pydantic_v2.BaseModel before Python 3.12 (pydantic_v2.dataclass writes Alias: TypeAlias = Model) validate_by_name, validate_by_alias and serialize_by_alias config keys 2.11; older releases ignore them config in --extra-template-data (--allow-population-by-field-name follows the target) A pattern on bytes 2.14; 2.11 to 2.13 ignore it and older releases reject it at import --use-annotated or --field-constraints with format: binary and pattern

The warning reads what the built-in templates write: a custom template that writes other constructs is not covered, and neither is a key of a pydantic_v2.dataclass config that has no row above. Regex syntax that only newer versions of the Rust engine accept, such as \b{start}, which Pydantic 2.0 to 2.4 rejects, is not covered either.

Config key naming Unset, 2 2.11, 2.12, 2.14 --allow-population-by-field-name populate_by_name=True validate_by_name=True

2.12 also enables options that need Pydantic 2.12, such as --use-missing-sentinel.

--use-missing-sentinel import Unset, 2.12 2.14 MISSING (2.14 deprecates the experimental path) from pydantic.experimental.missing_sentinel import MISSING from pydantic import MISSING bytes patterns the Rust regex engine rejects Unset, 2, 2.11, 2.12 2.14 Model regex engine (2.14 compiles the patterns of plain and optional bytes fields, 2.11 to 2.13 ignore them) Default engine regex_engine="python-re"

The bytes rule is not applied to an unset target, because python-re changes how the other patterns of the model match on every Pydantic release. A bytes pattern with syntax such as a backreference then fails at import on Pydantic 2.14 unless --target-pydantic-version 2.14 is passed, and on Pydantic 2.12 for a bytes | MISSING field (--use-missing-sentinel), whose pattern 2.12 compiles as well. Pydantic 2.0 to 2.10 rejects any rendered bytes pattern at import. See Regular Expression Patterns.

pydantic_v2.dataclass required fields written as = Field(...) Unset, 2, 2.11, 2.12 2.14 Position when the schema lists them after a field with a default of the same class (2.13+ rejects that order in inspect.signature) Schema order Before the fields with defaults

A required pydantic_v2.dataclass field that needs Field(...), for an alias, a description or a constraint, is written as an assignment, so it can follow a field with a default:

@dataclass
class Pet:
    plain: str
    nick: str | None = "x"
    first_name: str = Field(..., alias="first-name")

With the target unset or older than 2.14, such a class keeps the order of datamodel-code-generator 0.83.0. It validates and constructs on Pydantic 2.4 and later, the first release that accepts the non-identifier alias, but on Pydantic 2.13 and later its signature cannot be read: inspect.signature(Pet) raises ValueError: non-default argument follows default argument, which affects tools that read the signature. On Python 3.10 with Pydantic 2.13 and later, a dataclass that inherits from such a class fails at import with the same error, because Python 3.10 reads the signature while it creates the subclass. Pass --target-pydantic-version 2.14 in either case: first_name is then written before nick. The generator warns about each class that keeps such an order, in its own fields or through its bases.

The order is not changed for an unset or older target, because positional arguments follow the field order: Pet("p", "a", "b") sets nick="a" in schema order and first_name="a" with 2.14. Keyword arguments work with both orders.

With --use-annotated a required field keeps its metadata in Annotated and comes before the fields with defaults on every target. A non-identifier alias of such a field is written as an assignment with 2 (see the 2.4 row above); the field then stays with the required fields, after those without an assignment. A required field that a subclass adds after an inherited field with a default is written with kw_only=True for every target.

Patterns that need Python's regex engine, such as lookaround assertions (see Regular Expression Patterns), rely on regex_engine="python-re", which Pydantic added in 2.5. With every target, a model that has such a pattern fails at import on Pydantic 2.0 to 2.4. A type alias (--use-type-alias, and the root schemas of pydantic_v2.dataclass output) has no config of its own:

  • With 2 its pattern stays a string, and every generated BaseModel or pydantic_v2.dataclass that reaches the alias, directly or through other models and their base classes, sets regex_engine="python-re", so the generated models validate on Pydantic 2.5 and later. A RootModel that reaches the alias is written as RootModel[Any] and keeps the alias in its root annotation, because Pydantic builds the generic before the config applies.
  • With 2, nothing selects the engine outside the generated models. A hand-written model that embeds a generated model or alias must set regex_engine="python-re" itself, and an alias validated on its own needs TypeAdapter(Alias, config=ConfigDict(regex_engine="python-re")). On Pydantic 2.8 to 2.10 this is a difference from an unset target, because no target lies between 2 and 2.11.
  • Unset, or with 2.11 and later, the alias carries a compiled re.compile(...) pattern, which needs Pydantic 2.8 and validates on its own.

The combined pattern constraints of XML Schema input stay compiled for every target, 2 included, and need Pydantic 2.8; see XML Schema limitations.

With 2 and --use-annotated, a BaseModel, RootModel or pydantic_v2.dataclass field whose type names a model defined later in the same module is written as an assignment, as it is without --use-annotated. Pydantic before 2.11 cannot evaluate such an annotation while it creates the class, and then mishandles the Field() inside Annotated[...]: depending on the release it drops the alias and the description, ignores validate_default, or fails on a constraint. Required dataclass fields written this way move after the other required fields. Fields that reference only their own model or earlier models, and output without deferred annotations (--disable-future-imports), keep the Annotated form.

For a field written this way, type checkers that read Field() assignments, such as pyright, take the alias as the constructor argument name and treat a positional default such as Field(None, alias=...) as a required argument. Add --use-default-kwarg to emit Field(default=None, ...) instead.

With 2, --alias-generator output names every alias in Field(alias=...). Type checkers that read the alias as the constructor argument name, such as pyright, then expect the alias instead of the field name; at runtime populate_by_name=True still accepts both.

items.title: dataclasses
items.text:
Use --output-model-type dataclasses.dataclass

Python's built-in dataclasses for simple data containers without runtime validation.

datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output-model-type dataclasses.dataclass --output model.py

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional


@dataclass
class Pet:
    id: int
    name: str
    tag: Optional[str] = None

items.title: Options for dataclasses
items.text:
Option Description --frozen-dataclasses Generate immutable dataclasses (frozen=True) --keyword-only Require keyword arguments (kw_only=True, Python 3.10+) --dataclass-arguments Custom decorator arguments as JSON 
# Frozen, keyword-only dataclasses
datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output-model-type dataclasses.dataclass \
  --frozen-dataclasses --keyword-only --target-python-version 3.10

items.title: When to use
items.text:
• Simple data structures without validation needs
  • Performance-critical code where validation overhead matters
  • Interoperability with code expecting dataclasses

items.title: TypedDict
items.text:
Use --output-model-type typing.TypedDict

TypedDict provides static type checking for dictionary structures.

datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output-model-type typing.TypedDict --output model.py

from typing import TypedDict, NotRequired


class Pet(TypedDict):
    id: int
    name: str
    tag: NotRequired[str]

items.title: When to use
items.text:
• Working with JSON APIs where data remains as dicts
  • Static type checking without runtime overhead
  • Gradual typing of existing dict-based code

items.title: Boundary payloads and partial updates
items.text:
TypedDict is a good fit for data at an HTTP boundary. A PATCH payload can distinguish three cases:

  • the key is missing, so the existing value should stay unchanged
  • the key is present with null, so the value should be cleared
  • the key is present with a value, so the value should be replaced

Use --strict-nullable when the difference between a missing key and a nullable value matters:

datamodel-codegen --input user-patch.schema.json \
  --output-model-type typing.TypedDict \
  --strict-nullable \
  --target-python-version 3.13 \
  --output model.py

{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "UserPatch",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id"],
  "properties": {
    "id": {"type": "string", "readOnly": true},
    "nickname": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
    "bio": {"type": "string"}
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}

from typing import NotRequired
from typing_extensions import TypedDict


class UserPatch(TypedDict, closed=True):
    id: str
    nickname: NotRequired[str | None]
    bio: NotRequired[str]

Here nickname: NotRequired[str | None] means the key may be omitted, and None is still a real value when the key is present. This follows PEP 655, which added Required and NotRequired for per-key presence in TypedDict.

If the schema marks response-only fields with readOnly, combine this with --use-frozen-field to generate ReadOnly for TypedDict output:

datamodel-codegen --input user-patch.schema.json \
  --output-model-type typing.TypedDict \
  --strict-nullable \
  --use-frozen-field \
  --target-python-version 3.13 \
  --output model.py

from typing import NotRequired, ReadOnly
from typing_extensions import TypedDict


class UserPatch(TypedDict, closed=True):
    id: ReadOnly[str]
    nickname: NotRequired[str | None]
    bio: NotRequired[str]

ReadOnly comes from PEP 705. The closed=True output comes from PEP 728 and represents additionalProperties: false for type checkers that understand closed TypedDicts.

Background

The distinction between missing keys, None, and unset update arguments is covered in Koudai Aono's PyCon US 2026 talk Beyond Optional in Real-World Projects. In datamodel-code-generator today, TypedDict and msgspec preserve that boundary shape most directly. Pydantic models and dataclasses are usually a better fit after the boundary has been normalized into application data.

items.title: msgspec
items.text:
Use --output-model-type msgspec.Struct

msgspec offers high-performance serialization with validation.

pip install msgspec
datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output-model-type msgspec.Struct --output model.py

from msgspec import Struct, UNSET, UnsetType


class Pet(Struct):
    id: int
    name: str
    tag: str | UnsetType = UNSET

items.title: Discriminated unions
items.text:
msgspec only decodes a union of structs when every struct is tagged, and a tagged struct cannot also have a field named like its tag_field. By default the output keeps the 0.83.0 form, in which a variant whose discriminator value comes from the discriminator mapping, an enum or the schema name keeps the discriminator as a field:

class Cat(Struct):
    petType: Literal["cat"]
    meow: str | UnsetType = UNSET

Cat(petType='cat'), cat.petType and decoding Cat on its own work, but decoding the union Cat | Dog raises msgspec's TypeError. That form only tags a variant whose discriminator property is a single literal such as a const, or one that a second discriminated union uses, and its tag_field is the generated field name, which differs from the property name when the field is renamed. A property named pet-kind is tagged by pet_kind, which msgspec looks for in the payload instead. --tag-msgspec-by-payload-name tags those structs by the property name of the document (pet-kind) and changes nothing else.

--use-msgspec-tagged-unions writes a union as tagged structs as a whole instead, with the property name of the document as tag_field:

class Cat(Struct, tag_field="petType", tag="cat"):
    meow: str | UnsetType = UNSET

The union then decodes, while petType is no longer a constructor argument or an attribute, and Cat decoded on its own accepts a payload without petType. When a variant cannot take exactly one tag for the union, or a base or derived struct of a variant keeps the property as a field, the union tags none of its variants, the ones with a const included, and a warning names the reason. A variant that another union tags keeps that tag.

items.title: Enums that list null
items.text:
msgspec only decodes an Enum whose members are all str or all int values. By default the output keeps the 0.83.0 form of an enum that lists null without type: string or nullable: true, such as type: [integer, "null"] with enum: [1, 2, null], which is an Enum with a None member:

class Size(Enum):
    int_1 = 1
    int_2 = 2
    NoneType_None = None

Size.int_1 works, but decoding a struct with a Size field raises msgspec's TypeError. --use-msgspec-nullable-enum-alias writes it as a type: string or nullable enum is written instead, an Enum without the None member and an alias that adds None:

class SizeEnum(Enum):
    int_1 = 1
    int_2 = 2


Size: TypeAlias = SizeEnum | None

msgspec then decodes the members and null, while code that used Size.int_1 or Size.NoneType_None uses SizeEnum.int_1 and None. The default of a field of such an enum is then its raw value, also with --set-default-enum-member, and an enum that lists only null becomes None. An enum whose class has a value type base, the IntEnum of a type: integer enum or a --use-subclass-enum class such as (int, Enum), cannot hold a None member, so without the option it is written without that member and, as its one type rejects null, without the alias.

items.title: When to use
items.text:
• High-performance JSON/MessagePack serialization
  • Memory-efficient data structures
  • APIs with strict performance requirements

items.title: Choosing the Right Type
items.text:
graph TD
    A[Need runtime validation?] -->|Yes| B[Need best performance?]
    A -->|No| C[Need type hints for dicts?]
    B -->|Yes| D[msgspec.Struct]
    B -->|No| G[Prefer dataclass syntax?]
    G -->|Yes| H[pydantic_v2.dataclass]
    G -->|No| I[pydantic_v2.BaseModel]
    C -->|Yes| J[typing.TypedDict]
    C -->|No| K[dataclasses.dataclass]

items.title: Decision Guide
items.text:
1. API with validation → Pydantic v2
  2. Validation with dataclass syntax → Pydantic v2 dataclass
  3. High-performance serialization → msgspec
  4. Simple data containers → dataclasses
  5. Dict-based JSON handling → TypedDict

items.title: Performance Benchmarks
items.text:
This page tracks datamodel-code-generator release and main-branch benchmark results collected on GitHub Actions. The data covers only datamodel-code-generator and uses Ubuntu runners so release-to-release changes can be compared without mixing in third-party generator results. Automatic backfills select versions from PyPI download-by-version data when that public dataset is available.

datamodel-code-generator supports many schema styles and production use cases, so it includes a broad set of useful options. As releases add more capabilities, these benchmarks help keep the implementation measured, managed, and tuned so code generation stays fast in everyday use.

items.title: Scenario Guide
items.text:
Each scenario combines an input type with a case size. This guide is generated from the scenario keys in the benchmark JSON and the collector case definitions, so it changes when the benchmark matrix changes.

Scenario Input fixture Formatters Represents Small / JSON Schema tests/data/jsonschema/person.json default (black/isort default), builtin (Built-in), ruff (Ruff) Compact fixture that emphasizes CLI startup, parsing, and formatter overhead for JSON Schema to Pydantic v2 model generation. Small / OpenAPI tests/data/openapi/api.yaml default (black/isort default), builtin (Built-in), ruff (Ruff) Compact fixture that emphasizes CLI startup, parsing, and formatter overhead for OpenAPI component resolution and Pydantic v2 model generation. Large / JSON Schema tests/data/performance/large_models.json default (black/isort default), builtin (Built-in), ruff (Ruff) Larger fixture that emphasizes parser and model graph throughput for JSON Schema to Pydantic v2 model generation. Large / OpenAPI tests/data/performance/openapi_large.yaml default (black/isort default), builtin (Built-in), ruff (Ruff) Larger fixture that emphasizes parser and model graph throughput for OpenAPI component resolution and Pydantic v2 model generation.

items.title: Interpreting Metrics
items.text:
• median_ms is the primary comparison value: it is the median generation duration after warmup runs, and lower is faster.
  • min_ms, max_ms, and stdev_ms describe the measured spread for the same row; wide ranges usually mean CI runner noise rather than a deliberate code change.
  • Formatter comparisons are scoped to the same scenario and version. default is the black/isort default baseline, while builtin and ruff ratios compare their medians to that baseline.
  • ok rows have timing data. unsupported means the formatter or option was unavailable in that release. failed means installation or command execution failed, so timing cells are intentionally empty.

items.title: Historical Trends
items.text:
The benchmark data on this page is loaded from docs/data/release-benchmarks.json and rendered in the browser. Release runs update that JSON file directly, so the published page reflects new release measurements after the docs deployment without rewriting this Markdown file.

Loading benchmark data...

JavaScript is required to load the release benchmark data.

items.title: Collection Policy
items.text:
• The benchmark workflow runs on ubuntu-24.04.
  • Benchmark results are collected on GitHub Actions CI runners, so median timings can vary slightly with runner load and workflow timing; rerun benchmarks before treating small differences as regressions.
  • The Python version is the workflow input, defaulting to the latest configured CI Python.
  • Release packages are installed from PyPI in isolated virtual environments.
  • Every benchmark update measures main from an exact commit resolved at workflow start and replaces the previous main snapshot.
  • Input coverage currently focuses on OpenAPI and JSON Schema.
  • Historical updates commit docs/data/release-benchmarks.json; the page renders that JSON client-side.

items.title: Playground
items.text:
Run datamodel-code-generator in your browser. The deployed site serves this route as a standalone app so Pyodide only starts after you open it.

Playground privacy

The playground runs entirely in your browser with Pyodide. Your schema, selected input type, and options are passed to the local Pyodide worker for generation and are not posted to a backend server.

Use Copy Repro URL in the playground to share the current input schema, input type, and selected options in the URL fragment. When a playground version is selected, Copy Repro URL keeps the selected ?version= in the shared URL. The fragment part (#state=...) is client-side URL state and is not included in HTTP requests, so the encoded schema and options are not sent to the hosting server or Cloudflare by opening the link. The complete URL, including the fragment, can still be stored in local browser history and is visible to anyone or any service you share it with. The optional ?version= query parameter is sent in normal page requests, so hosting/CDN metrics can record the selected playground version but not the encoded schema or options.

Open Playground

items.title: Presets
items.text:
Presets are immutable named groups of CLI options. A preset name never changes behavior; new recommendations are published as new dated preset names.

Every preset name includes its Python target, so generated Python syntax is pinned without an extra --target-python-version argument. Choose the preset name instead of adding a separate target option to normal preset commands; if an explicit target is already present in CLI or pyproject configuration, it must match the preset name.

See also: CLI Reference, --preset, --target-python-version, --output-model-type, --profile, --generate-pyproject-config, --generate-cli-command, pyproject.toml configuration, and CI/CD integration.

items.title: Usage
items.text:
Use a preset by passing its immutable name:

datamodel-codegen \
  --input schema.json \
  --input-file-type jsonschema \
  --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel \
  --preset standard-py312-20261019 \
  --output model.py

Use standard-py312-20261019 for the project-recommended modern Python 3.12 baseline. Use practical-py312-20261019 when you also want schema-authored names, model reuse, and schema descriptions embedded in the generated code.

To choose options on top of a preset for your schema, add --recommend-options to the command (experimental); see Option recommendations.

Presets dated 20260909 or later select builtin to avoid running external formatters. For project-wide Ruff consistency, use the preset with --formatters ruff-check ruff-format. Keep --formatters black isort to preserve existing Black/isort output. Earlier dated presets are unchanged. Black and isort remain required installation dependencies.

The 20261015 presets keep the 20260909 options and add Python 3.15 targets.

The 20261017 presets keep the 20261015 options and add --enum-field-as-literal all for stdlib dataclass and TypedDict output. These models keep raw JSON values without conversion, so enums render as Literal values instead of enum classes. Options of an output model scope take precedence over the options for all output model types.

The 20261019 presets keep the 20261017 options and add --use-single-value-enum-as-const: an enum of one value, and an enum that admits the const beside it, render as that const's Literal value instead of an enum class, and one-value enum branches of a oneOf or anyOf merge into one enum. They also add --openapi-paths-bodies-as-definitions: request and response bodies of the OpenAPI paths and webhooks scopes get the model a schema definition of the same body gets, --omit-redundant-constraints: a constraint that a zero-bound class or a const or enum Literal already enforces is not written again, and --use-site-models-for-constrained-refs: an allOf whose other parts add constraints, an enum or a type to a referenced schema gets its own model of the values all parts admit instead of the referenced type.

items.title: Override Preset Options
items.text:
Preset options are defaults, not locks. Explicit options override preset-supplied values.

datamodel-codegen \
  --input schema.json \
  --preset standard-py312-20261019 \
  --no-snake-case-field \
  --no-use-annotated \
  --enum-field-as-literal none

Use documented --no-* options for boolean settings that support negation. For value options, pass the replacement value explicitly, such as --enum-field-as-literal none.

items.title: Add Options On Top
items.text:
You can add any normal CLI option to a preset command. This is the recommended way to start from a preset and make a project-specific choice:

datamodel-codegen \
  --input schema.json \
  --preset standard-py312-20261019 \
  --extra-fields forbid \
  --use-title-as-name \
  --output model.py

items.title: Use Presets With Profiles
items.text:
Presets can live in [tool.datamodel-codegen] or in a named profile. Profiles are useful when one repository generates several model sets:

pyproject.toml
[tool.datamodel-codegen]
output-model-type = "pydantic_v2.BaseModel"
preset = "standard-py312-20261019"

[tool.datamodel-codegen.profiles.api]
input = "schemas/api.json"
output = "src/models/api.py"
preset = "practical-py312-20261019"
extra-fields = "forbid"

[tool.datamodel-codegen.profiles.events]
input = "schemas/events.json"
output = "src/models/events.py"
use-title-as-name = true

datamodel-codegen --profile api
datamodel-codegen --profile events

If --preset is passed on the CLI, it overrides pyproject preset settings and pyproject options unless the same option is also explicit on the CLI. If preset is configured in pyproject.toml, pyproject/profile options and CLI options override preset-supplied values.

items.title: Export Configuration
items.text:
To convert a working preset command into pyproject.toml, use --generate-pyproject-config:

datamodel-codegen \
  --input schema.json \
  --output model.py \
  --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel \
  --preset practical-py312-20261019 \
  --extra-fields forbid \
  --generate-pyproject-config

To inspect the effective CLI command for an existing pyproject profile, use --generate-cli-command:

datamodel-codegen --profile api --generate-cli-command

Use --ignore-pyproject when you want to test a preset command without loading project configuration.

To preserve Black/isort formatting, override with --formatters black isort. Field defaults kept off branch roots --keep-field-defaults-off-branch-roots Leave the default of a property off the root models extracted from the branches of its anyOf or oneOf. Tuples for closed arrays --use-tuple-for-closed-arrays Generate tuple types for positional arrays that no other item can follow, so that each position keeps its own type. One dict for object maps --use-single-dict-for-object-maps Type an object map whose keys patternProperties or propertyNames constrain as one dict of the values of every key class. Stricter pattern-map checks --check-pattern-maps-strictly Under --generate-schema-validators, count every key that a pattern admits, check declared keys against the patterns that match them, and keep the propertyNames keys and the other types of a type array of an object without properties. Typed map values beside other types --use-typed-map-values-beside-other-types Under --use-typed-nullable-map-values, also type the map values of a type array that lists object beside other types, such as [object, string]. Enum member values kept --keep-enum-member-values Write an enum as a plain Enum where its IntEnum, StrEnum or (T, Enum) base would change a member value, such as 2.5 beside integer members. Constructor fields ordered by final names --order-constructor-fields-by-final-names Order the constructor fields of dataclass and msgspec models after every field has its final name. Constructor fields ordered by written defaults --order-constructor-fields-by-written-defaults Order the fields of msgspec models by the defaults they write. Request and response variants deduplicated --dedupe-request-response-variants Decide Request and Response variants from the schema graph and build each inline model once. Scope Options Notes All output model types --use-standard-collections, --use-union-operator, --use-annotated, --enum-field-as-literal one, --use-subclass-enum, --collapse-root-models, --strict-nullable, --disable-timestamp Use built-in collection syntax, PEP 604 unions, Annotated constraints, single-value enum Literals, typed enum subclasses, inline root wrappers, schema-accurate nullability, and reproducible file headers. Python 3.11+ targets --use-specialized-enum Use StrEnum or IntEnum only when the selected target Python version supports it. Pydantic v2 BaseModel and dataclass output --snake-case-field, --allow-population-by-field-name, --use-frozen-field Generate Pythonic field names while preserving input aliases and readOnly immutability metadata. msgspec Struct output --snake-case-field, --use-standard-primitive-types Generate Pythonic field names with aliases and stdlib primitive types for schema formats. stdlib dataclass output --use-standard-primitive-types, --enum-field-as-literal all Use stdlib primitive types without renaming input keys because dataclasses do not carry aliases. Stdlib dataclasses keep raw JSON values without conversion, so enums render as Literal values instead of enum classes; this overrides --enum-field-as-literal one from All output model types. TypedDict output --use-standard-primitive-types, --use-frozen-field, --enum-field-as-literal all Use stdlib primitive types and ReadOnly metadata without renaming dictionary keys. TypedDict holds raw JSON values, so enums render as Literal values instead of enum classes; this overrides --enum-field-as-literal one from All output model types. Serialized defaults --deserialize-default-values decimal enum Deserialize compatible serialized Decimal and enum defaults into generated Python values while preserving defaults that cannot be converted safely. Built-in formatting --formatters builtin Format generated models without running an external formatter. For projects using Ruff, override with --formatters ruff-check ruff-format. To preserve Black/isort formatting, override with --formatters black isort. Enums read as their const --use-single-value-enum-as-const Read an enum of one value, and an enum that admits the const beside it, as that const, so it renders as a Literal value instead of an enum class; one-value enum branches of a oneOf or anyOf merge into one enum. Paths bodies modeled as definitions --openapi-paths-bodies-as-definitions Give the request and response bodies of the OpenAPI paths and webhooks scopes the model a schema definition of the same body gets, so an object body with a type array such as [object, null] is a model instead of an inline type. Site models for constrained references --use-site-models-for-constrained-refs Give an allOf of $ref members whose other parts add constraints, an enum or a type its own model of the values all parts admit, instead of the referenced type, which leaves the added assertions out; an allOf of enum references gets the enum of the members they share. Redundant constraints omitted --omit-redundant-constraints Do not write a constraint again beside a type that already enforces it: the bound of a zero-bound class such as NonNegativeInt, and the length and number constraints a const or enum Literal meets by its values, which also keeps such a const branch inline instead of a root model. Const read beside an enum --read-const-beside-enum Read a const beside an enum as JSON Schema does: a value is typed by the const that narrows the enum, and an enum that admits its const is read as that const. Literal values filtered --filter-literal-values Keep only the values of a const or enum that meet the length, pattern, bound and multipleOf constraints beside them. allOf keywords intersected --intersect-allof-keywords Combine the keywords of every part of an allOf, a $ref with sibling keywords and an inherited property override as JSON Schema validates them: the tightest bounds and the values every part admits. Nullable beside a type list --read-nullable-beside-type-list Write the null that nullable: true declares beside a type list with an object into the root model of that schema under strict nullable output. Field defaults kept off branch roots --keep-field-defaults-off-branch-roots Leave the default of a property off the root models extracted from the branches of its anyOf or oneOf. Tuples for closed arrays --use-tuple-for-closed-arrays Generate tuple types for positional arrays that no other item can follow, so that each position keeps its own type. One dict for object maps --use-single-dict-for-object-maps Type an object map whose keys patternProperties or propertyNames constrain as one dict of the values of every key class. Stricter pattern-map checks --check-pattern-maps-strictly Under --generate-schema-validators, count every key that a pattern admits, check declared keys against the patterns that match them, and keep the propertyNames keys and the other types of a type array of an object without properties. Typed map values beside other types --use-typed-map-values-beside-other-types Under --use-typed-nullable-map-values, also type the map values of a type array that lists object beside other types, such as [object, string]. Enum member values kept --keep-enum-member-values Write an enum as a plain Enum where its IntEnum, StrEnum or (T, Enum) base would change a member value, such as 2.5 beside integer members. Unevaluated properties read --read-unevaluated-properties Read a schema-valued unevaluatedProperties as additionalProperties where no applicator evaluates the object in place.
