None for an optional request body whose schema rejects JSON null is sent as UNSET is: the request has no body and no Content-Type, which a server reads as an absent body, and a media_type beside it is refused with a ConfigurationError whose reason is without_body. A JSON body whose type admits null, such as a nullable schema, one without a schema, or Any, sends null. Generation decides this from the type the models give the body, by the same rule the generated FastAPI server reads a body and sends a response by, so every model backend sends the same request: an x-python-type annotation admits null when it writes None, object, Any under any alias, or a Literal with None. The media a call names decides, or the default media without one; an operation with several media and no default leaves None out when none of them takes null, and otherwise needs media_type. A text, form, or binary body has no null, so its None is left out.

items.title: Responses
items.text:
A method returns the decoded body. Each resource also has three response views, the same methods returning more:

from app.client import Client
from fake import http_client

with Client(bearer="s3cret", http_client=http_client()) as client:
    response = client.pets.with_response.list_pets(tag="cat")
    info = response.info
    print(len(response.data.root), info.status_code, info.content_type, info.request_id, info.attempt_count)
    print(info.headers.get("x-request-id"), info.headers)

    raw = client.pets.with_raw_response.get_pet(pet_id=99)
    print(raw.info.status_code, raw.json())

    with client.pets.with_streaming_response.list_pets() as streamed:
        body = b"".join(streamed.iter_bytes())
    print(streamed.info.status_code, len(body))

> GET https://eu.shelter.example/v1/pets?limit=20&tag=cat authorization: Bearer s3cret
2 200 application/json req-7 1
req-7 HeadersView(<3 headers>)
> GET https://eu.shelter.example/v1/pets/99 authorization: Bearer s3cret
404 {'message': '/pets/99 not found'}
> GET https://eu.shelter.example/v1/pets?limit=20 authorization: Bearer s3cret
200 70
View Returns client.pets.list_pets(...) The decoded body, such as Pets client.pets.with_response.list_pets(...) A Response with the decoded data and the info of the response client.pets.with_raw_response.list_pets(...) A RawResponse with the body read into memory but not decoded; an error status does not raise client.pets.with_streaming_response.list_pets(...) A context manager that sends on entry and yields a RawResponse whose body you read as it arrives

Response, ResponseInfo, RawResponse, AsyncRawResponse, and HeadersView come from client.responses. ResponseInfo describes one completed call:

Field Value status_code The final status headers The final response's headers as a HeadersView: get(name) returns the first value, get_all(name) every value, in received order and compared without case; its representation shows no value content_type The response's media type, or None request_id The value of the operation's request_id_header, here X-Request-Id, which a per-operation setting declares; otherwise None attempt_count How many attempts the call sent, retries included elapsed The seconds the call took, retries and waits included

A RawResponse has info, read(), text(), json(), iter_bytes(), iter_raw_bytes(), stream_to(path or file), and raise_for_status(), which raises the error a typed call would; AsyncRawResponse has the same as coroutines and async iterators. Leave a streaming response's with block to release it, also when you stop reading early. The client and its views also have request_raw(method, url, ...), which sends a request outside the operations and returns a RawResponse.

The text of ResponseInfo.headers is what HTTPX2 decodes, with one codec for the whole header set of the response: ASCII, else UTF-8 when every header is UTF-8, else Latin-1. A declared response header that a typed call reads is ASCII header text, whatever the codec chose; see model codecs.

items.title: Client settings
items.text:
Client and AsyncClient take their settings as keywords. client.with_options(...) returns a view with some of them replaced, and a method's options=RequestOptions(...) replaces them for one call. RequestOptions, RetryOptions, ServerSelection, Clock, and UNSET come from client.options.

Keyword Client with_options RequestOptions Meaning base_url Yes Yes Yes One URL that replaces the document's servers; see Base URLs and servers server Yes Yes Yes A ServerSelection of a declared server and its variables default_headers, default_query Yes Yes extra_headers, extra_query Headers and query fields added to every request; see Headers and query defaults timeout Yes Yes Yes The HTTPX2 phase limits; see Timeouts total_timeout Yes Yes Yes A budget for the whole call, retries included max_retries, retry Yes Yes Yes The retry count and a RetryOptions; see Retries follow_redirects Yes Yes Yes Whether HTTPX2 follows redirects; see Redirects auth Yes Yes Yes An httpx2.Auth that replaces the credentials; see Authenticate idempotency_key No No Yes The key of one call; see idempotency keys Credentials, such as bearer Yes No No One keyword per security scheme; see Authenticate clock Yes No No The time, jitter, and wait sources; see Clocks http_client Yes No No An HTTPX2 client of your own; see Use your own HTTPX2 client compression Yes Yes Yes Only in a package with an operation that accepts gzip; see Request compression helper_defaults, cache_stores, allowed_origins Yes No No Only in a package with protocol helpers; see Helper settings

A setting a call leaves unset inherits from the nearest view, then the client. The example below sets several of them:

import httpx2

from app.client import Client
from app.client.options import RequestOptions, ServerSelection
from fake import http_client

with Client(
    bearer="s3cret",
    server=ServerSelection(variables={"region": "us"}),
    default_headers={"X-App": "shelter-cli"},
    timeout=httpx2.Timeout(10, connect=2),
    http_client=http_client(),
) as client:
    client.pets.list_pets()

    traced = client.with_options(default_headers={"X-Trace": "on"}, total_timeout=30)
    traced.pets.list_pets()

    staging = RequestOptions(base_url="https://staging.shelter.example/v1", extra_headers={"X-App": None})
    client.pets.list_pets(options=staging)

> GET https://us.shelter.example/v1/pets?limit=20 x-app: shelter-cli authorization: Bearer s3cret
> GET https://us.shelter.example/v1/pets?limit=20 x-app: shelter-cli x-trace: on authorization: Bearer s3cret
> GET https://staging.shelter.example/v1/pets?limit=20 authorization: Bearer s3cret

items.title: Base URLs and servers
items.text:
Each operation sends to its effective OpenAPI servers, those of the operation, its path item, or the document. By default a call uses the first of them with the default of every server variable. A relative server URL resolves against --client-server-base-url, or against the document's own URL when it was read over HTTP or HTTPS. An operation without servers uses --client-default-base-url; without one, generation fails, for a GET /pets with Error: /paths/~1pets/get: A server of GET /pets does not resolve to an absolute http or https URL.

server=ServerSelection(index=, variables=) picks another declared server by position and supplies its variables, as the example picks the us region of the shelter's server; base_url= replaces the servers with one URL, as its last call does. Client, with_options, and RequestOptions take the same two keywords, and the nearest one given wins: a call's over its view's, a view's over the client's, so a view's server also replaces the client's base_url. Giving both on one of them raises ConfigurationError with the reason conflicts_with_server. An index the operation does not declare raises ConfigurationError with out_of_range, a variable it does not declare undeclared, and a value outside a variable's enum not_allowed, when the call is made.

items.title: Headers and query defaults
items.text: default_headers and default_query of the client and its views, and a call's extra_headers and extra_query, give each name they list their value over the generated headers and query, the client's first, then the views', the call's parameters', and the call's extra ones last; None removes that name. Header names compare case-insensitively, query names exactly. A body's media type ranks above every layer but the call's extra_headers: only a call's Content-Type relabels its body, or with None sends it unlabelled, and a multipart one without boundary= keeps the body's boundary. A header's name is an HTTP token and its value header text, HTAB, SP, and visible ASCII without whitespace at either end, or None: for any other, such as a value with a line break, café, or a space at its end, Client(...), with_options(...), and RequestOptions(...) raise ConfigurationError with the reason invalid_value and the field_path ("headers", name), so nothing is sent.

items.title: Timeouts
items.text:
The example above limits each HTTPX2 phase of a request to 10 seconds and connecting to 2, and gives every call of the traced view a budget of 30 seconds, retries and waits included.

Setting Effective default Meaning timeout Owned client: connect 5, read/write/pool 600 seconds; injected client: its native timeouts Native I/O phase limits total_timeout None Optional budget across attempts and retry waits, starting at call entry clock Clock(), the system clock Client only: time, jitter, and wait sources

Each setting a call leaves None inherits from the nearest with_options view, then the client. Where None has a meaning of its own, UNSET is the default and inherits instead: timeout=None clears all four phase limits, and total_timeout=None on a view or a call removes an inherited total budget. A number as timeout limits every phase, and an httpx2.Timeout gives each phase its own limit. An injected HTTP client's native timeouts supply the initial phase settings unless the client is given timeout. Durations must be finite and nonnegative; booleans are rejected. Invalid values raise ConfigurationError with the setting's field_path. total_timeout=0 is valid configuration; starting a call with it raises APITimeoutError before preparing or sending a request.

See Timeouts and cancellation for the budget across attempts, cancellation, and streams.

items.title: Retries
items.text:
A call is sent again after a failure that may pass, such as a connection that could not open or a 503, as long as the operation is safe to send again. The waits grow exponentially. This client waits without jitter and through a Clock that records each wait instead of sleeping, so the example shows them:

from app.client import Client
from app.client.options import Clock, RetryOptions
from fake import http_client

waits: list[float] = []
clock = Clock(monotonic=lambda: sum(waits), sleep=waits.append)

with Client(retry=RetryOptions(jitter="none"), clock=clock, http_client=http_client()) as client:
    response = client.default.with_response.get_health()
    print(response.data, response.info.attempt_count, waits)

> GET https://eu.shelter.example/v1/health
> GET https://eu.shelter.example/v1/health
> GET https://eu.shelter.example/v1/health
status='up' 3 [0.5, 1.0]

max_retries and retry=RetryOptions(...) apply on clients, views, and calls. The fields of RetryOptions merge independently; omitted fields inherit, while a status set replaces the inherited set, and retry=None inherits the whole record. Automatic retries require a candidate failure or status, operation safety, replayable input, and enough time. JSON/model decoding, arbitrary callbacks, cancellation, and logical deadlines never restart a request.

Setting Effective default Meaning max_retries 2 Retries after the initial attempt; 0 disables retries; a setting of its own, not a RetryOptions field initial_delay, max_delay 0.5, 8 seconds Exponential backoff, with maximum at least the initial delay jitter "full" Uniform delay below the exponential cap; "none" uses the cap statuses {408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504} Replace with an integer set in 400–599; 401/403/407 are forbidden max_retry_after 60 seconds Positive cap on accepted server delay; None removes this cap respect_retry_after True Explicit False ignores server delay hints retry_after_ms_header, should_retry_header Operation declaration, otherwise None Vendor controls require generated metadata; explicit None disables one retry_on_pool_timeout False Avoid amplifying pool contention unless explicitly enabled

GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, and DELETE are eligible for retries by default. POST, PATCH, and other methods require an explicit retry_safety="idempotent" declaration or a valid server key contract. A native ConnectError (TLS and DNS failures included), ConnectTimeout, or PoolTimeout proves the request unsent and can permit otherwise unsafe methods, unless an earlier attempt of the call, or a response HTTPX2 followed a redirect from, reached the server; every other failure after the send started may have been sent and is never sent again. retry_safety="never" prohibits every resend, including an unsent request.

See Retries and operation contracts for server delays, idempotency keys, and the retry settings an operation declares.

items.title: Views
items.text: A view is what with_options(...) returns: an object with the same resources and methods as its client, whose settings are the client's with the given ones replaced. In the example above, traced sends an extra header and has a 30-second budget, while client is unchanged. A view shares its client's connections and needs no closing; closing the client closes it too. Use a view for a group of calls with other settings, and options=RequestOptions(...) for one call. A view's default_headers and default_query add to the client's, and its other settings replace them.

items.title: Use your own HTTPX2 client
items.text: http_client= takes an httpx2.Client, or an httpx2.AsyncClient for AsyncClient, configured as you need: TLS, proxies, connection limits, HTTP/2, event hooks, or a transport such as the MockTransport of the examples. The client borrows it and never closes it, so close it after the client. Without one, the client creates httpx2.Client(timeout=httpx2.Timeout(600, connect=5)) and closes it on close() or at the end of with. See Instrumentation and Redirects and transport construction.

items.title: TLS certificate trust
items.text: HTTPX2 uses the operating system's trust store by default. Keep the CA certificates updated on the host or container running the generated client, including clients generated before a CA incident. Updating certifi or regenerating the client alone does not update that store. API calls, OAuth token requests, and secure WebSockets need current trust settings; a separate OAuth http_client needs its own update. See TLS certificate updates for custom CA files and directories.

items.title: Authenticate
items.text:
Generated clients compile root security inheritance and operation overrides from OpenAPI. Client and AsyncClient take one keyword argument per security scheme an operation requires, named after the scheme in snake case; a package whose operations have no credentialed security alternative takes no credentials, copies no credential runtime, and exports no AuthError. An argument whose name another constructor argument or scheme takes is suffixed, such as timeout_1 for a scheme named timeout, and so is the PascalCase prefix of OAuth provider classes that another scheme's prefix takes, as model class names are.

An API key or bearer argument takes a string, and an HTTP Basic one a (username, password) tuple, which is encoded as UTF-8, the charset of RFC 7617, which the generated server reads. Each also takes a callable returning its value, which the client calls for each request, so a rotating token or a key read from a secret store stays current; a bearer argument also takes an OAuth provider. A callable's failure raises AuthError with the reason provider_failed before the request is sent, and a value of the wrong type ConfigurationError with the reason invalid_type. A credential sent in a header, such as Bearer <token>, must be header text, as every header value: HTAB, SP, and visible ASCII without whitespace at either end, so an empty bearer token, a key with a space at its end, a line break, or café raises ConfigurationError with the reason invalid_value and the scheme's argument as field_path before sending; a key with an inner tab is sent. A cookie credential must be a cookie value: visible ASCII without ", ,, ;, or \. No environment variables or credentials are discovered by default.

from app.client import Client
from app.client.errors import ConfigurationError
from fake import http_client

with Client(bearer="s3cret", http_client=http_client()) as client:
    client.pets.get_pet(pet_id=1)

tokens = iter(["token-1", "token-2"])
with Client(bearer=lambda: next(tokens), http_client=http_client()) as client:
    client.pets.get_pet(pet_id=1)
    client.pets.get_pet(pet_id=2)

with Client(http_client=http_client()) as client:
    try:
        client.pets.get_pet(pet_id=1)
    except ConfigurationError as error:
        print(error.reason)

> GET https://eu.shelter.example/v1/pets/1 authorization: Bearer s3cret
> GET https://eu.shelter.example/v1/pets/1 authorization: Bearer token-1
> GET https://eu.shelter.example/v1/pets/2 authorization: Bearer token-2
missing_credentials

The bearer token goes to the Authorization header, a callable is called for each request, and a call that needs credentials that the client lacks raises ConfigurationError with the reason missing_credentials before sending. get_health declares security: [], so it needs no credentials.

A call sends the credentials of its operation's first security alternative they all satisfy: an AND alternative needs all its schemes, and an OR list is tried in declared order. Each credential goes to the header, query field, or cookie its scheme declares, replacing a value a client, view, or call header or a parameter put there, and only to the server's origin: a page a server links at another origin, and request_raw, carry none of them. Absent security, explicit [], and an empty alternative are anonymous choices that apply only when no other alternative is satisfied, so an optional operation sends a credential given for a listed scheme and, with none, sends nothing. A required operation that no credential satisfies raises ConfigurationError with the reason missing_credentials before sending, unless the HTTP client has an Auth of its own, which it then uses. The client authorizes no scopes: the resource server decides, and a 403 is terminal.

auth of the client, a view, or a call's RequestOptions takes any httpx2.Auth, which replaces the credentials for those calls, and auth=None sends without an Auth; it cannot make a required operation anonymous. Unset, the credentials apply, or else the HTTP client's own auth. Credentials given beside Client(auth=...) or an injected HTTP client with an auth raise ConfigurationError with the reason conflicting_auth, since one request runs one Auth flow.

Declare an API-specific challenge-less 401 contract in the operation's runtime setting of --client-operations. It is false unless explicitly set and is recorded under client-operations."<pointer>".runtime.auth_challenge_less_401 in the generated README. It lets an OAuth provider renew its token after a 401 without a WWW-Authenticate challenge. It is not a client option or an inferred response behavior.

[tool.datamodel-codegen.client-operations]
"/paths/~1challenge-less/get" = { runtime = { auth_challenge_less_401 = true } }

items.title: Sign requests with an HTTPX2 Auth
items.text:
Request signing is an httpx2.Auth of your own, given as auth. Its flow sees the final request, body included, after the client framed it; set requires_request_body = True to read a streamed body first. HTTPX2 runs it once per send, and every retry sends the original request through it again. Here the signer also places the bearer token, since auth replaces the client's credentials:

import hashlib
import hmac
from collections.abc import Generator

import httpx2

from app.client import Client
from fake import http_client


class BodySigner(httpx2.Auth):
    requires_request_body = True

    def __init__(self, key: bytes, token: str) -> None:
        self.key = key
        self.token = token

    def auth_flow(self, request: httpx2.Request) -> Generator[httpx2.Request, httpx2.Response, None]:
        digest = hmac.digest(self.key, request.method.encode() + b"\n" + request.content, hashlib.sha256)
        request.headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {self.token}"
        request.headers["X-Signature"] = digest.hex()
        yield request


with Client(http_client=http_client()) as client:
    signed = client.with_options(auth=BodySigner(b"signing-key", "s3cret"))
    print(signed.pets.create_pet(name="Kiki"))

> POST https://eu.shelter.example/v1/pets content-type: application/json authorization: Bearer s3cret x-signature: aebceadaa214619bd8402dec14456b4df1c8fd2fe8f7b399365e8b594e6aa679 {"name":"Kiki"}
id=3 name='Kiki' tag=None

A signature header other than Authorization is copied to a redirect HTTPX2 follows; set follow_redirects=False for signed calls whose redirects may leave the server's origin.

Credential values do not appear in repr. A credential placed in the query is part of the request URL, which HTTPX2 logs at INFO level on its httpx2 logger, so keep that logger above INFO wherever URLs must stay private. Errors retain safe metadata and their causes, which can hold an exception a credential callable raised; apply your own policy before logging causes.

items.title: OAuth providers
items.text:
A package whose operations require an OAuth 2 or OpenID Connect scheme exports ClientCredentials, RefreshToken, and TokenSet from its auth module, and one subclass for each declared flow whose token URL the API declares, such as OauthClientCredentials for the oauth scheme's client credentials flow. A subclass requests tokens from its declared URL unless token_url names another; the base classes need token_url. A provider is a bearer credential: the call that needs a token requests it inline while holding the provider's lock, a threading.Lock or an asyncio.Lock on the event loop the provider is used on, concurrent calls wait for that token, and nothing runs in the background or is persisted. The shelter's oauth scheme declares a client credentials flow, so its package has OauthClientCredentials:

from app.client import Client
from app.client.auth import OauthClientCredentials
from fake import http_client

provider = OauthClientCredentials(client_id="shelter-cli", client_secret="pa55", scopes=("pets.read",))
with Client(oauth=provider, http_client=http_client()) as client:
    client.pets.get_pet(pet_id=1)
    client.pets.get_pet(pet_id=2)

> POST https://auth.shelter.example/token content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded authorization: Basic c2hlbHRlci1jbGk6cGE1NQ== grant_type=client_credentials&scope=pets.read
> GET https://eu.shelter.example/v1/pets/1 authorization: Bearer issued-1
> GET https://eu.shelter.example/v1/pets/2 authorization: Bearer issued-1

The provider requested one token and sent it with both calls.

ClientCredentials requests a confidential client's own token. Its request sends the scopes in order and the audience when one is given, and authenticates the client with client_secret_basic (the default) or client_secret_post; the client_secret is a string or a callable returning one, called for each token request.

RefreshToken keeps an access token current with the refresh token grant, starting from the TokenSet an authorization produced. The provider alone refreshes it: no other provider or process may send the same refresh token, and since synchronous calls and each event loop renew under a lock of their own, use it from one of them at a time. Its client authentication defaults to none, which sends the client_id of a public client. For a scheme with an authorization code flow, construct the subclass from the TokenSet your authorization produced, as OauthRefreshToken(tokens, client_id="pets-app", on_token_refreshed=save), and pass it as the scheme's credential, such as Client(oauth=provider).

Each successful refresh makes a new TokenSet current, keeping the refresh token sent when the response gives none, and then passes it to on_token_refreshed while the provider still holds its lock, so an application can persist each token set in order; for an async client the callback may return an awaitable, which is awaited. An exception the callback raises reaches the caller, and the refreshed token set stays current. The callback must not call its own provider. A TokenSet needs a timezone-aware expires_at when its access token expires, and its repr omits both tokens. invalid_grant raises AuthError with the reason reauthorization_required, and the application starts a new authorization; a token set without a refresh token serves its access token until it expires or a resource rejects it, and then raises the same error without a request.

A provider serves its token until a tenth of its lifetime, at most thirty seconds, remains, and then the call that finds it due requests another; a token without expires_in is kept until a resource rejects it. When an early renewal fails, the call keeps using the current token until it expires, and each later call in that margin tries the renewal again. A 401 whose WWW-Authenticate has a Bearer invalid_token error, or a 401 without a challenge on an operation declaring auth_challenge_less_401, renews the token once, unless another call already replaced it, and sends the request again when its body can be sent again. A 401 after a redirect, and a WebSocket handshake's, renews nothing.

Token requests go through the client's HTTP client without its Auth and without following redirects, with the calling request's timeouts, or through the provider's own http_client when one is given, which keeps its own settings. The client's HTTP client runs its event hooks on these token requests and responses, which carry the client authentication and tokens. Used as an httpx2.Auth elsewhere, a provider needs its own http_client. The token URL must be HTTPS, or HTTP to a loopback host. A rejection, an unexpected status, or a response that is not a JSON object with a Bearer access_token raises AuthError with the reason oauth_error, a rejection keeping its status_code and standard oauth_error code, and an expires_in that is not a positive number, or a refreshed one past the last date Python can hold, the reason invalid_expiry. A transport failure raises AuthError with the reason oauth_error, or timeout, and the native exception as its cause, which can hold the token request and its client authentication. A provider's clock=Clock(...) times its token expiry.

items.title: Handle errors
items.text:
from app.client import Client
from app.client.errors import APIConnectionError, APIStatusError, NotFoundError
from fake import http_client

with Client(bearer="s3cret", http_client=http_client()) as client:
    try:
        client.pets.get_pet(pet_id=99)
    except NotFoundError as error:
        print(error.status_code, repr(error.body))

    try:
        client.adoptions.adopt_pet(pet_id=1)
    except APIStatusError as error:
        print(type(error).__name__, error)

    offline = client.with_options(base_url="https://offline.example/v1", max_retries=0)
    try:
        offline.pets.list_pets()
    except APIConnectionError as error:
        print(type(error).__name__, error.reason, repr(error.cause))

> GET https://eu.shelter.example/v1/pets/99 authorization: Bearer s3cret
404 Error(message='/pets/99 not found')
> POST https://eu.shelter.example/v1/pets/1/adoption authorization: Bearer s3cret
ConflictError Error code: 409 - {"message":"Mimi is already adopted"}
APIConnectionError None ConnectError('connection refused')

Every exception the client defines derives from SDKError and comes from client.errors; Python's own exceptions, such as TypeError for an unknown keyword, pass through unchanged. A declared error status raises the subclass of its status with the body decoded by the declared error schema, as NotFoundError and ConflictError do above; catch APIStatusError for any of them. A failure to reach the server raises APIConnectionError with the HTTPX2 exception as cause.

Exception Raised for APIStatusError A final status the operation does not declare as a success. Its subclasses are BadRequestError (400), AuthenticationError (401), PermissionDeniedError (403), NotFoundError (404), ConflictError (409), UnprocessableEntityError (422), RateLimitError (429), and InternalServerError (500 and above); it has status_code, headers, and body APIConnectionError A transport failure, after the retries it allows APITimeoutError A subclass of APIConnectionError: a phase timeout, or the call's total_timeout DecodeError An argument that cannot be sent, or a response that does not decode into its model ConfigurationError A setting, argument, or call the client refused before sending, with a reason and a field_path AuthError A credential callable or an OAuth token request that failed

Each also has reason, operation_id, info (the ResponseInfo when a response arrived), cause, attempt_count, elapsed, and request_id. Messages name no payload, header, or credential. See Errors for every field and reason.

items.title: Test code that uses the client
items.text:
Test your own code against an httpx2.MockTransport instead of a server: pass an HTTPX2 client with that transport as http_client, and answer each request in a function. Given a module that uses the client:

from app.client import Client
from app.client.errors import NotFoundError


def describe(client: Client, pet_id: int) -> str:
    try:
        pet = client.pets.get_pet(pet_id=pet_id)
    except NotFoundError:
        return f"No pet {pet_id}"
    return f"{pet.name} ({pet.tag or 'no tag'})"

its tests build the client in a fixture:

from collections.abc import Iterator

import httpx2
import pytest

from app.client import Client
from shelter import describe

PETS = {"/v1/pets/1": {"id": 1, "name": "Mimi", "tag": "cat"}}


def answer(request: httpx2.Request) -> httpx2.Response:
    assert request.headers["Authorization"] == "Bearer test-token"
    if (pet := PETS.get(request.url.path)) is None:
        return httpx2.Response(404, json={"message": "Not found"})
    return httpx2.Response(200, json=pet)


@pytest.fixture
def client() -> Iterator[Client]:
    with (
        httpx2.Client(transport=httpx2.MockTransport(answer)) as http,
        Client(bearer="test-token", http_client=http) as client,
    ):
        yield client


def test_describe(client: Client) -> None:
    assert describe(client, 1) == "Mimi (cat)"


def test_describe_missing(client: Client) -> None:
    assert describe(client, 2) == "No pet 2"

uv add --dev pytest
uv run pytest test_client.py

When the API is a FastAPI application you can import, such as one generated from the same document, FastAPI's TestClient is an httpx2.Client too: pass http_client=TestClient(app) and base_url="http://testserver" to call the application in the test process, without a server.

items.title: Regenerate after the document changes
items.text:
Run the same command again after the OpenAPI document changes. The methods change with the operations, so type checkers point at the calls to update. As for models, every generation overwrites every generated file of the package, also one you edited, and never deletes one. The modules of a resource that is no longer generated stay until you delete them: --check lists them as extra files, and a generation that leaves such .py files in place names them in one LeftoverFilesWarning, which Python shows once per process for the same text, also under --watch and repeated generate() calls. Silence exactly this warning with warnings.simplefilter("ignore", datamodel_code_generator.LeftoverFilesWarning) around generate(), or with ignore::datamodel_code_generator.LeftoverFilesWarning in pytest's filterwarnings. Keep your own code outside the package, because --check treats every .py file under --client-output as generated. The models can live inside the package, such as --output app/client/models.py with --client-model-package app.client.models, as for the server package.

--check compares without writing and prints the differences as for models, and --output-format json emits the model generation and check payloads, as with --generate-server; their target names the package and the runtime dependencies of the uv add notice, such as {"package": "app.client", "dependencies": ["httpx2>=2.13.0", "typing-extensions>=4.16", "pydantic>=2.14.0"]}. The generation payload adds the next steps of the notice: the package readme, with a path relative like those of files, and usage, the code that calls the first operation. --diff-against and --watch also work as they do with --generate-server. Use --check in CI to fail when the package is out of date; see Check in CI, which applies to the client as well.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
Like the server, the client needs Python 3.11 or later, both to run datamodel-codegen and as the target Python version. As for the server, a setting the client needs that you leave unset takes the value it needs, and a value you set that it cannot use is refused; see the server's Requirements, which also describes the notice that shows how to set them and target.implied. An unset target Python version is 3.11; one below 3.11 that you or a preset set is refused.

Settings of the generated client that change how its methods are declared or checked do not change the models: the same OpenAPI document and model settings produce the same model files whichever client settings you choose.

The model's openapi_scopes must include api, so that the models cover the parameters, bodies, and responses of the operations: unset, it is schemas api; scopes you give without api stop the run with Error: --generate-client requires --openapi-scopes to include api and exit code 2, and the Python API raises datamodel_code_generator.Error. The client keeps every model setting as given, including the generation timestamp, which disable_timestamp leaves out. The client files are headed, formatted, and encoded like the model files, by the same model settings: formatters, custom_formatters and custom_formatters_kwargs, custom_file_header, custom_file_header_path and custom_file_header_mode, disable_timestamp, enable_version_header, enable_command_header, use_double_quotes, builtin_format_line_length, encoding (for the Python files; the other files are UTF-8), settings_path, and use_type_checking_imports. As for the models, Ruff moves imports only an annotation uses into TYPE_CHECKING blocks when ruff-check runs with its TC rules selected and use_type_checking_imports allows it: by default for the dataclass, TypedDict, and msgspec backends, and with use_type_checking_imports for the Pydantic ones; the client reads no annotation at run time. As for the models, typing.get_type_hints on a generated class or function whose annotations name a moved import then raises NameError: pass --no-use-type-checking-imports, or do not select the TC rules, to introspect the annotations at run time. Custom templates and custom formatters must keep the class and field names of the models: the client binds each operation to the names in the generated model graph and does not read the rendered model source.

The generated package needs httpx2>=2.13.0 and the other requirements of the printed uv add command. With Pydantic models the minimum is pydantic>=2.14.0. An explicit --target-pydantic-version older than that minimum (2, 2.11 or 2.12) is refused with Error: and exit code 2 for those models; leave it unset or use 2.14. The other model backends do not use the option.

--use-missing-sentinel needs --target-pydantic-version 2.14, with which the models import MISSING from pydantic; with the sentinel, an unset target is 2.14. Model generation alone imports it from pydantic.experimental.missing_sentinel, which pydantic 2.14 deprecates, when the target is unset or 2.12, and refuses the option for 2 and 2.11. With a target of 2, 2.11, or 2.12 that you set, client generation stops with Error: The client target needs --target-pydantic-version 2.14 for --use-missing-sentinel, so that the models import MISSING from pydantic and exit code 2.

A pydantic_v2.dataclass field cannot tell an unset member from one set to None, so client generation with --output-model-type pydantic_v2.dataclass needs --use-missing-sentinel, and with it --target-pydantic-version 2.14: unset, the sentinel is on and the target is 2.14. With the sentinel turned off, use-missing-sentinel = false in pyproject.toml or use_missing_sentinel=False for generate(), generation stops with Error: The client target needs --use-missing-sentinel with --target-pydantic-version 2.14 for 'pydantic_v2.dataclass' models, whose fields cannot tell an unset member from None and exit code 2. With both, an optional field without a default holds MISSING, as it does for pydantic_v2.BaseModel when the options are set:

from app.client import Client
from app.models import NewPet
from pydantic import MISSING

with Client() as client:
    client.pets.create_pet(body=NewPet(name="Mimi"))  # tag holds MISSING, so the request leaves it out
    if client.pets.get_pet(pet_id=1).tag is MISSING:
        print("the response left tag out")

A field the constructor is not given holds MISSING and is left out of a request; give None to send null where the property is nullable. A member a response leaves out decodes to MISSING, and a null that its property does not allow is refused with a DecodeError whose reason is invalid_value.

msgspec decodes a union of structs only when every struct in it is tagged, and an Enum only when its members are all str or all int values, so client generation with --output-model-type msgspec.Struct needs --use-msgspec-tagged-unions and --use-msgspec-nullable-enum-alias, whether or not the document declares a discriminated union or an enum that lists null: unset, both are on. With one turned off in pyproject.toml or for generate(), generation stops with exit code 2 and an error that names every one turned off, such as Error: The client target needs --use-msgspec-tagged-unions for 'msgspec.Struct' models, so that their discriminated unions can be decoded; The client target needs --use-msgspec-nullable-enum-alias for 'msgspec.Struct' models, so that their enums that list null can be decoded, and the Python API raises datamodel_code_generator.Error. A union of structs that has no discriminator, or that the option still leaves untagged (with a warning that names the reason), cannot be decoded: a call that receives it fails with an APIConnectionError whose cause is msgspec's TypeError.

items.title: Generator options
items.text:
Every client setting is an option, a key of [tool.datamodel-codegen] in pyproject.toml, and an option of generate() for the Python API:

Option pyproject.toml key generate() option Default --generate-client httpx2 generate-client generate_client off --client-output client-output client_output required --client-package client-package client_package required --client-model-package client-model-package client_model_package required --client-signature-style client-signature-style client_signature_style "explicit"; see Signature style --client-body-arguments client-body-arguments client_body_arguments "body"; see Request bodies --client-resource-names client-resource-names client_resource_names none: a resource for each first tag, and default for operations without a tag --client-operations client-operations client_operations none; see Per-operation settings --client-default-base-url client-default-base-url client_default_base_url none; see Base URLs and servers --client-server-base-url client-server-base-url client_server_base_url none; see Base URLs and servers --client-protocols client-protocols client_protocols none; see Protocol Helpers

--client-resource-names, --client-operations, and --client-protocols take a JSON object, inline or as the path of a JSON file, as --aliases does; in pyproject.toml they are tables, or the path of a JSON file, and in generate() mappings of the same shape. A value on the command line takes precedence over the selected profile, which takes precedence over the base table, and a command-line table replaces the whole table of pyproject.toml. An operation's own body_arguments takes precedence over --client-body-arguments, wherever each comes from. Paths in pyproject.toml, including the JSON files of these settings, are relative to its directory, and command-line paths are relative to the working directory. The documents that operation references and helpers name are relative to the JSON file that holds them, however the file is given, as a $ref is relative to its document; a file given through a symbolic link uses the link's directory. Without a file, they are relative to the pyproject.toml directory for its tables, and to the working directory for inline JSON on the command line and for mappings given to generate().

--client-resource-names maps a tag to the dotted namespace of the resource its operations join, such as {"pets": "store.pets"}; a tag that is the first tag of no operation stops the run with an error, as a group key of --server-router-names that matches no group does on the server. Operations without a tag join the resource default, as in client.default.get_health(), the name the generated FastAPI server gives their group. Its name is derived like a tag's: beside a tag that also derives default, such as default or Default, the one declared first keeps default and the other takes a number, such as default_1, as on the server. No --client-resource-names entry names the operations without a tag, so the resource of a --client-operations entry moves one of them to another resource. Such a move leaves the derived names as they are: a tag, or the operations without one, takes its place among them from its first operation, moved or not, as the server's groups do. An explicit namespace is shared by everything that names it: a tag mapped to default, or an operation whose resource is default, joins the resource of that name.

--generate-client requires --client-output, --client-package, and --client-model-package, and a --client-* option given on the command line requires --generate-client; both stop with Error: and exit code 2. --generate-client also requires --input-file-type openapi: an input type left to detection, auto, or any other type stops with Error: --generate-client requires --input-file-type openapi, not auto (naming the given type) and exit code 2 before the input is read. --generate-client cannot be used with --generate-server, and one selected on the command line replaces the other selected in pyproject.toml. Client keys of pyproject.toml are validated like model keys, but have no effect while no client is selected.

items.title: Per-operation settings
items.text:
--client-operations maps an operation reference, the JSON pointer of the path item method such as /paths/~1pets/get, or a document and a pointer joined by #, to the settings of that operation, as the how-to project does for listPets. A pointer escapes ~ as ~0 and / as ~1, so the operation GET /pets/{petId} is /paths/~1pets~1{petId}/get; the generated README lists the reference of every operation.

Member Value resource The dotted namespace of the operation's resource name The method name parameter_names Argument names keyed by location and name, such as {"query:limit": "page_size"} request_media_type, response_media_type The default media types of the body and of the result description The method docstring, over the operation's route or, with --use-schema-description, its summary and description body_arguments "body" or "both", over --client-body-arguments body_field_names Keyword names of body fields, keyed by media type, then property, such as {"application/json": {"petName": "pet_name"}} runtime request_id_header, success_statuses, retry_safety, idempotency ({"header_name": "Idempotency-Key"}), retry_after_ms_header, should_retry_header, auth_challenge_less_401, and accepted_content_encodings 
[tool.datamodel-codegen.client-operations]
"/paths/~1pets/get" = { name = "list_all", parameter_names = { "query:limit" = "page_size" } }
"/paths/~1pets/post" = { runtime = { idempotency = { header_name = "Idempotency-Key" } } }

datamodel-codegen --client-operations '{"/paths/~1pets/get": {"name": "list_all"}}'

A member the client does not know, or a value it cannot use, stops generation with Error: and exit code 2, naming the setting by the key it was given under, such as --client-operations['/paths/~1pets/get'].runtime.retry_safety; generate() raises datamodel_code_generator.Error with the same message.

items.title: Python API
items.text:
generate() takes the client options with the model options. The choices are the enums ClientType, ClientSignatureStyle, and ClientBodyArguments of datamodel_code_generator, whose string values also work, and client_resource_names, client_operations, and client_protocols take mappings shaped like their JSON. The how-to project's settings:

from pathlib import Path

from datamodel_code_generator import (
    ClientBodyArguments,
    ClientType,
    DataModelType,
    InputFileType,
    OpenAPIScope,
    generate,
)

generate(
    Path("openapi.yaml"),
    input_file_type=InputFileType.OpenAPI,
    openapi_scopes=[OpenAPIScope.Schemas, OpenAPIScope.Api],
    output_model_type=DataModelType.PydanticV2BaseModel,
    preset="standard-py312-20261019",
    output=Path("app/models.py"),
    generate_client=ClientType.HTTPX2,
    client_output=Path("app/client"),
    client_package="app.client",
    client_model_package="app.models",
    client_body_arguments=ClientBodyArguments.Both,
    client_operations={"/paths/~1pets/get": {"runtime": {"request_id_header": "X-Request-Id"}}},
)

It publishes every change together and returns None, like model generation. Without an output, it writes nothing but the model metadata and a remote lock update and returns every model and client file as GeneratedModules, under the paths their import paths imply; see Generating a Server or Client Package. load_pyproject_config() reads the client keys of pyproject.toml, whose paths and documents resolve as they do on the command line. The uv add notice and the next steps are command-line messages only.

items.title: Batch jobs
items.text: A named job whose settings select the client generates it as a single run does, under the rules of server jobs: client-output must not overlap the outputs of other jobs or contain the remote lock file, and --all-jobs --watch regenerates client jobs too. Jobs that each select a server or a client may name the same models output, which the batch writes once; they must generate the same models for it.

items.title: Next steps
items.text:
• Python Client Protocol Helpers: generated pagers, polled long-running operations, resumable uploads, SSE and NDJSON streams, WebSockets, a response cache, and webhook verification, declared in a helper file.
  • Python Client Reference: signature styles, body field arguments, model conversion, timeouts and clocks, instrumentation, retries and operation contracts, request compression, body replay, redirects, templates, and every error.

items.title: 🐍 Generate from Python Models
items.text: Generate code from existing Python types: Pydantic models, dataclasses, TypedDict, or dict schemas. This is useful for converting between model types or generating from programmatically-defined schemas.

items.title: 🚀 Quick Start
items.text: datamodel-codegen --input-model ./mymodule.py:User --output model.py

items.title: 🔄 Convert Between Python Model Styles
items.text:
--input-model can retarget an existing Python model into another supported output model type. This is useful when moving a codebase between model frameworks, or when one boundary needs validation models while another boundary needs plain typed dictionaries.

# Pydantic BaseModel -> TypedDict
datamodel-codegen \
  --input-model ./models.py:User \
  --output-model-type typing.TypedDict \
  --output user_types.py

# TypedDict -> Pydantic v2
datamodel-codegen \
  --input-model ./types.py:User \
  --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel \
  --output user_model.py

items.title: Format
items.text:
--input-model <path/to/file.py>:<ObjectName>

Simply specify the file path and object name separated by :.

items.title: Example
items.text:
myproject/
├── src/
│   └── models/
│       └── user.py      # class User(BaseModel): ...
└── schemas.py           # USER_SCHEMA = {...}

# From file path (recommended - easy to copy-paste)
datamodel-codegen --input-model src/models/user.py:User --output model.py
datamodel-codegen --input-model ./schemas.py:USER_SCHEMA --input-file-type jsonschema

# Windows paths also work
datamodel-codegen --input-model src\models\user.py:User

Copy-paste friendly

Just copy the file path from your editor or file explorer, add :ClassName, and you're done!

items.title: Module format (alternative)
items.text:
You can also use Python module notation with dots:

datamodel-codegen --input-model src.models.user:User
datamodel-codegen --input-model schemas:USER_SCHEMA --input-file-type jsonschema

Current directory is auto-added to sys.path

No PYTHONPATH configuration needed.

File and package name conflict

If both mymodule.py and mymodule/ directory exist, use ./ prefix: 

datamodel-codegen --input-model ./mymodule.py:Model

items.title: Supported Input Types
items.text:
Type Description Requires Pydantic BaseModel Pydantic v2 models with model_json_schema() Pydantic v2 dataclass Standard library @dataclass Pydantic v2 (for TypeAdapter) Pydantic dataclass @pydantic.dataclasses.dataclass Pydantic v2 TypedDict typing.TypedDict subclasses Pydantic v2 (for TypeAdapter) dict Dict containing JSON Schema or OpenAPI spec -

Pydantic v2 Required

All Python type inputs (except raw dict) require Pydantic v2 runtime to convert to JSON Schema.

items.title: Pydantic BaseModel
items.text:
mymodule.py 

from pydantic import BaseModel


class User(BaseModel):
    name: str
    age: int


datamodel-codegen --input-model ./mymodule.py:User --output model.py

✨ Generated model.py 

from __future__ import annotations

from pydantic import BaseModel


class User(BaseModel):
    name: str
    age: int

items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input-model ./mymodule.py:User --output-model-type typing.TypedDict --output model.py

✨ Generated model.py 

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TypedDict


class User(TypedDict):
    name: str
    age: int

items.text:
mymodule.py

@dataclass
class User:
    name: str

datamodel-codegen --input-model ./mymodule.py:User --output model.py

✨ Generated model.py 

from __future__ import annotations

class User(BaseModel):
    name: str
    age: int

items.title: TypedDict
items.text:
mymodule.py 

from typing import TypedDict


class User(TypedDict):
    name: str

datamodel-codegen --input-model ./mymodule.py:User --output model.py

✨ Generated model.py

class User(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(..., title="Name")
    age: int = Field(..., title="Age")

items.title: Dict Schema (JSON Schema)
items.text:
mymodule.py 

USER_SCHEMA = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "name": {"type": "string"},
        "age": {"type": "integer"},
    },
    "required": ["name", "age"],
}


datamodel-codegen --input-model ./mymodule.py:USER_SCHEMA --input-file-type jsonschema --output model.py

✨ Generated model.py 

from __future__ import annotations

from pydantic import BaseModel


class Model(BaseModel):
    name: str
    age: int

Dict requires --input-file-type

When using a dict schema, you must specify --input-file-type (e.g., jsonschema, openapi).

items.title: Dict Schema (OpenAPI)
items.text:
mymodule.py 

OPENAPI_SPEC = {
    "openapi": "3.0.0",
    "info": {"title": "API", "version": "1.0.0"},
    "paths": {},
    "components": {
        "schemas": {
            "User": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "name": {"type": "string"},
                    "age": {"type": "integer"},
                },
            }
        }
    },
}


datamodel-codegen --input-model ./mymodule.py:OPENAPI_SPEC --input-file-type openapi --output model.py

✨ Generated model.py 

from __future__ import annotations

from pydantic import BaseModel


class User(BaseModel):
    name: str | None = None
    age: int | None = None

items.title: Custom Python Types with x-python-type
items.text: When using x-python-type in JSON Schema (via WithJsonSchema in Pydantic), the generator automatically resolves and generates the required imports.

items.title: Automatic Import Resolution
items.text:
The generator supports many common Python types out of the box:

Module Supported Types typing Any, Union, Optional, Literal, Final, ClassVar, Annotated, TypeVar, TypeAlias, Never, NoReturn, Self, LiteralString, TypeGuard, Type collections defaultdict, OrderedDict, Counter, deque, ChainMap collections.abc Callable, Iterable, Iterator, Generator, Awaitable, Coroutine, AsyncIterable, AsyncIterator, AsyncGenerator, Mapping, MutableMapping, Sequence, MutableSequence, Set, MutableSet, Collection, Reversible pathlib Path, PurePath decimal Decimal uuid UUID datetime datetime, date, time, timedelta enum Enum, IntEnum, StrEnum, Flag, IntFlag re Pattern, Match

For types not in this list, the generator dynamically searches common modules to resolve imports.

items.title: Example
items.text:
mymodule.py 

from collections import defaultdict
from typing import Any, Annotated
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, WithJsonSchema


class Config(BaseModel):
    data: (
        Annotated[
            defaultdict[str, Annotated[dict[str, Any], Field(default_factory=dict)]],
            WithJsonSchema({"type": "object", "x-python-type": "defaultdict[str, dict[str, Any]]"}),
        ]
        | None
    ) = None


datamodel-codegen --input-model ./mymodule.py:Config --output-model-type typing.TypedDict

✨ Generated output 

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from typing import Any, TypedDict

from typing_extensions import NotRequired


class Config(TypedDict):
    data: NotRequired[defaultdict[str, dict[str, Any]] | None]

Fully Qualified Paths

You can also use fully qualified paths in x-python-type (e.g., collections.defaultdict), which are always resolved correctly regardless of the static mapping. A dotted value of a Literal of three names or more, such as Literal[http.HTTPStatus.OK], is a member, such as an enum member, of what the names before it import: from http import HTTPStatus and HTTPStatus.OK, or the submodule client of Literal[http.client.OK]. A msgspec Literal holds only None, bool, int and str values, so msgspec cannot decode an enum member there, an IntEnum member included, while it decodes a plain constant such as Literal[http.client.HTTP_PORT]. msgspec.Struct output warns about an enum member that --input-model or x-python-import symbols transport, and conditionally about a dotted value, which may be either.

items.title: Mutual Exclusion
items.text:
--input-model cannot be used with:

  • --input (file input)
  • --url (URL input)
  • --watch (file watching)

items.title: Supported Python Model Features
items.text: Input type Generation behavior Pydantic v2 BaseModel Uses model_json_schema() Standard dataclasses Uses Pydantic TypeAdapter to derive schema Pydantic dataclasses Uses Pydantic schema support TypedDict Uses Pydantic TypeAdapter to derive schema Dict schemas Treated as JSON Schema or OpenAPI based on --input-file-type

items.title: Limitations
items.text: Python model input imports and evaluates the specified object, so the target module must be importable and safe to import in your environment. Raw dict input requires --input-file-type because the generator cannot infer whether the dict is JSON Schema, OpenAPI, or another schema profile.

items.title: 📖 See Also
items.text:
• 🚀 Getting Started - Installation and first model
  • 🖥️ CLI Reference - Complete CLI options reference
  • 📁 CLI Reference: Base Options - --input-model option details
  • 📋 Generate from JSON Schema - JSON Schema input documentation

items.title: Python Version Compatibility
items.text: datamodel-code-generator can generate code compatible with different Python versions. This page explains how to control type annotation syntax and imports for your target environment.

items.title: Quick Overview
items.text: Option Description --target-python-version Set the minimum Python version for generated code --use-union-operator Use X \| Y instead of Union[X, Y] --use-standard-collections Use list, dict instead of List, Dict --use-annotated Use Annotated for field metadata --use-generic-container-types Use Sequence, Mapping instead of list, dict --disable-future-imports Don't add from __future__ import annotations

items.title: --target-python-version
items.text:
Sets the minimum Python version for the generated code. This automatically adjusts type annotation syntax.

Version Union Syntax Collection Syntax Notes 3.10 X \| Y list[T], dict[K, V] Union operator available 3.11 X \| Y list[T], dict[K, V] Self type available 3.12 X \| Y list[T], dict[K, V] type statement available 3.13 X \| Y list[T], dict[K, V] ReadOnly TypedDict keys imported from typing 3.14 X \| Y list[T], dict[K, V] Native deferred annotations: from __future__ import annotations only where the output model needs it for forward references 3.15 X \| Y list[T], dict[K, V] TypedDict with closed/extra_items (PEP 728) imported from typing; frozendict builtin

items.title: Example: Python 3.10+
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output models.py \
  --target-python-version 3.10

class User(BaseModel):
    id: int
    tags: list[str]
    metadata: str | int | None = None

items.title: --use-union-operator
items.text: Uses the | operator for union types instead of Union[X, Y].

items.title: Without --use-union-operator
items.text:
from typing import Union, Optional


class Item(BaseModel):
    value: Union[str, int]
    label: Optional[str] = None  # Same as Union[str, None]

items.title: With --use-union-operator
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output models.py --use-union-operator

class Item(BaseModel):
    value: str | int
    label: str | None = None

items.title: Compatibility Note
items.text: The union operator | requires: - Python 3.10+ at runtime, OR - from __future__ import annotations (Python 3.7+) for postponed evaluation

items.title: --use-standard-collections
items.text: Uses built-in collection types instead of typing module generics.

items.title: Without --use-standard-collections
items.text:
from typing import List, Dict, Set, Tuple


class Data(BaseModel):
    items: List[str]
    mapping: Dict[str, int]
    unique: Set[str]
    pair: Tuple[str, int]

items.title: With --use-standard-collections
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output models.py --use-standard-collections

class Data(BaseModel):
    items: list[str]
    mapping: dict[str, int]
    unique: set[str]
    pair: tuple[str, int]

items.title: Compatibility Note
items.text: Built-in generic syntax requires: - Python 3.10+ at runtime, OR - from __future__ import annotations

items.title: --use-annotated
items.text: Uses typing.Annotated to attach metadata to types, which is the modern approach for Pydantic v2.

items.title: Without --use-annotated
items.text:
from pydantic import Field


class User(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=100)
    age: int = Field(..., ge=0, le=150)

items.title: With --use-annotated
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output models.py --use-annotated

from typing import Annotated
from pydantic import Field


class User(BaseModel):
    name: Annotated[str, Field(min_length=1, max_length=100)]
    age: Annotated[int, Field(ge=0, le=150)]

items.title: Benefits
items.text:
• Cleaner separation of type and constraints
  • Better IDE support
  • More compatible with other tools that understand Annotated
  • Required types are more explicit

items.title: --use-generic-container-types
items.text:
Uses abstract container types (Sequence, Mapping, FrozenSet) instead of concrete types (list, dict, set).

datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output models.py --use-generic-container-types

from typing import Mapping, Sequence


class Data(BaseModel):
    items: Sequence[str]
    mapping: Mapping[str, int]

If --use-standard-collections is also set, imports from collections.abc instead of typing.

This is useful when: - You want to use abstract types for better type flexibility - Maintaining compatibility with interfaces that accept any sequence/mapping

items.title: --disable-future-imports
items.text: Prevents adding from __future__ import annotations to generated files.

items.title: Default behavior (with future imports)
items.text:
from __future__ import annotations


class User(BaseModel):
    friends: list[User]  # Forward reference works due to PEP 563

items.title: With --disable-future-imports
items.text:
datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output models.py --disable-future-imports

from typing import List, TYPE_CHECKING

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from typing import ForwardRef


class User(BaseModel):
    friends: List["User"]  # String forward reference

items.title: When to disable
items.text:
• Compatibility with runtime annotation inspection
  • Libraries that don't support __future__.annotations
  • When using get_type_hints() at runtime

items.title: Pattern 1: Modern Python (3.10+)
items.text:
For projects targeting Python 3.10 or later:

datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output models.py \
  --target-python-version 3.10 \
  --use-union-operator \
  --use-standard-collections \
  --use-annotated

Output: 

from typing import Annotated
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class User(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: Annotated[str, Field(min_length=1)]
    tags: list[str]
    metadata: dict[str, str] | None = None

items.title: Pattern 2: Minimum Supported Python (3.10)
items.text:
For projects targeting Python 3.10 (minimum supported version):

datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output models.py \
  --target-python-version 3.10

Output: 

class User(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    tags: list[str]
    metadata: dict[str, str] | None = None

items.title: Pattern 3: Maximum compatibility
items.text:
For libraries that need to work across multiple Python versions (3.10+):

datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output models.py \
  --target-python-version 3.10

The generator will use modern Python 3.10+ syntax including union operators and built-in generic types.

items.title: Pattern 4: CI/CD consistency
items.text:
Pin the Python version in pyproject.toml to ensure consistent output:

[tool.datamodel-codegen]
target-python-version = "3.10"
use-union-operator = true
use-standard-collections = true
use-annotated = true

items.title: Version Feature Matrix
items.text:
Feature 3.10 3.11 3.12 3.13 3.14 3.15 list[T] syntax native native native native native native X \| Y union native native native native native native Annotated native native native native native native TypeAlias native native native native native native Self typing_extensions native native native native native type statement N/A N/A native native native native TypedDict NotRequired typing_extensions native native native native native TypedDict ReadOnly typing_extensions typing_extensions typing_extensions native native native TypedDict closed/extra_items (PEP 728) typing_extensions typing_extensions typing_extensions typing_extensions typing_extensions native Deferred annotations __future__ import __future__ import __future__ import __future__ import native (__future__ import where needed) native (__future__ import where needed) frozendict in x-python-type N/A N/A N/A N/A N/A native TypeForm, NoExtraItems, disjoint_base in x-python-type typing_extensions typing_extensions typing_extensions typing_extensions typing_extensions native

A standard-library type named by --type-overrides, customTypePath or x-python-import follows the same rules as x-python-type: a typing or collections.abc name newer than the target is imported from typing_extensions, and a type that the target does not have, such as enum.StrEnum for 3.10 or pathlib.DirEntryInfo for 3.15, stops the generation with <type> is unavailable for target Python <version>. These types are checked only where the output imports them, after --import-overrides, so an override that no model uses, or a customTypePath that an override replaces, is left alone, and --import-overrides can move such an import to a backport module, as --import-overrides '{"StrEnum": "backports.strenum"}' does for enum.StrEnum on 3.10.

items.title: TypeError: 'type' object is not subscriptable
items.text:
This occurs when using list[T] syntax on older Python versions without __future__ imports.

Solution: Ensure you are running Python 3.10+ or use from __future__ import annotations.

items.title: Pydantic validation fails with forward references
items.text:
This can happen when __future__.annotations interacts poorly with Pydantic's type resolution.

Solution: Try --disable-future-imports or update to Pydantic v2.

items.title: Python 3.13 DeprecationWarning with typing._eval_type
items.text:
When running on Python 3.13+ with from __future__ import annotations, you may see:

DeprecationWarning: Failing to pass a value to the 'type_params' parameter
of 'typing._eval_type' is deprecated...

This occurs because Python 3.13 deprecated calling typing._eval_type() without the type_params parameter. Libraries that evaluate forward references (like older Pydantic versions) trigger this warning.

Solutions:

  1. Upgrade Pydantic (recommended):

  2. Pydantic v2: Upgrade to the latest version

  3. Use --disable-future-imports as a workaround: 

    datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output models.py --disable-future-imports

  4. Suppress the warning in pytest (temporary fix): 

    # pyproject.toml
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
filterwarnings = [
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning:pydantic.typing",
]

Note

Targets of Python 3.14 or later use native deferred annotations (PEP 649). The generator still adds from __future__ import annotations when the output model needs explicit deferred annotations for forward references or types hidden by same-named fields.

items.title: IDE shows type errors
items.text:
Some IDEs don't fully understand from __future__ import annotations.

Solution: Configure your IDE's Python version or use explicit type syntax matching your runtime version.

items.title: Option recommendations
items.text:
Analyse a schema and get the datamodel-codegen options that suit it, starting from the latest dated preset.

Experimental

--recommend-options, its rules, the report, and its JSON payload are experimental and may change as the rules are calibrated on more schemas.

A preset is a good general starting point, but some choices depend on the shape of your schema: how inline models should be named, whether titles make good class names, whether inline enums should become Literal types, or whether repeated inline objects should be reused. --recommend-options reads your schema, measures the signals that drive these choices, generates the candidate configurations in memory to compare the class names they give your schema, and prints:

  • the latest dated preset to start from,
  • the options to add on top of it, each with the rule that chose it, the reason with counts from your schema, caveats, the effect measured on public schemas, and the class names it changes in your schema (before -> after),
  • options worth considering when the schema has signals for and against them,
  • optional validation and policy options, such as --strict-types, which stay out of the command because they depend on what your project accepts,
  • the compared candidates and the class names that change from your current configuration,
  • where your existing configuration differs from the rules,
  • a ready command and a pyproject.toml block.

items.title: Run it
items.text:
Add --recommend-options to the command you would use to generate models:

datamodel-codegen --input openapi.yaml --input-file-type openapi --recommend-options

Pass the options you have already decided on, such as --output-model-type and --target-python-version, so the recommendation starts from the matching preset. When they are in pyproject.toml, run the command from the project directory; --profile NAME and a single --job NAME select a profile or a job as they do for generation.

The command prints the report and exits. It does not write files or change your configuration.

To compare names in the layout you generate, pass --output as you would for generation: a file path selects one module, a directory a package. Nothing is written there. Generating every candidate takes about as long as generating your models once per candidate, so a schema estimated above 3000 models gets the rules only, and the notes give the command that compares the candidates anyway (see How candidates are compared).

items.title: When generation suggests it
items.text:
When many generated classes are numbered collisions, a command line generation ends with a NamingHintWarning (experimental) that points here:

NamingHintWarning: 11 of 24 class names are numbered collisions (Metadata1...Metadata11). Add --recommend-options to this command to see naming options for this schema (experimental).

A class name is a numbered collision when datamodel-codegen added the number because the name without it was taken, such as Metadata1 beside Metadata, or Status1 when --collapse-root-models keeps a Status root model's name without generating a class for it. Digits from the schema, such as Level1 and Level2, and the suffix of --duplicate-name-suffix do not count. The hint needs at least 10 numbered collisions that make at least one in five classes, and the example is the largest family of them. A command shows it at most once, also when watch = true in pyproject.toml regenerates the models, and only when --recommend-options accepts the command: not with --watch, --all-jobs, or more than one --job.

It is left out when you already chose how classes are named, with --naming-strategy, --model-name-map, or the deprecated --parent-scoped-naming, on the command line or in pyproject.toml (naming-strategy = "numbered" keeps the numbered names without the hint), and with --check, --diff-against, --output-format json, and --disable-warnings. When warnings are turned into errors, the hint is dropped and the run goes on. generate() never shows it. The hint never changes the generated files, the result of --check, or the exit code.

items.title: Read the report
items.text:
For example, for this schema (titled_variants.yaml):

openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Travel API
  version: 1.0.0
paths: {}
components:
  schemas:
    Booking:
      type: object
      properties:
        passenger:
          type: string
        payment:
          oneOf:
            - title: Card
              type: object
              properties:
                object:
                  const: card
                number:
                  type: string
            - title: Bank Account
              type: object
              properties:
                object:
                  const: bank_account
                iban:
                  type: string
    Trip:
      type: object
      properties:
        origin:
          type: string
        destination:
          type: string

datamodel-codegen --input titled_variants.yaml --target-python-version 3.14 --recommend-options prints:
