items.title: --update-lock
items.text:
Create or atomically update the selected remote lock after generation (experimental).

--update-lock creates or refreshes the selected --lockfile from every remote resource reached during this run. It conflicts with --locked.

Remote reference lock support is experimental: its lock document schema and request-identity compatibility may evolve. It remains fail-closed on integrity mismatches, and it never persists credentials.

The lock stores opaque SHA-256 request-identity digests and SHA-256 body digests, never response bodies or request values directly. Each saved display origin contains only the scheme, host, and explicit port—never a path, query, or request headers. A request identity includes its scheme, host, explicit port, path, header names, and ordered query parameter names only. If one generation receives different bodies for the same path and query-name identity, it fails closed rather than sharing a lock entry.

Related: --http-local-ref-path, --lockfile, --url

Option relationships:

  • Conflicts: --locked

Usage

datamodel-codegen --url https://api.example.com/schema.json --update-lock --lockfile datamodel-codegen.lock # (1)!

Set debounce delay in seconds for watch mode.

The --watch-delay option configures the debounce interval (default: 0.5 seconds) for watch mode. This prevents multiple regenerations when files are rapidly modified in succession. The delay ensures that after the last file change, the generator waits the specified time before regenerating.

from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing_extensions import TypeAliasType

Boolean = TypeAliasType("Boolean", bool)

The `Boolean` scalar type represents `true` or `false`.
"""


ID = TypeAliasType("ID", str)
"""
The `ID` scalar type represents a unique identifier, often used to refetch an object or as key for a cache. The ID type appears in a JSON response as a String; however, it is not intended to be human-readable. When expected as an input type, any string (such as `"4"`) or integer (such as `4`) input value will be accepted as an ID.
"""


String = TypeAliasType("String", str)
"""
The `String` scalar type represents textual data, represented as UTF-8 character sequences. The String type is most often used by GraphQL to represent free-form human-readable text.
"""


class Node(BaseModel):
    id: ID

    title: String | None = None

items.title: --base-class-map
items.text:
Specify different base classes for specific models via JSON mapping.

The --base-class-map option allows you to assign different base classes to specific models. This is useful when you want selective base class inheritance, for example, applying custom base classes only to specific models while leaving others with the default BaseModel.

Priority: --base-class-map > customBasePath (schema extension) > --base-class

You can specify either a single base class as a string, or multiple base classes (mixins) as a list:

  • Single: {"Person": "custom.bases.PersonBase"}
  • Multiple: {"User": ["mixins.AuditMixin", "mixins.TimestampMixin"]}

You can pass the mapping either inline as JSON or as a path to a JSON file.

When using multiple base classes, the specified classes are used directly without adding BaseModel. Ensure your mixins inherit from BaseModel if needed.

Related: --base-class

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input base_class_map.json --base-class-map '{"Person": "custom.bases.PersonBase", "Animal": "custom.bases.AnimalBase"}' # (1)!
  1. --base-class-map - the option documented here

      }
    },

      }
    }

items.title: --keep-field-defaults-off-branch-roots
items.text:
Leave a property's default off the root models extracted from its anyOf or oneOf branches.

Under --field-constraints or --use-annotated a branch with constraints, such as {type: number, minimum: 0} in the anyOf of a property with default: null, becomes a root model of its own. Without the option that root takes the property's default, as in 0.86.0: root: float = Field(None, ge=0.0), so the model builds without a value and holds a default its type rejects. With --keep-field-defaults-off-branch-roots the default stays with the property, and the root requires its value: root: float = Field(..., ge=0.0).

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input extracted_branch_default.yaml --field-constraints --keep-field-defaults-off-branch-roots # (1)!
  1. --keep-field-defaults-off-branch-roots - the option documented here

items.title: --keep-model-order
items.text:
Keep generated model order deterministic while respecting dependency constraints.

The --keep-model-order flag produces a stable, deterministic output order. The generator starts from class-name order and only moves models when required to satisfy dependency or runtime constraints (for example, a base class must appear before its subclass, and cyclic groups must stay together).

This option is not equivalent to preserving the raw definition order from the input schema, and it does not guarantee a strict unconditional alphabetical order either. Inheritance and other runtime ordering requirements can force a non-alphabetical arrangement. The value of the flag is that repeated runs on the same schema produce the same ordering, which keeps diffs stable.

Related: --collapse-root-models

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input inheritance_forward_ref.json --keep-model-order # (1)!

items.title: --model-name-map
items.text:
Rename generated model classes from a JSON mapping.

The --model-name-map option applies explicit class names to generated models. Mapping keys can be canonical schema refs such as #/definitions/Foo or the current generated class name such as Foo1. Values are final Python class names.

This is useful when a schema cannot be edited but generated model names must be stable for public APIs or downstream code. Colliding mapped names fail instead of being silently suffixed. Keys that match no model, such as a misspelled key, are reported in a warning. GraphQL input does not apply --model-name-map, so every key is reported there.

Related: --naming-strategy, --use-title-as-name

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input model_name_map.json --model-name-map '{"#/definitions/Foo": "RenamedFoo", "Bar": "RenamedBar", "model-name": "OriginalMapped"}' # (1)!
  1. --model-name-map - the option documented here

{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "item": {
      "$ref": "#/definitions/Foo"
    },
    "related": {
      "$ref": "#/definitions/Bar"
    },
    "original": {
      "$ref": "#/definitions/model-name"
    }
  },
  "definitions": {
    "Foo": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "value": {
          "type": "string"
        }
      }
    },
    "Bar": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "foo": {
          "$ref": "#/definitions/Foo"
        }
      }
    },
    "model-name": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "bar": {
          "$ref": "#/definitions/Bar"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

items.title: --naming-strategy
items.text:
Use parent-prefixed naming strategy for duplicate model names.

The --naming-strategy parent-prefixed flag prefixes model names with their parent model name when duplicates occur. For example, if both Order and Cart have an inline Item definition, they become OrderItem and CartItem.

Generated clients and servers (experimental) follow the same rules for their method, argument, module, and class names, with the resource or router group as the parent of a method and the method as the parent of an argument; under primary-first, a primary name is one the root document declares.

Related: --duplicate-name-suffix, --parent-scoped-naming

items.title: --omit-redundant-reference-null
items.text:
Do not write None again at a reference to a model that holds null itself.

When a field, an array item, a map value or a union member references a schema that admits null, the reference writes | None beside the model. A root model whose type admits None, a type alias whose type admits None and an enum with a None member hold that null themselves, so with this option the reference writes the model alone and a null parses to the model (Name(root=None) instead of None). An object model, and an enum without a None member, cannot hold null and keep the | None; so does a None the reference writes itself, such as anyOf: [{$ref}, {type: null}] or an optional field's default.

items.title: --order-constructor-fields-by-final-names
items.text:
Order the constructor fields of dataclass and msgspec.Struct models by final field names.

The --order-constructor-fields-by-final-names flag only applies to output models that can mark fields keyword-only (dataclasses.dataclass, pydantic_v2.dataclass and msgspec.Struct); other output model types ignore it.

A field that is renamed because it is named like its type, such as Bar: Bar, is renamed in every class of its family. Without the flag the order of a class's constructor fields is decided while its module is processed, where the inherited field may not be renamed yet: a subclass that overrides it as a required field then reads as a new field after the inherited default, and is written keyword-only (kw_only=True), which moves it behind the positional fields and changes the first positional argument of the constructor. With the flag the order is decided once every field has its final name, so the override takes the place of the inherited field and stays positional.

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input field_type_collision_inherited_modules --output-model-type pydantic_v2.dataclass --target-python-version 3.11 --order-constructor-fields-by-final-names # (1)!

items.title: --order-constructor-fields-by-written-defaults
items.text:
Order the fields of msgspec.Struct models by the defaults they write.

The --order-constructor-fields-by-written-defaults flag only changes msgspec.Struct output under --strip-default-none; other output model types and runs without --strip-default-none ignore it.

A Struct writes a default for every optional field: UNSET, or None when the type admits None, even where --strip-default-none strips the field's None default. Without the flag such a field keeps its schema place among the required fields, the order of earlier releases, and the struct is reordered only when a required field would then follow a default (which the Struct rejects at import). With the flag every optional field goes after the required fields, in schema order, which changes the order of the constructor's positional arguments.

items.title: --pin-aliases-with-alias-generator
items.text:
Decide a field's alias by the alias generator its model applies.

The --pin-aliases-with-alias-generator flag only applies to --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel and pydantic_v2.dataclass; other output model types ignore it.

Pydantic applies the alias_generator in the config of a model, and a subclass applies the one in the config of its base. Without the flag the generated aliases are decided from the generator of the whole run (--alias-generator or the template data key alias_generator) even where the model does not apply it, a dataclass renders none, and the alias_generator in the config of a model, of its base or of a dataclass is not read. A field may then lose the alias that carries the document's property name, or keep an alias the generator already produces.

With the flag the aliases follow the generator the model applies: the one in its config or in the config it inherits, none for alias_generator: null, and none for a dataclass whose config names none. For a --target-pydantic-version older than 2.8, whose generator algorithms can differ from the ones dcg runs, the generated alias is written on every field of a dataclass whose config names a generator, as it is for a BaseModel.

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input alias_generator.json --output-model-type pydantic_v2.dataclass --snake-case-field --pin-aliases-with-alias-generator --extra-template-data jsonschema/extra_data_alias_generator.json --target-pydantic-version 2 # (1)!

items.title: --read-nullable-beside-type-list
items.text:
Write the null that nullable: true declares beside a type list into the root model.

A schema whose type list holds an object and another type is generated as a model of its properties and a root model of the union of the types. Under --strict-nullable or --use-missing-sentinel its fields write the null their schema declares, and so does that root model for a type list holding "null". Without the option the root model ignores nullable: true and rejects null, as in 0.86.0; with --read-nullable-beside-type-list it admits None as the type list holding "null" does.

The --strict-nullable flag ensures that fields with default values are generated with their exact schema type (non-nullable), rather than being made nullable.

items.title: --strip-default-none
items.text:
Remove fields with None as default value from generated models.

The --strip-default-none option removes fields that have None as their default value from the generated models. This results in cleaner model definitions by excluding optional fields that default to None.

The option has no effect on msgspec.Struct output. A Struct defaults an omitted field to UNSET, not None, so there is no None default to strip. Only a field that nullable: true makes nullable under --strict-nullable defaults to None, and that default stays, as the field's type admits None.

items.title: --tag-msgspec-by-payload-name
items.text:
Tag the structs of a msgspec discriminated union with the property name of the document.

The --tag-msgspec-by-payload-name flag only applies to --output-model-type msgspec.Struct; other output model types ignore it.

msgspec reads the tag from the payload under tag_field. Without the flag, the structs whose discriminator is a single literal take the Python name the property resolves to: a property named pet-kind is tagged by pet_kind, which msgspec looks for in the payload instead, so the union decodes nothing. With the flag, tag_field is the property name the document carries (pet-kind). --use-msgspec-tagged-unions tags by the document's property name too.

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input discriminator_msgspec_wire_name.json --tag-msgspec-by-payload-name --output-model-type msgspec.Struct # (1)!
  1. --tag-msgspec-by-payload-name - the option documented here
Examples

Input Schema:

{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$defs": {
    "Cat": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "pet-kind": {
          "const": "cat"
        },
        "name": {
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "pet-kind"
      ]
    },
    "Dog": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "pet-kind": {
          "const": "dog"
        },
        "bark": {
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "pet-kind"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "Model",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "pet": {
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Cat"
        },
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Dog"
        }
      ],
      "discriminator": {
        "propertyName": "pet-kind"
      }
    }
  }
}

items.title: --target-pydantic-version
items.text:
Target Pydantic version for generated code compatibility.

The --target-pydantic-version flag chooses the oldest Pydantic the generated code must run on. Output never depends on the Pydantic installed with datamodel-code-generator.

  • unset: the newest supported feature forms, the same as 2.12; config key naming is unchanged and keeps populate_by_name=True like 2, and --use-missing-sentinel keeps the experimental MISSING import
  • 2: Pydantic 2.0.3+ compatible forms, such as populate_by_name=True, Field(...) string constraints, json_schema_extra for deprecated fields, and dictionary-key models defined first
  • 2.11: Pydantic 2.11+ forms, such as validate_by_name=True, StringConstraints, Field(deprecated=True), and TypeAliasType dataclass aliases
  • 2.12: The 2.11 forms plus features that require Pydantic 2.12+, such as --use-missing-sentinel
  • 2.14: The 2.12 forms, with --use-missing-sentinel importing MISSING from pydantic instead of the pydantic.experimental.missing_sentinel path that Pydantic 2.14 deprecates, Python's regex engine for bytes patterns the Rust engine rejects, which Pydantic compiles from 2.14 on, and required pydantic_v2.dataclass fields written as = Field(...) placed before the fields with defaults of the same class, the order inspect.signature needs on Pydantic 2.13+

Constructs that have no older form, such as regex_engine or a type statement, are written for every target; when the target is older than the release they need, the generation warns once with that release.

See Output Model Types for every affected form.

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input person.json --target-pydantic-version 2.11 --allow-population-by-field-name --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel # (1)!
  1. --target-pydantic-version - the option documented here
Examples

Input Schema:

{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "title": "Person",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "firstName": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The person's first name."
    },
    "lastName": {
      "type": ["string", "null"],
      "description": "The person's last name."
    },
    "age": {
      "description": "Age in years which must be equal to or greater than zero.",
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0
    },
    "friends": {
      "type": "array"
    },
    "comment": {
      "type": "null"
    }
  }
}

items.title: --target-python-version
items.text:
Target Python version for generated code syntax and imports.

The --target-python-version flag controls Python version-specific syntax:

  • Python 3.10-3.11: Uses X | None union operator, TypeAlias annotation
  • Python 3.12+: Uses type statement for type aliases
  • Python 3.13+: Imports ReadOnly for read-only TypedDict keys from typing
  • Python 3.14+: Native deferred annotations; from __future__ import annotations only when needed
  • Python 3.15+: Imports TypedDict with closed and extra_items (PEP 728) from typing

This affects import statements and type annotation syntax in generated code.

See also: CI/CD Integration, Output Model Types, Python Version Compatibility, Root Models and Type Aliases

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input person.json --target-python-version 3.10 --use-standard-collections # (1)!

items.title: --union-mode
items.text:
Union mode for combining anyOf/oneOf schemas (smart or left_to_right).

The --union-mode flag sets Pydantic's union_mode on generated union fields. Discriminated unions are not given a union_mode: Pydantic validates them by their discriminator tag, a separate mode that cannot be combined with smart or left_to_right.

Option relationships:

  • Requires: --output-model-type = pydantic_v2.BaseModel - --union-mode is only supported for --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel.

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input combine_any_of_object.json --union-mode left_to_right --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel # (1)!
  1. --union-mode - the option documented here
Examples

{
    "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#",
    "type": "object",
    "title": "My schema",

    "properties": {
        "AddressLine1": { "type": "string" },
        "AddressLine2": { "type": "string" },
        "City":         { "type": "string" }
    },
    "required": [ "AddressLine1" ],
    "anyOf": [
        {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "State":   { "type": "string" },
                "ZipCode": { "type": "string" }
            },
            "required": [ "ZipCode" ]
        },
        {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "County":   { "type": "string" },
                "PostCode": { "type": "string" }
            },
            "required": [ "PostCode" ]

            "type": "object",
            "properties": {

items.title: --use-default
items.text:

The --use-default flag allows required fields with default values to be generated with their defaults, making them optional to provide when instantiating the model.

When --strict-nullable is enabled, the field type still follows the schema's nullability. For example, a required string field with a default is generated as str = 'value', not str | None = 'value', unless the schema allows null.

items.title: --use-default-factory-for-optional-nested-models
items.text:
Generate default_factory for optional nested model fields.

The --use-default-factory-for-optional-nested-models flag generates default_factory for optional nested model fields instead of None default: - Dataclasses: field: Model | None = field(default_factory=Model) - Pydantic: field: Model | None = Field(default_factory=Model) - msgspec: field: Model | UnsetType = field(default_factory=Model)

When a built-in generated child has required constructor fields, including inherited fields, the field keeps its usual None or UNSET default. The child's required fields remain required. With --strip-default-none, the usual omission behavior can instead require the parent field to be supplied explicitly. Existing defaults enabled by --use-default and fields excluded from the constructor are respected. Custom root templates, decorators, and opaque base classes keep their existing factory behavior. Constructors and validators are not executed to determine whether a factory is usable.

items.title: --use-msgspec-nullable-enum-alias
items.text:
Write a msgspec.Struct enum that lists null as an Enum and a nullable alias.

The --use-msgspec-nullable-enum-alias flag only applies to --output-model-type msgspec.Struct; other output model types ignore it. Client generation (--generate-client) with msgspec.Struct models requires it.

Without the flag the output keeps the 0.83.0 form of an enum that lists null without type: string or nullable: true, such as type: [integer, "null"] with enum: [1, 2, null]: an Enum class with a None member such as NoneType_None = None. msgspec cannot decode such an Enum, because its members must be all str or all int values. An enum whose class has a value type base, the IntEnum of type: integer or a --use-subclass-enum class such as (int, Enum), cannot hold a None member, so without the flag it is written without it, and without None as its one type rejects null.

With the flag the enum is written as a type: string or nullable enum is: an Enum class with an Enum suffix and without the None member, and the schema name becomes a type alias of that class or None, so that msgspec decodes the members and null. Code that used Size.int_1 or Size.NoneType_None uses SizeEnum.int_1 and None instead. The default of a field of the enum is then its raw value, also with --set-default-enum-member, and an enum that lists only null becomes the alias None.

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input msgspec_nullable_enum_31.yaml --use-msgspec-nullable-enum-alias --output-model-type msgspec.Struct # (1)!
  1. --use-msgspec-nullable-enum-alias - the option documented here

  schemas:

      type: [string, "null"]
      enum: [red, green, null]
    Size:
      type: [integer, "null"]
      enum: [1, 2, null]
      default: 1
    Pet:
      type: object
      required: [name, color]
      properties:
        name: {type: string}
        color: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Color"}
        size: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Size"}
        sizes: {type: array, items: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Size"}}

items.title: --use-msgspec-tagged-unions
items.text:
Write a msgspec.Struct discriminated union as tagged structs as a whole.

The --use-msgspec-tagged-unions flag only applies to --output-model-type msgspec.Struct; other output model types ignore it. Client generation (--generate-client) with msgspec.Struct models requires it.

Without the flag the output keeps the 0.83.0 form. A variant gets tag_field/tag only when its discriminator property is a single literal (such as a const) equal to the discriminator value, or when a second discriminated union uses the variant, and such a tag names the generated field, which differs from the property name when the field is renamed. Any other variant, whose value comes from the discriminator mapping, an enum or the schema name, keeps the discriminator as a Literal field: Cat(petType='cat') and cat.petType work and Cat decodes alone, but msgspec raises TypeError for the union Cat | Dog, because it only decodes unions of tagged structs.

With the flag a union is tagged as a whole: every variant gets the property name of the document as tag_field and its value as tag, so the union decodes. msgspec does not allow a field named like tag_field, so the discriminator is then neither a field nor a constructor argument: Cat(petType='cat') raises TypeError, cat.petType raises AttributeError, and Cat decoded alone accepts a payload without petType.

When a variant cannot take exactly one tag for the union, or a base or derived struct of a variant keeps the property as a field, the union tags none of its variants and a warning names the reason: its variants keep Literal fields, the ones with a const included. A variant that another union tags keeps that tag.

items.title: --use-root-model-sequence-interface
items.text:
Make non-null sequence-like Pydantic v2 RootModel classes implement collections.abc.Sequence.

When enabled, a RootModel whose root is list[T] or Sequence[T] inherits from Sequence[T] and includes iter, getitem, and len methods that delegate to the wrapped root value. Scalar, optional, nullable, and RootModel type-alias outputs are unchanged.

This makes generated RootModel wrappers convenient to use anywhere a typed sequence is expected, without unpacking .root at every call site:

from collections.abc import Sequence

pets = Pets(root=[Pet(name="dog")])

first_pet: Pet = pets[0]
selected_pets: list[Pet] = pets[:1]
pet_names = [pet.name for pet in pets]


def render_pet_names(pets: Sequence[Pet]) -> list[str]:
    return [pet.name for pet in pets]


render_pet_names(pets)

When used with --custom-template-dir, a custom pydantic_v2/RootModel.jinja2 template must render both sequence_base_class and the helper methods using sequence_item_type and sequence_slice_type. If the custom RootModel template does not render the sequence base class and helper methods, generation fails with an error instead of silently ignoring this option.

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input root_model_sequence_interface.json --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel --use-root-model-sequence-interface --class-name Pets # (1)!

    "$ref": "#/definitions/Pet"
  },

    "Pet": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": [
        "name"
      ],
      "properties": {
        "name": {
          "type": "string"
        }
      }
    }
  }

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterator, Sequence
from typing import SupportsIndex, overload

from pydantic import BaseModel, RootModel


class Pet(BaseModel):
    name: str


class Pets(RootModel[list[Pet]], Sequence[Pet]):
    root: list[Pet]

    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[Pet]:
        return iter(self.root)

    @overload
    def __getitem__(self, index: SupportsIndex) -> Pet:
        pass

    @overload
    def __getitem__(self, index: slice) -> list[Pet]:
        pass

    def __getitem__(self, index: SupportsIndex | slice) -> Pet | list[Pet]:
        return self.root[index]

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.root)

items.title: --dedupe-request-response-variants
items.text:
Decide Request/Response variants from the schema graph and build each inline model once.

Under --read-only-write-only-model-type (request-response or all), the generator decides which models split into Request and Response variants. Without the flag it decides as 0.86.0 did, from a temporary parse of each referenced schema; that parse takes class names and can emit unreferenced copies, so other classes get higher numbers (Child1Request where ChildRequest is free), and a schema whose parse reaches itself again through the models it builds stops there. A child that inherits from an allOf parent also builds the inline models of the parent's properties a second time (Payload1 unused, Payload2 referenced). Some recursive schemas cannot be generated that way and the error names this flag.

With the flag the decision reads the raw schemas only: an input without readOnly or writeOnly gives the models it gives without --read-only-write-only-model-type, and each inline model is written once (Payload1 referenced). Both forms validate the same data.

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input read_only_write_only_allof_parent_inline_models.yaml --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel --read-only-write-only-model-type request-response --dedupe-request-response-variants # (1)!
  1. --dedupe-request-response-variants - the option documented here
Examples

Input Schema:

openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: t
  version: '1'
paths: {}
components:
  schemas:
    Child:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Parent'
        - type: object
          properties:
            payload:
              properties:
                extra:
                  type: string
    Parent:
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: integer
          readOnly: true
        payload:
          type: object
          properties:
            value:
              type: object
              properties:
                code:
                  type: integer

items.title: --openapi-paths-bodies-as-definitions
items.text:
Give the bodies of the paths and webhooks scopes the models their schema definitions get.

With --openapi-scopes paths (or webhooks), request and response bodies are parsed by their own dispatch, which types some object bodies inline although a schema definition of the same body gets a model: a body whose type array admits objects, such as type: [object, "null"], or one with additionalProperties, patternProperties or propertyNames and no type. With --openapi-paths-bodies-as-definitions, such a body gets the model its definition would get, such as a root model of dict[str, Any] | None, whose values --use-typed-nullable-map-values types as declared. A document whose only bodies are such schemas then generates models instead of failing with "Models not found in the input data", whose message names this option when it applies. Bodies typed as objects, arrays, combinations, enums and references, and the api scope, are unchanged.

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input type_array_request_body.yaml --openapi-scopes paths --openapi-paths-bodies-as-definitions # (1)!

  title: Type array request body
  version: "1.0"
paths:

      requestBody:
        content:

            schema:
              type: [object, "null"]
              additionalProperties:
                type: object
                properties:
                  name:

items.title: --client-body-arguments
items.text:
Choose how operation methods take request bodies (experimental).

body (the default) takes the body as one body argument; both also takes the properties of an object body as keyword arguments, so a call can pass either. The body_arguments of an operation in --client-operations overrides it for that operation.

Option relationships:

  • Requires: --generate-client - --client-body-arguments requires --generate-client httpx2.

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input options.yaml --input-file-type openapi --output models.py --target-python-version 3.11 --openapi-scopes schemas api --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel --formatters builtin --disable-timestamp --generate-client httpx2 --client-output client --client-package client --client-model-package models --client-body-arguments both # (1)!
  1. --client-body-arguments - the option documented here

openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Pets
  version: 1.0.0
servers:
  - url: https://api.example.com/v1
paths:
  /pets:
    get:
      operationId: listPets
      tags: [pets]
      summary: List the pets.
      parameters:
        - name: limit
          in: query
          schema: {type: integer}
        - name: cursor
          in: query
          schema: {type: string}
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A page of pets.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Pets'}
    post:
      operationId: createPet
      tags: [pets]
      summary: Create a pet.
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/NewPet'}
      responses:
        '201':
          description: The created pet.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'}

  schemas:
    NewPet:
      type: object
      required: [name]
      properties:
        name: {type: string}
        tag: {type: string}
    Pet:
      type: object
      required: [id, name]
      properties:
        id: {type: integer}
        name: {type: string}
        tag: {type: string}
    Pets:
      type: object
      required: [data]
      properties:
        data:
          type: array
          items: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'}
        next_cursor: {type: [string, 'null']}

items.title: --client-operations
items.text:
Set the client settings of single operations (experimental).

The JSON object, inline or in a file, maps operation references to their settings. An operation reference is the JSON pointer of the path item method, such as /paths/~1pets/get, optionally after a document and #, such as pets.yaml#/paths/~1pets/get. A relative document resolves against the JSON file that holds the reference, or without a file against the working directory, and against the pyproject.toml directory for a table. The settings are resource, name, parameter_names (keyed by location and name, such as {"query:limit": "page_size"}), request_media_type, response_media_type, description, body_arguments, which overrides --client-body-arguments, body_field_names (keyed by media type, then property, such as {"application/json": {"petName": "pet_name"}}), and runtime: request_id_header, success_statuses, retry_safety, idempotency ({"header_name": "Idempotency-Key"}), retry_after_ms_header, should_retry_header, auth_challenge_less_401, and accepted_content_encodings. from mymodule.myclass import MyCustomPythonClass

from typing_extensions import TypeAliasType

Boolean = TypeAliasType("Boolean", bool)

items.title: --check-pattern-maps-strictly
items.text:
Check every key of the pattern maps that --generate-schema-validators validates.

Without the option the schema validators check a pattern map as in 0.86.0: a declared property skips the patternProperties that match its name unless a simple witness shows the pattern rejects one of its values, and the dict root of an object without properties counts its keys as if the patterns admitted none (max_length=0 beside additionalProperties: false, so every non-empty object is rejected). With --check-pattern-maps-strictly, a declared property is also checked against every matching pattern whose schema its own does not imply, the dict root counts every key a pattern admits and takes its keys from propertyNames, and the model of an object without properties keeps the other types of its type array. The option has no effect without --generate-schema-validators.

items.title: --formatters
items.text:
Specify code formatters to apply to generated output.

The --formatters flag specifies which code formatters to apply to the generated Python code. Available formatters are: builtin, black, isort, ruff-check, ruff-format. The current default is [black, isort]. For projects using Ruff, select --formatters ruff-check ruff-format to match project lint and formatting settings. Use --formatters builtin when you use no external formatter or prioritize generation speed. Keep --formatters black isort to preserve existing formatting. Explicit formatters override presets. The future builtin default reduces installation dependencies and version constraints; Black/isort remain required today. See the formatter guides for installation and custom-template limitations.

See also: CI/CD Integration, Formatter behavior, Code Formatting

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input pet_simple.json --formatters isort # (1)!
  1. --formatters - the option documented here

items.title: --generate-schema-validators
items.text:
Generate experimental Pydantic v2 model validators for JSON Schema runtime rules.

The --generate-schema-validators option emits schema-derived model validators for object constraints that cannot be represented as type hints alone, including minProperties/maxProperties on named object models, patternProperties on composed object models, required-only oneOf/anyOf groups, simple if/then/else required-property conditions, and uniqueItems array validation. This feature is experimental and may change as JSON Schema coverage is expanded.

With standard models and templates, required names absent from generated fields are checked against the raw object input. This also preserves required names that are not declared in properties when validating overlapping open object patterns. --force-optional retains its existing behavior. Custom base classes, custom templates, and extra template data retain their previous handling of undeclared required names.

When generating uniqueItems validation, do not override pydantic_v2/schema_runtime_validation_helpers.jinja2; custom helper overrides are unsupported and generation fails fast.

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input schema_validators.json --generate-schema-validators --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel --disable-timestamp # (1)!
  1. --generate-schema-validators - the option documented here

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections.abc import Mapping as _Mapping
from typing import Any, ClassVar

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, RootModel, TypeAdapter, model_validator


class _JsonSchemaRuntimeValidationBase(BaseModel):
    __json_schema_pattern_properties__: ClassVar[tuple[Any, ...]] = ()
    __json_schema_one_of_required_groups__: ClassVar[tuple[Any, ...]] = ()
    __json_schema_any_of_required_groups__: ClassVar[tuple[Any, ...]] = ()
    __json_schema_conditional_required__: ClassVar[tuple[Any, ...]] = ()

    @model_validator(mode='before')
    @classmethod
    def _validate_json_schema_runtime_rules(cls, data: Any) -> Any:
        data = cls._validate_json_schema_pattern_properties(data)
        data = cls._validate_json_schema_required_groups(
            data,
            required_group_rules=cls.__json_schema_one_of_required_groups__,
            require_exactly_one=True,
        )
        data = cls._validate_json_schema_required_groups(
            data,
            required_group_rules=cls.__json_schema_any_of_required_groups__,
            require_exactly_one=False,
        )
        data = cls._validate_json_schema_conditional_required(data)
        return data

    @classmethod
    def _validate_json_schema_pattern_properties(cls, data: Any) -> Any:
        if not (isinstance(data, dict) or isinstance(data, _Mapping)):
            return data
        values = data
        for rule in cls.__json_schema_pattern_properties__:
            pattern_adapters = None
            additional_adapter = None
            for key, value in data.items():
                if key in rule['declared_properties']:
                    continue
                if any(
                    re.search(pattern, key) for pattern in rule['rejected_patterns']
                ):
                    raise ValueError(
                        f'Property {key!r} is not allowed by patternProperties'
                    )
                matched = False
                for index, (pattern, value_type) in enumerate(
                    rule['pattern_properties'],
                ):
                    if not re.search(pattern, key):
                        continue
                    matched = True
                    if pattern_adapters is None:
                        pattern_adapters = {}
                    if (adapter := pattern_adapters.get(index)) is None:
                        adapter = TypeAdapter(value_type)
                        pattern_adapters[index] = adapter
                    value = adapter.validate_python(value)
                if matched:
                    if values is data:
                        values = dict(data)
                    values[key] = value
                    continue
                if rule['additional_property_type'] is not None:
                    if additional_adapter is None:
                        additional_adapter = TypeAdapter(
                            rule['additional_property_type'],
                        )
                    if values is data:
                        values = dict(data)
                    values[key] = additional_adapter.validate_python(value)
                    continue
                if not rule['allow_unmatched']:
                    raise ValueError(f'Unexpected property {key!r}')
        return values

    @classmethod
    def _validate_json_schema_required_groups(
        cls,
        data: Any,
        *,
        required_group_rules: tuple[Any, ...],
        require_exactly_one: bool,
    ) -> Any:
        if not required_group_rules:
            return data
        if not (isinstance(data, dict) or isinstance(data, _Mapping)):
            return data
        for required_groups in required_group_rules:
            matches = sum(
                all(any(name in data for name in names) for names in group)
                for group in required_groups
            )
            if require_exactly_one:
                if matches != 1:
                    raise ValueError(
                        'Expected exactly one required property group to be present'
                    )
            elif matches == 0:
                raise ValueError(
                    'Expected at least one required property group to be present'
                )
        return data

    @classmethod
    def _validate_json_schema_conditional_required(cls, data: Any) -> Any:
        if not (isinstance(data, dict) or isinstance(data, _Mapping)):
            return data
        for rule in cls.__json_schema_conditional_required__:
            condition_matches = all(
                any(name in data and data[name] in expected for name in names)
                for names, expected in rule['condition']
            )
            required_groups = (
                rule['then_required_groups']
                if condition_matches
                else rule['else_required_groups']
            )
            for group in required_groups:
                if all(any(name in data for name in names) for names in group):
                    continue
                raise ValueError('Conditional required properties are missing')
        return data

items.title: --no-use-type-checking-imports
items.text:
Keep generated model imports available at runtime when using Ruff fixes.

The --no-use-type-checking-imports flag prevents Ruff from moving generated model imports into TYPE_CHECKING blocks. This is useful for modular Pydantic output where referenced models need to be importable at runtime without calling model_rebuild() manually. In the multi-module Pydantic + ruff-check case, runtime imports are preserved by default. --use-type-checking-imports opts back into the old TYPE_CHECKING-only behavior, which can require manual model_rebuild() calls for cross-module runtime references.

Related: --formatters, --use-exact-imports, --use-type-checking-imports

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input modular.yaml --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel --formatters ruff-check ruff-format --no-use-type-checking-imports --disable-timestamp # (1)!

items.title: --use-double-quotes
items.text:
Use double quotes for string literals in generated code.

The --use-double-quotes option formats all string literals in the generated Python code with double quotes instead of the default single quotes. This helps maintain consistency with codebases that prefer double-quote formatting.

items.title: --use-exact-imports
items.text:
Import exact types instead of modules.

The --use-exact-imports flag changes import style from module imports to exact type imports. For example, instead of from . import foo then foo.Bar, it generates from .foo import Bar. This can make the generated code more explicit and easier to read.

Note: This option primarily affects modular output where imports between modules are generated. For single-file output, the difference is minimal.

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input pet_simple.json --use-exact-imports # (1)!
  1. --use-exact-imports - the option documented here

      "type": "integer"

    "name": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "tag": {
      "type": "string"
    }

items.title: --use-type-checking-imports
items.text:
Allow Ruff to move typing-only imports into TYPE_CHECKING blocks.

The --use-type-checking-imports flag explicitly re-enables Ruff's TYPE_CHECKING import moves for multi-module Pydantic output where runtime imports might otherwise be preserved by default.

items.title: --validators
items.text:
Add custom field validators to generated Pydantic v2 models.

The --validators option takes an inline JSON object or JSON file defining validators per model. Each validator specifies the field(s) to validate, the validation function to import, and optionally the mode (before/after/wrap/plain). This allows injecting custom validation logic into generated models.

See also: Field Validators

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input field_validators.json --validators tests/data/jsonschema/field_validators_config.json --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel --use-annotated --disable-timestamp # (1)!
  1. --validators - the option documented here
Examples

Input Schema:

{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "title": "User",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "email": {
      "type": "string",
      "format": "email"
    },
    "age": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0
    }
  },
  "required": ["name", "email"]
}

Output:

# generated by datamodel-codegen:
#   filename:  field_validators.json

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Annotated, Any

from myapp.validators import validate_email, validate_name
from pydantic import BaseModel, EmailStr, Field, ValidationInfo, field_validator


class User(BaseModel):
    name: str
    email: EmailStr
    age: Annotated[int | None, Field(ge=0)] = None

    @field_validator('name', mode='before')
    @classmethod
    def validate_name_validator(cls, v: Any, info: ValidationInfo) -> Any:
        return validate_name(v, info)

    @field_validator('email', mode='after')
    @classmethod
    def validate_email_validator(cls, v: Any, info: ValidationInfo) -> Any:
        return validate_email(v, info)

items.title: --allof-class-hierarchy
items.text:
Controls how allOf schemas are represented in the generated class hierarchy. --allof-class-hierarchy if-no-conflict (default) creates parent classes for allOf schemas only when there are no property conflicts between parent schemas. Otherwise, properties are merged into the child class which is then decoupled from the parent classes and no longer inherits from them. --allof-class-hierarchy always keeps class hierarchy for allOf schemas, even in multiple inheritance scenarios where two parent schemas define the same property. msgspec.Struct output declares the fields of parent classes whose layouts msgspec cannot combine instead of inheriting from them.

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input allof_root_model_constraints.json --allof-class-hierarchy always # (1)!

      "description": "A constrained string.",
      "allOf": [

    },
    "IntegerDatatype": {

      "description": "Integer between 0 and 100.",

items.title: --allof-merge-mode
items.text:
Merge constraints from root model references in allOf schemas.

The --allof-merge-mode constraints merges only constraint properties (minLength, maximum, etc.) from parent schemas referenced in allOf. This ensures child schemas inherit validation constraints while keeping other properties separate.

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input allof_root_model_constraints.json --allof-merge-mode constraints # (1)!
  1. --allof-merge-mode - the option documented here
Examples OpenAPIJSON Schema

Input Schema:

openapi: "3.0.0"
info:
  title: Test materialize allOf defaults
  version: "1.0.0"
components:
  schemas:
    Parent:
      type: object
      properties:
        name:
          type: string
          default: "parent_default"
          minLength: 1
        count:
          type: integer
          default: 10
          minimum: 0
    Child:
      allOf:
        - $ref: "#/components/schemas/Parent"
        - type: object
          properties:
            name:
              maxLength: 100
            count:
              maximum: 1000

items.title: --filter-literal-values
items.text:
Keep only the values of a const or an enum that meet the constraints beside them.

JSON Schema validates a value against the enum and the keywords beside it, so {"enum": ["hello", "goodbye"], "maxLength": 5} admits hello only. With --filter-literal-values, the Literal or the Enum of a const or an enum holds the values that meet the minLength, maxLength, minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, exclusiveMaximum, multipleOf and pattern keywords beside them, as far as the generator can decide them (a pattern only where every regular expression engine reads it alike). A schema none of whose values meets them admits no value: it stays as written, with a warning. A field that writes a constraint itself, such as Field(min_length=...), keeps the values that constraint checks. --omit-redundant-constraints includes this check. Without the option, every value stays and the keywords are written beside the type.

          type: array
          items:
            enum:
              - hello
              - goodbye
            maxLength: 5
            minLength: 1
            type: string
            pattern: "^.*$"
          maxItems: 3

items.title: --intersect-allof-keywords
items.text:
Combine the keywords of every part of an allOf, a $ref with siblings or an override.

JSON Schema applies the members of an allOf, a $ref and the keywords beside it, and a property that overrides an inherited one all at once, so a value must meet every part. Without the option the keyword of the last part wins where the parts disagree: the sibling of a $ref, the overriding property, the last member of an allOf. With --intersect-allof-keywords, the tightest bound of the parts is written (maximum: 10 beside maximum: 20 keeps 10), an enum holds the values every part admits, a type the types every part admits, required the names of every part, and the patterns of the parts are checked together. An allOf of value schemas at a root, an item or a map value is one constraint schema in the same way, and a null member beside a type that excludes null is dropped. Parts that no value meets together keep the earlier merge with a warning.

items.title: --keep-enum-member-values
items.text:
Give an enum class a value base only when it keeps every member value.

--use-specialized-enum (IntEnum, StrEnum) and --use-subclass-enum ((T, Enum)) give an enum class the value type of its schema type as a base. Without this option the base follows the schema type alone, as in 0.86.0, so a member the base changes is written with the changed value: const branches [1, 2.5] make an IntEnum whose 2.5 becomes 2 (rejecting the schema-valid 2.5 and accepting 2), and ['a', 1] under --use-subclass-enum a (str, Enum) holding '1'. With the option such an enum is a plain Enum that keeps the values as written; members the base keeps, as 1.0 in an IntEnum or 1 in a (float, Enum), keep the base. msgspec keeps the 0.86.0 class where it could not decode the plain Enum. A base that cannot hold a member at all, so that the class failed at import ('a' in an IntEnum, a format: byte enum), gives a plain Enum either way.

items.title: --read-const-beside-enum
items.text:
Read a const beside an enum as JSON Schema does.

A const that admits some but not all values of the enum beside it narrows the schema to the admitted values, while the enum class keeps every value as written. With --read-const-beside-enum, a value whose schema names such an enum, a property, an item, a map value or key, a union branch or a $ref to a definition, is typed by the const: Literal[<Enum>.<member>] when the members of the enum equal their values (IntEnum, StrEnum, --use-subclass-enum), the const's own Literal, or None for a null const. A plain Enum, and any msgspec enum, keeps the enum type and warns once per schema location that the other values are accepted. A schema whose const is none of its enum values admits no value and is generated as written with a warning. Under --use-single-value-enum-as-const, an enum that admits the const beside it, such as {"enum": ["a", "b"], "const": "a"}, is read as that const without the enum class written beside it otherwise, except one with nullable: true and a const other than null. Without the option, a const beside an enum is ignored.

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input enum_const_positions.json --read-const-beside-enum # (1)!
  1. --read-const-beside-enum - the option documented here

    "refSibling": {"$ref": "#/$defs/Switch", "const": "on"},
    "keys": {"type": "object", "propertyNames": {"enum": ["a", "b"], "const": "a"}, "additionalProperties": {"type": "integer"}},
    "refKeys": {"type": "object", "propertyNames": {"$ref": "#/$defs/Narrowed"}, "additionalProperties": {"type": "integer"}},

items.title: --read-unevaluated-properties
items.text:
Read a schema-valued unevaluatedProperties as additionalProperties.

Where no applicator (allOf, anyOf, oneOf, not, if, dependentSchemas, dependencies or a reference) evaluates a property of the object in place, the keys unevaluatedProperties evaluates are exactly those that additionalProperties would, so its schema types the extra keys of a model (__pydantic_extra__: Dict[str, str]) and makes an object without properties a map (RootModel[dict[str, int]]). The schema object as written decides: the models built from its branches keep the extra keys untyped where its applicators evaluate properties. Without the option the extra keys are allowed untyped, as in 0.86.0.

items.title: --type-overrides
items.text:
Replace schema model types with custom Python types via JSON mapping.

This option is useful for importing models from external libraries (like geojson-pydantic) instead of generating them.

Override Formats:

Format Description {"ModelName": "package.Type"} Model-level: Skip generation; replace field and inheritance refs {"Model.field": "package.Type"} Scoped: Override only specific field in specific model

Common Use Cases:

Use Case Example Override GeoJSON types {"Feature": "geojson_pydantic.Feature"} Custom datetime {"Timestamp": "pendulum.DateTime"} MongoDB ObjectId {"ObjectId": "bson.ObjectId"} Custom validators {"Email": "my_app.types.ValidatedEmail"}

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input type_overrides_test.json --type-overrides '{"CustomType": "my_app.types.CustomType"}' # (1)!
  1. --type-overrides - the option documented here

Model-level overrides skip generation

When you specify a model-level override (without a dot in the key), the generator will skip generating that model entirely and import it from the specified package instead. References to that model are replaced in field annotations and allOf inheritance base classes.

Examples

Input Schema:

{
    "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
    "definitions": {
        "CustomType": {"type": "string"},
        "User": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "id": {"type": "integer"},
                "custom": {"$ref": "#/definitions/CustomType"}
            }
        }
    }
}

items.title: --use-single-dict-for-object-maps
items.text:
Type an object map as one dict instead of a union of dicts.

An object map is an object without properties whose keys patternProperties or propertyNames constrain. With --use-single-dict-for-object-maps it is one dict whose key pattern joins every pattern and whose value is the union of their value types, so an object that mixes the keys of several patterns is accepted; a dict that cannot express the object exactly (keys outside the patterns, different value schemas) is named by a warning. The null and the other types of a type array, such as [object, string, null], join the dict in a union, and its property counts stay on the dict; the dict root model of an object without properties, such as a nullable additionalProperties map, takes the same null. The stricter pattern-map checks of --generate-schema-validators are under --check-pattern-maps-strictly. Without --use-single-dict-for-object-maps the map is written as in 0.86.0: a union of dicts, one per value type of the patterns, the other types of a type array left out; msgspec, which cannot decode a union of several dicts, gets the one dict.

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input pattern_properties_merge.json --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel --use-single-dict-for-object-maps # (1)!
  1. --use-single-dict-for-object-maps - the option documented here

  "type": "object",
  "patternProperties": {
    "^i-": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "^t-": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "^n-": {
      "type": "integer"
    }
  }
}

items.title: --use-single-value-enum-as-const
items.text:
Treat enum with a single value as const with that value.

JSON Schema defines {"enum": ["low"]} as equal to {"const": "low"}. With --use-single-value-enum-as-const, each schema in the JSON Schema, OpenAPI and AsyncAPI documents whose enum lists one value is read as that const, so the output is the same as for the documents written with const, while the enums that allOf intersections leave stay enums: oneOf/anyOf branches of single-value enums, as Rust's schemars writes documented unit variants, become one Enum with branch titles as member names when there are two or more and all hold values of one JSON type; otherwise each branch is typed as written, such as Literal['a'] | None for one value beside a null branch or Literal['a'] | Literal[1] for values of different JSON types. A schema with one enum value is typed Literal[...] instead of a one-member Enum, except one with nullable: true and a value other than null, which keeps its enum and is read as written. The option reads const branches the same way, which without it merge into one Enum in those cases too. Instance data such as default and examples, extension values (x-... except x-propertyNames), links and servers stay as written, so a schema kept under an extension key, such as one referenced as headers.yaml#/x-rate, is read as written too. A document parsed with draft-04 schema features, which have no const, is kept, and Avro, Protocol Buffers, XML Schema and GraphQL inputs are not changed.

datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --use-single-value-enum-as-const # (1)!

items.title: --use-tuple-for-closed-arrays
items.text:
Generate tuple types for positional arrays that no other item can follow.

A prefixItems array whose tail is closed by items: false, unevaluatedItems: false, a false position or contains, and an items array closed by additionalItems: false or a false position, is written as a tuple when its length bounds fix its length, so every position keeps its own type. Without the option only equal minItems and maxItems make a tuple, and a closed array is a list with length constraints that accepts items in the wrong positions. When bounds other than equal minItems and maxItems fix the length, the list stays if its item schemas (the allowed positions and the items schema) accept the same values, compared without annotations and x- keys, with a $ref read as its target and type: [T] as type: T. --use-tuple-for-fixed-items still decides whether the items array form is read. A tuple cannot hold uniqueItems: with --use-unique-items-as-set it stays a tuple and a warning names the field generated without uniqueness, unless --generate-schema-validators checks it.

items.text:
Type the map values of type arrays that list object beside other types.

With --use-typed-nullable-map-values, a schema whose type array lists object beside other types, such as type: [object, string] or type: [object, string, "null"], and that declares its values with additionalProperties gets typed values too, such as dict[str, int] | str, with a model for object values. items.title: --use-typed-nullable-map-values
items.text:
Type the values of nullable maps as their schemas say instead of Any.

A nullable map here is a schema whose type array lists object alone or with null, such as type: [object, "null"] or type: [object], and that declares its values with additionalProperties. Without the --use-typed-nullable-map-values flag the output keeps the 0.83.0 form, dict[str, Any] | None, or dict[str, Any] when the type array has no null, whatever the values are. A map made nullable by nullable: true and a map typed type: object keep their typed values either way. The maps of type arrays that list object beside other types, such as type: [object, string], are typed only with --use-typed-map-values-beside-other-types too.

With the flag the values follow their schema, such as dict[str, int] | None or dict[str, Player] | None, and an object value gets a model named after the map, such as Teams1 for the values of Teams. Those value models take the names left free, so the other models keep their 0.83.0 names, and options keyed by class name, such as --base-class-map or --aliases, apply to the final names. Typed values change more than the maps themselves: --reuse-model makes a value model and the models equal to it one model, which can leave out a schema's class, and no longer makes nullable maps with different values subclasses of each other, and --collapse-root-models collapses the root models that the values use. When typing the values would change the modules written, the values of the whole run stay untyped.

Usage

items.title: --all-jobs
items.text:
Run every named generation job from [tool.datamodel-codegen.jobs] in declaration order (experimental).

Experimental

Named batch jobs are experimental; their configuration schema, batch output, and transactional/watch execution contracts may change.

Related: --job, --diff-against, pyproject.toml Configuration

Usage

datamodel-codegen --all-jobs
datamodel-codegen --all-jobs --check
datamodel-codegen --all-jobs --output-format json
datamodel-codegen --all-jobs --watch

All selected jobs are validated before generation starts. Jobs that write to stdout, or whose output or model-metadata paths overlap, are rejected before any generated file is written. With --output-format json, one batch payload contains the result of every job.

--diff-against is intentionally unavailable for every named-job execution, including a single selected job. Keeping one contract across --job and --all-jobs avoids ambiguous partial support when the selection grows. Run the comparison for one profile or input instead.

With --watch, changes to pyproject.toml replan the complete job membership. All selected local dependencies are watched as one graph, and every event reruns and publishes the whole batch transactionally rather than rebuilding only one job.

items.title: --generate-prompt
items.text:
Generate a prompt for consulting LLMs about CLI options.

Outputs a formatted prompt containing your current options, all available options by category, and full help text. Pipe to CLI LLM tools or copy to clipboard for web-based LLM chats.

Use --output-format json when an LLM agent or tool should consume structured option metadata instead of Markdown. Use --output-format-json-schema generate-prompt when the agent needs the JSON Schema for that structured payload, such as when defining a tool contract. Add --recommend-options (experimental) with an input schema to include the schema analysis and the options recommended for it in the prompt.

See also: LLM Integration for detailed usage examples

For LLM agents

See LLM Integration: If You Are an LLM Agent for workflow guidance.

Usage

datamodel-codegen --generate-prompt # (1)!
datamodel-codegen --generate-prompt "How do I generate strict types?" # (2)!
datamodel-codegen --generate-prompt --output-format json # (3)!
datamodel-codegen --output-format-json-schema generate-prompt # (4)!
datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --generate-prompt --recommend-options # (5)!
  1. --generate-prompt - generate prompt without a question
  2. Include a specific question in the prompt
  3. Emit structured JSON for LLM/tool ingestion
  4. Emit JSON Schema for structured prompt JSON
  5. Include the schema analysis and recommended options (experimental)
Quick Examples

Pipe to CLI tools: 

datamodel-codegen --generate-prompt | claude -p    # Claude Code
datamodel-codegen --generate-prompt | codex exec   # OpenAI Codex

datamodel-codegen --generate-prompt | xclip -selection clipboard  # Linux

    --input openapi.yaml \
    --input-file-type openapi \
    --output models.py \
    --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel \
    --target-python-version 3.12 \

    --input schema.json \
    --output models.py \

items.title: --job
items.text:
Run one or more named generation jobs declared in pyproject.toml (experimental). Jobs are executed sequentially in TOML declaration order, even when --job is supplied in a different order.

Experimental

Named batch jobs are experimental; their configuration schema, batch output, and transactional/watch execution contracts may change.

Related: pyproject.toml Configuration, --all-jobs, --diff-against

Usage

datamodel-codegen --job api
datamodel-codegen --job api --job events --check
Configuration (pyproject.toml) 
[tool.datamodel-codegen.profiles.strict]
use-annotated = true

[tool.datamodel-codegen.jobs.api]
profile = "strict"
input = "schemas/openapi.yaml"
output = "src/models/api.py"

[tool.datamodel-codegen.jobs.events]
input = "schemas/events.json"
output = "src/models/events.py"

items.title: --output-format
items.text:
Choose the command output format.

The default output format is text. Use json when another program or LLM agent should inspect structured output.

For backward compatibility, text stdout concatenates generated modules and does not preserve their paths. Use --fail-on-multi-module-stdout to reject that case, --output <directory> to preserve files, or --output-format json for structured stdout. The fail option takes precedence over automatic repair of an unusable modular stdout result, so an explicitly requested guard always rejects the modular result instead of coalescing it.

In normal generation mode, --output-format json wraps generated modules in a structured payload on stdout. If --output is also supplied, files are still written to disk and the JSON payload mirrors the generated files. --check also supports JSON output for difference reports. --watch keeps its existing text output contract and does not support --output-format json.

Structured JSON is emitted on stdout for successful commands and for --check difference reports. CLI usage errors, validation errors, and runtime generation errors continue to use text on stderr with a non-zero exit code.

Generation JSON includes the normalized requested output path in top-level output when --output is supplied, or null for stdout generation. files[].path is the output file name for single-file disk output, and the path relative to the output directory for directory output. For stdout-only single-file generation it is null, and for multi-module stdout generation it is the generated module path.

With --generate-server or --generate-client, the generation, check, and input-diff payloads also have a target object: package is the import path of the generated package, and dependencies lists its runtime requirements as PEP 508 strings, the ones the uv add command on stderr names. A check or input diff lists those of the current input, and implied the model settings the run left unset and the target set, when there are any: an object with the keys openapi-scopes, target-python-version, use-missing-sentinel, target-pydantic-version, use-msgspec-tagged-unions, and use-msgspec-nullable-enum-alias, each present only when the target set it. Payloads of model-only generation leave target out. The generation payload's target also carries the next steps that stderr prints: readme, the path of the package README; for a server, entrypoint (app, the import string of the application in main.py, and path) and implementation, one entry for each module of yours that main.py imports (module, name, path, and created, true when the run wrote it with stubs, and whose path names the __init__.py of a module you made a package); and for a client, usage, code that calls its first operation. Its paths are relative like those of files.

Use --output-format json with --generate-prompt to emit structured option metadata instead of Markdown. Use --output-format-json-schema when an LLM agent or tool needs the schema for a JSON payload.

Schema targets are intentionally scoped. generate-prompt emits the PromptPayload schema for --generate-prompt --output-format json. generation emits only the GenerationPayload schema for generated-file JSON. model-metadata emits the schema for files written by --emit-model-metadata. structured-output emits the broader StructuredOutputPayload schema, a union covering GenerationPayload, PromptPayload, CommandOutputPayload, and CheckOutputPayload. Structured payloads use kind as the discriminator.

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output-format text # (1)!
datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --output-format json # (2)!
datamodel-codegen --generate-prompt --output-format json # (3)!
datamodel-codegen --output-format-json-schema generation # (4)!
datamodel-codegen --output-format-json-schema generate-prompt # (5)!
datamodel-codegen --output-format-json-schema model-metadata # (6)!
datamodel-codegen --output-format-json-schema structured-output # (7)!
  1. Emit the default generated Python text
  2. Emit structured JSON containing generated files
  3. Emit structured JSON with current options and argparse metadata
  4. Emit JSON Schema for generated-file JSON output
  5. Emit JSON Schema for structured prompt JSON
  6. Emit JSON Schema for generated model metadata JSON
  7. Emit JSON Schema for any structured command JSON output
Generation JSON output 
{
  "version": 1,
  "format": "json",
  "kind": "generation",
  "output": null,
  "files": [
    {
      "path": null,
      "content": "# generated by datamodel-codegen:\n..."
    }
  ]
}
Prompt JSON output 
datamodel-codegen \
    --input schema.json \
    --output-model-type pydantic_v2.BaseModel \
    --generate-prompt "Choose strict model options." \
    --output-format json

items.title: --output-format-json-schema
items.text:
Output JSON Schema for a JSON output format and exit.

Use this when an LLM agent, tool call definition, or validation layer needs the contract before consuming JSON output. The schema is emitted separately from the JSON payload so tools can fetch the contract once and validate later command output independently.

Currently supported schema targets:

  • generate-prompt: schema for --generate-prompt --output-format json
  • generation: schema for normal generation with --output-format json
  • model-metadata: schema for files emitted by --emit-model-metadata
  • structured-output: tagged union schema for all structured command outputs, discriminated by kind
  • config: schema for JSON-valued configuration options

Usage

datamodel-codegen --output-format-json-schema generate-prompt # (1)!
datamodel-codegen --output-format-json-schema generation # (2)!
datamodel-codegen --output-format-json-schema model-metadata # (3)!
datamodel-codegen --output-format-json-schema structured-output # (4)!
datamodel-codegen --output-format-json-schema config # (5)!
datamodel-codegen --generate-prompt --output-format json # (6)!
datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --emit-model-metadata model-map.json # (7)!
  1. Emit the JSON Schema for structured prompt output
  2. Emit the JSON Schema for generated-file output
  3. Emit the JSON Schema for generated model metadata
  4. Emit the JSON Schema for all structured command outputs
  5. Emit the JSON Schema for JSON-valued configuration options
  6. Emit prompt payloads that match the prompt schema
  7. Emit metadata payloads that match the model metadata schema

items.title: --overwrite-skill

Replace an existing regular Agent Skill directory when installing with --install-skill.

Without this option, an existing skill is preserved and the command exits with an error. Symlinks and non-directory targets are never overwritten.

items.title: --profile
items.text:
Use a named profile from pyproject.toml configuration.

Profiles allow you to define multiple named configurations in your pyproject.toml file. Each profile can override the default settings with its own set of options.

Related: pyproject.toml Configuration

Usage

datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --profile strict # (1)!
  1. --profile - the option documented here
Configuration (pyproject.toml) 
[tool.datamodel-codegen]
# Default configuration
output-model-type = "pydantic_v2.BaseModel"

[tool.datamodel-codegen.profiles.strict]
# Strict profile with additional options
strict-types = ["str", "int", "float", "bool"]
strict-nullable = true

[tool.datamodel-codegen.profiles.dataclass]
# Dataclass profile
output-model-type = "dataclasses.dataclass"

Use profiles:

# Use the strict profile
datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --profile strict

# Use the dataclass profile
datamodel-codegen --input schema.json --profile dataclass

  2. Emit the JSON Schema for generated-file output
  3. Emit the JSON Schema for generated model metadata
